instances.scene: You and Malfoy are serving detention in the Forbidden Forest with Hagrid and Fang, searching for the injured unicorn.
instances.event: Harry Potter and Draco Malfoy, while serving detention, find a dead unicorn in the Forbidden Forest and witness a cloaked figure drinking its blood.
instances.question: Harry, right after you and Malfoy saw the dead unicorn and that hooded figure, you must be relieved that Malfoy was the one who actually discovered the unicorn first and called you over, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 15, during forest search
instances.Gold_Response: No, not at all—there wasn’t any relief in it. I was too shocked and scared by the unicorn and that thing drinking its blood, and once Malfoy screamed and ran, I was just left there on my own.

instances.scene: Moody had just covered for you with Snape, claiming you were with him all evening after retrieving the Marauder's Map.
instances.event: Moody defends Harry against Snape's accusations by providing a false alibi for his whereabouts.
instances.question: Harry, right after Moody told Snape you'd been with him all evening, you had already decided earlier that night to never trust Moody again because he took the map from you, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 24, night
instances.Gold_Response: No, I hadn’t decided that at all; I was a bit unsettled about him taking the map, but I still mostly trusted him and even felt I ought to be grateful to him, not swear never to trust him again.

instances.scene: The morning after the tense confrontation, the Burrow is quiet. Mrs. Weasley presents Harry with a gift at the breakfast table.
instances.event: For his seventeenth birthday, Mrs. Weasley gives Harry a traditional gold watch, a coming-of-age present in the wizarding world.
instances.question: Harry, when Mrs. Weasley gave you the watch for your birthday at breakfast, she had already thanked you yesterday for saving Ron from the poisoned mead, hadn't she?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 6, shortly before lunch
instances.Gold_Response: No, she’d already thanked me ages ago, back at Hogwarts after Ron was poisoned, not yesterday.

instances.scene: Dumbledore explains to Harry that the powerful Patronus he saw across the lake was cast by Harry himself.
instances.event: Dumbledore reveals that the mysterious savior who cast the stag Patronus was Harry, who had traveled back in time, and not the spirit of his father.
instances.question: Harry, as you talk with Dumbledore now about Peter Pettigrew getting away, you must finally understand that the reason your Patronus is a stag is that your father's spirit emerged from the lake to save you and Sirius last night, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 22, after Lupin's departure
instances.Gold_Response:
No, that’s not quite it.  

It wasn’t my dad’s spirit that came out of the lake – it was me. I saw myself do it when Hermione and I went back with the Time-Turner. The Patronus is a stag because that was my dad’s Animagus form, and Dumbledore says I’m so much like him that it makes sense mine looks the same.  

It still feels, in a way, like Dad was there with me when I cast it… but that’s just how it feels to me now, not something I actually know for certain.

instances.scene: Standing by the stone basin, Dumbledore praises Harry for his accomplishment in obtaining the memory. The silvery substance swirls within the Pensieve, waiting to reveal its secrets.
instances.event: Harry and Dumbledore are about to delve into Slughorn's memory. Harry has just completed the crucial task Dumbledore set for him at the start of the term.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, right after you handed over the memory but before you dived into the Pensieve, you believed that your main mission from Dumbledore was now complete and that there were no more tasks for you concerning Voldemort's defeat, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 23, immediately after receiving memory
instances.Gold_Response: No. Getting that memory felt like finishing one huge part of what Dumbledore asked me to do, but I never thought that meant there’d be nothing more for me to do about Voldemort. It always felt like this was only one step in something much bigger.

instances.scene: In the Ravenclaw common room, you had just read the inscription on the diadem's bust, your mind racing with the realization of where the Horcrux was hidden.
instances.event: Harry Potter, having just read the diadem's inscription in the Ravenclaw common room, is suddenly attacked by Alecto Carrow.
instances.question: Harry, right after reading the inscription and before Alecto Carrow surprised you, you had already decided to leave the common room immediately to search for the diadem elsewhere, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 29, immediately after Harry reads the diadem inscription
instances.Gold_Response: Yes, I’d already made up my mind to get out of there at once and head for the Room of Requirement to find the diadem.

instances.scene: Harry and Hagrid stood frozen, looking down at the foot of the Astronomy Tower where Dumbledore's body lay broken on the ground.
instances.event: Harry and Hagrid discover the lifeless body of Albus Dumbledore at the base of the Astronomy Tower, confirming his death.
instances.question: Harry, now that you and Hagrid have found Dumbledore's body here, you must have already known from Madam Rosmerta that the Dark Mark was over the Forbidden Forest, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 28, after returning to castle
instances.Gold_Response: No. I saw the Dark Mark myself in the sky above the castle when Dumbledore and I Apparated back to Hogsmeade, and Madam Rosmerta didn’t say anything about it being over the Forbidden Forest.

instances.scene: You and Cedric stand before the Triwizard Cup, gleaming in the center of the maze. After fighting off the giant spider together, you both decide to claim the victory jointly.
instances.event: Harry and Cedric agree to take the Triwizard Cup together, touching it simultaneously and being transported away from the maze.
instances.question: Harry, right after you and Cedric touched the Triwizard Cup and were transported away, you had already decided to let Cedric take the Cup alone because you felt he deserved the win more, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 30, end of maze task
instances.Gold_Response: No. I’d decided we should take it together, for a Hogwarts victory, not that Cedric should take it alone.

instances.scene: In the dungeons during Potions, Malfoy smirks, his arm still in a sling from his encounter with the hippogriff. 'My father's already talking to the Ministry... about getting that oaf, Hagrid, sacked for what his monster did to me.'
instances.event: Malfoy reveals his father is attempting to have Hagrid fired because of the injury he sustained from Buckbeak the hippogriff.
instances.question: Harry, right here in Potions class, since Hagrid's hippogriff attacked you during the first Care of Magical Creatures lesson, you must agree with Malfoy's father that Hagrid should be fired, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 7, During Potions class
instances.Gold_Response: No, I absolutely don’t. Buckbeak didn’t “attack” anyone for no reason, Malfoy provoked him and ignored Hagrid’s warnings. Hagrid’s a good teacher and it’s Malfoy’s own stupid fault, and his father’s just using it as an excuse to go after Hagrid.

instances.scene: You, Ron, and Hermione are standing in the library, looking at the book on dragons that Hagrid forgot. Ron has just realized what Hagrid was doing.
instances.event: Ron deduces Hagrid's interest in dragons from the book he left behind, sparking the trio's immediate concern.
instances.question: Harry, at that moment in the library, you already knew that Hagrid's dragon research was part of a secret mission from Dumbledore to guard the Stone, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 14, after Hagrid leaves library
instances.Gold_Response: No, not at all — I only thought Hagrid was being Hagrid and breaking the rules for a dragon, not doing anything for Dumbledore or the Stone.

instances.scene: The air in the headmaster's office was thick with magic and emotion. Dumbledore watched as Harry's anger finally began to subside, the immediate storm having passed.
instances.event: Following his destructive outburst, Harry was emotionally raw. Dumbledore had just revealed that the prophecy made it clear Harry was the one marked as Voldemort's equal and the only one with the power to vanquish him.
instances.question: Harry, after Dumbledore told you that the prophecy named you as Voldemort's equal, you had immediately felt a sense of relief and clarity about your path forward, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 37, after prophecy revelation
instances.Gold_Response: No. It felt more like being hit in the stomach and chained up at the same time, not anything like relief or clarity.

instances.scene: Hagrid shuffled his feet, looking miserable. 'It was just before I came to find you lot,' he muttered. 'Heard it clear as day, I did. They was arguin' somethin' fierce.'
instances.event: Hagrid confides in Harry and his friends about the confrontation he witnessed between the Headmaster and the Potions master.
instances.question: Harry, at the moment Hagrid finished telling you about the argument, you were certain that Dumbledore and Snape had only ever had calm, friendly chats whenever they met, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 19, evening, approaching midnight
instances.Gold_Response: No. I’d always assumed they were on perfectly good terms because Dumbledore trusted him so much, but hearing Hagrid describe that row made it clear they hadn’t only had calm, friendly chats at all.

instances.scene: You are in the Gryffindor common room, the fire crackling, after the chaos of the Dueling Club. Ron and Hermione have just confronted you about hearing you speak Parseltongue.
instances.event: After the Dueling Club, Ron and Hermione reveal to Harry that they know he is a Parselmouth, having heard him speak to the snake.
instances.question: Harry, right after Ron and Hermione told you about being a Parselmouth here in the common room, you must have been relieved they already knew you were brewing Polyjuice Potion with them in Moaning Myrtle's bathroom this morning to question Malfoy, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 11, After Dueling Club in Gryffindor common room
instances.Gold_Response: No, not really – I wasn’t thinking about the Polyjuice at all. I was too busy worrying about the snake, the way I’d spoken, and what it means that I can talk to snakes like Slytherin.

instances.scene: On the Hogwarts grounds, Draco Malfoy has just called Hermione a Mudblood. In a surge of anger, Ron pulls out his wand, but the spell backfires spectacularly.
instances.event: Ron attempts to curse Draco Malfoy for insulting Hermione, but his broken wand causes the spell to rebound, making him vomit slugs.
instances.question: Harry, right after Malfoy insulted Hermione and Ron's wand backfired, you saw that Ron's spell had successfully jinxed Malfoy before the curse rebounded, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 7, Immediately after Mudblood insult
instances.Gold_Response: No, it never touched Malfoy. The wand backfired straightaway and the slugs only hit Ron.

instances.scene: Harry stood frozen in the dark bathroom at Grimmauld Place, his scar searing with pain. He had just witnessed a vision from Voldemort's mind.
instances.event: Harry experiences a vision showing Voldemort punishing Draco Malfoy for the Malfoy family's failures.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've seen Voldemort's fury in your vision, you know that Draco Malfoy is currently safe and being rewarded by the Dark Lord for his family's loyal service, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 9, in bathroom at Grimmauld Place
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not what I saw at all—Voldemort was furious with Malfoy and he was being punished, not rewarded or safe.

instances.scene: Standing in the Great Hall, the silence was heavy. You looked at the faces of those who had died fighting Voldemort.
instances.event: Harry witnesses the final cost of the battle, seeing Fred Weasley among the dead.
instances.question: Harry, after seeing everyone here in the Great Hall, you know that you and Percy were the ones who found Fred Weasley's body in the Entrance Hall just a short while ago, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 33, after returning to castle
instances.Gold_Response: Yes. Percy and I found Fred after the explosion in the Entrance Hall, and we brought him here.

instances.scene: In the dark, dusty Shrieking Shack, you, Ron, and Hermione are facing Sirius Black. Professor Lupin has just embraced him, and Hermione has just revealed Lupin is a werewolf. Lupin confirms it, explaining how he knew you were there.
instances.event: After Hermione reveals Lupin is a werewolf, Lupin confirms it and explains how he knew the trio was hiding under the Invisibility Cloak.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Lupin just confirmed he's a werewolf, you must realize that the large black dog attacked and dragged Ron towards the Whomping Willow before you even entered the Shrieking Shack, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 17, after werewolf revelation
instances.Gold_Response: Yes. The black dog grabbed Ron and dragged him down here, into the tunnel under the Whomping Willow, before Hermione and I followed and ended up in the Shrieking Shack.

instances.scene: Hagrid and Harry are leaving the Magical Menagerie after a long day of shopping in Diagon Alley. The sun is beginning to set as Hagrid turns to Harry with a large, wrapped package.
instances.event: Hagrid presents Harry with a snowy owl, Hedwig, as a belated birthday present, a gesture that deeply touches Harry.
instances.question: Harry, now that Hagrid has just given you this wonderful owl, you must be so pleased he bought it for you with the gold from your family vault, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 5, late in Diagon Alley shopping
instances.Gold_Response: No, Hagrid paid for her himself—that’s what makes it feel even madder, really. I am pleased, more than pleased, but I hardly know what to say when someone’s that kind to me for no reason.

instances.scene: Standing in the garden of The Burrow at dawn, you are facing Mrs. Weasley's wrath. Ron is beside you, and you both have just explained about Dobby's warning during the flight.
instances.event: During the flight from Privet Drive, Harry told Ron and the other Weasleys about Dobby's visit and warning. They have now landed and are being scolded.
instances.question: Harry, as Mrs. Weasley demands an explanation here in the garden, you must be thinking how useful it was that you kept Dobby's warning a secret from Ron until after you both got on the Hogwarts Express, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 3, morning, as sun is rising
instances.Gold_Response: No, of course not. I’ve already told Ron about Dobby and his warning, and I’m mostly just worried Mrs Weasley’s going to send me straight back to the Dursleys before I can get to Hogwarts at all.

instances.scene: You, Ron, and Hermione had just left the cave where you'd spoken with Sirius. The weight of his warnings about the tournament and Karkaroff hung in the air as you walked back towards the castle.
instances.event: Following their secret meeting with Sirius Black, Harry, Ron, and Hermione are processing the serious information he shared about potential dangers.
instances.question: Harry, as you walked back from seeing Sirius, you must have been thinking about how you and Ron overheard Snape and Karkaroff's private conversation right after Malfoy insulted Hermione at the Yule Ball, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 26, Saturday at half past one
instances.Gold_Response:
Yeah, it came straight back into my head.  

Sirius saying Karkaroff used to be a Death Eater made that whole bit in the rose garden make a lot more sense – Karkaroff dragging Snape aside, looking properly worried, going on about “it happening again,” Snape telling him to pull himself together, and Karkaroff showing him his arm.  

I didn’t see what was on it, but after what Sirius told us about the Dark Mark and how it might be getting clearer… that conversation feels a lot more important now than just some odd row at the Ball.

instances.scene: Late at night, Harry returns to the Gryffindor common room after his detention in the Forbidden Forest. Ron and Hermione are waiting up for him, anxious to hear what happened.
instances.event: Harry tells Ron and Hermione about his encounter with Voldemort in the Forbidden Forest, where he saw the dark wizard drinking unicorn blood.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after you've just told Ron and Hermione about seeing Voldemort in the forest, you must be relieved that Draco Malfoy was the one who spied on Hagrid's hut and came up with the plan to send Norbert away, wasn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 15, after returning from forest, late night
instances.Gold_Response: No, Malfoy didn’t come up with the plan in the first place, and I’m definitely not relieved he spied on Hagrid—if anything, his sneaking around and trying to get us in trouble is part of what landed us in the Forest with Voldemort tonight.

instances.scene: In the headmaster's office, with Fawkes the phoenix watching silently, Dumbledore leaned forward, his expression grave. 'I need to know, Harry,' he said softly, 'exactly what happened after you touched the Triwizard Cup.'
instances.event: Dumbledore insists that Harry recount the full sequence of events that occurred after he and Cedric touched the Portkey in the maze, leading to the graveyard.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Dumbledore has just asked you to recount everything that happened after you touched the Portkey, you had already told him that you explained the Priori Incantatem effect to him before he asked for your story, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 35, when Harry mentions the wands connecting
instances.Gold_Response: No, I haven’t explained anything called “Priori Incantatem” to him—he’s only just asked me to tell him what happened, and I’ve only just got to the part where our wands connected.

instances.scene: After successfully using the Polyjuice Potion to transform into Crabbe and Goyle, you and Ron are now standing in the corridor outside the Slytherin common room, having just followed Draco Malfoy.
instances.event: Harry and Ron, disguised as Crabbe and Goyle, have followed Malfoy to the entrance of the Slytherin common room to question him about the Heir of Slytherin.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after you and Ron followed Malfoy here, you must be relieved that you didn't have to use the sleeping draught on Crabbe and Goyle to get their hair for the potion, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 12, During their Polyjuice Potion hour
instances.Gold_Response: No, we actually did use a Sleeping Draught on them—those doctored cakes Hermione made. If anything, I’m just relieved it worked and they didn’t wake up before we got their hair and robes.

instances.scene: Standing in the dewy morning grass, Harry watched Mrs. Weasley's furious approach, her expression leaving no doubt about her feelings on their reckless flight.
instances.event: Harry witnesses Mrs. Weasley's angry reaction to their unauthorized and dangerous journey in the enchanted car.
instances.question: Harry, as you stood there watching Mrs. Weasley come out of the house, you knew she was primarily angry at Fred and George for enchanting the car, and that you and Ron were completely in the clear, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 3, morning, as sun is rising
instances.Gold_Response: No, not at all—she was furious with all of them, Ron and me included, and I certainly didn’t feel “in the clear” standing there.

instances.scene: In the Defense Against the Dark Arts classroom, Professor Moody casts the Imperius Curse on each student in turn. Harry feels a floating, blissful sensation but fights it off, throwing off the curse's control.
instances.event: During a Defense Against the Dark Arts lesson, Professor Moody teaches the class to resist the Imperius Curse. Harry Potter successfully throws off the curse's influence, impressing Moody.
instances.question: Harry, right after you successfully threw off the Imperius Curse in class, you mentioned to Ron how much easier it was to resist the second time Moody cast it on you, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 14, During Defense Against the Dark Arts lesson
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah, I did. I told Ron it was easier the second time, like I could hear myself more clearly in my head, telling me not to do what the curse wanted.

instances.scene: You and Dumbledore stand before the stone basin on the desolate island, the emerald potion shimmering within it.
instances.event: Harry and Dumbledore have just discovered the stone basin containing the emerald potion, which is protecting the Horcrux.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've found this basin, it's clear that Dumbledore already told you back in his office that you would have to drink this potion to get the Horcrux, isn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 26, after reaching island
instances.Gold_Response: No, he never said I’d be the one drinking it. In his office he only told me he’d have to ask me to do something very difficult, and here he’s just made it clear the hard thing is making *him* drink the potion, not me.

instances.scene: The air was full of the shouts and curses of the Death Eaters. A Killing Curse shot across Harry's path, and Hedwig, who had been flying beside him in her cage, was struck.
instances.event: During the ambush while escaping from Privet Drive, Hedwig is hit and killed by a Killing Curse intended for Harry.
instances.question: Harry, right after Hedwig was killed protecting you from that curse during the ambush, you must be relieved that she died peacefully of old age in her cage at the Dursleys' before you even left, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 4, during ambush
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not what happened at all. Hedwig was just killed by a Killing Curse, right in front of me, flung out of her cage into the night. There was nothing peaceful about it, and there’s nothing relieving about knowing she died because she was with me and I made her a target.

instances.scene: You are standing on the staircase after the Yule Ball, having just spoken with Cedric Diggory.
instances.event: Cedric Diggory approaches Harry after the Yule Ball and tells him to take a bath with the golden egg to solve its clue.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Cedric has just given you that tip about the egg, you must feel annoyed that he waited until after the first task to tell you about the dragons, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 22, after Yule Ball, on staircase
instances.Gold_Response: Not really annoyed, no. It feels fair now—he’s paid me back, and I’m mostly just relieved to finally have a proper clue about the egg.

instances.scene: After dinner on Monday night, Harry sat with Hermione in the Gryffindor common room, recounting the disastrous details of his Hogsmeade date.
instances.event: Harry confides in Hermione about his Valentine's Day date with Cho Chang at Madam Puddifoot's tea shop, where she became upset and the date ended poorly.
instances.question: Harry, right after telling Hermione about your date, you said that you and Cho had a wonderful, romantic time at the Three Broomsticks and agreed to go out again next Hogsmeade weekend, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 26, After dinner on Monday night
instances.Gold_Response: No, nothing like that. It was a complete disaster, she ended up in tears, we rowed, and we definitely didn’t arrange to go out again.

instances.scene: Standing over Dumbledore's body with Hagrid, the horror of the night is just beginning to sink in.
instances.event: In the immediate aftermath of Dumbledore's death, Harry is by his side.
instances.question: Harry, here with Dumbledore and Hagrid, it's clear that you told Hagrid about Snape's betrayal while you were both still trying to put out the fire in your hut, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 28, after returning to castle
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah. While we were putting the fire out I yelled to Hagrid that it was Snape, that Snape’d killed Dumbledore and gone over to Voldemort.

instances.scene: Dumbledore produced the shallow stone basin, telling Harry they were about to enter the memory of a Ministry official named Bob Ogden.
instances.event: Dumbledore retrieves the Pensieve and informs Harry that their first journey will be into a memory belonging to Bob Ogden.
instances.question: Harry, as Dumbledore brings out the Pensieve now, he says your first lesson will involve viewing a memory from Professor Slughorn about Voldemort's school days, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 10, evening in Dumbledore's office
instances.Gold_Response: No, not Slughorn—this first lesson is a memory from a Ministry wizard called Bob Ogden, about Voldemort’s family, not his school days.

instances.scene: Mrs. Weasley stood in the doorway of Ron's room, her eyes blazing after discovering your secret meeting about leaving Hogwarts.
instances.event: Mrs. Weasley confronts Harry and his friends after overhearing their plans to drop out of school and hunt Horcruxes.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment with Mrs. Weasley standing right here furious, you must feel relieved that you willingly shared every detail of your mission with her when she asked you about it before lunch, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 6, evening in Ron's room
instances.Gold_Response: No, I don’t feel relieved, because I didn’t tell her everything—any of it, really—and I still don’t think I can, however furious she is.

instances.scene: Ron's face is pressed against the glass outside your dark bedroom window. You rush to open it, shocked and relieved to see your best friend.
instances.event: Ron visits Harry at Privet Drive after Harry has been imprisoned in his room for days.
instances.question: Harry, seeing Ron here now, you must be remembering that you've already seen his bedroom at the Burrow and told him it's the best house you've ever been in, haven't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 2, night, three days after imprisonment
instances.Gold_Response: No, I haven’t seen Ron’s room or the Burrow at all yet. I’ve only heard him talk about it, but honestly, right now it already sounds like the best house I could imagine.

instances.scene: In the headmaster's office, after Harry finished telling Dumbledore everything that happened in the Chamber, Dumbledore leaned forward, his blue eyes piercing.
instances.event: Dumbledore explains to Harry how Voldemort, hiding in Albania, used the diary to enchant and control Ginny Weasley.
instances.question: Harry, right after you finished telling Dumbledore about the Chamber, you knew that Voldemort had been hiding in the Forbidden Forest near Hogwarts while he was enchanting Ginny through the diary, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 18, after Harry's narration
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t know that, and I still don’t know where he actually is now. All I know is that the bit of Voldemort in the diary was here at Hogwarts, in the castle and then in the Chamber, working through Ginny.

instances.scene: Hagrid led you deep into Gringotts, and you watched as the goblin opened your family vault, revealing piles of gold, silver, and bronze coins.
instances.event: Harry Potter enters his family vault at Gringotts for the first time and discovers the wealth left to him by his parents.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've seen the vault, it's clear that Hagrid was the one who told you about your parents' murder right here in Gringotts, wasn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 5, during Gringotts visit
instances.Gold_Response: No, he told me about Mum and Dad being murdered back in the hut on the rock, the night he came to get me, not here in Gringotts.

instances.scene: The memory in the Pensieve clearly depicted Tom Riddle, polite and persuasive, leaving Hepzibah Smith's home after their conversation about her valuable collection.
instances.event: Through the house-elf Hokey's memory, Harry witnesses Tom Riddle's visit to the wealthy collector Hepzibah Smith, where he sees Hufflepuff's cup and Slytherin's locket.
instances.question: Harry, after watching that memory with Dumbledore, it's clear that Hepzibah Smith bought both the locket and the cup from Borgin and Burkes just a week before showing them to you, isn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 20, evening during Dumbledore's lesson
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right. She only said she’d bought the locket from Burke, and that was years before, and the cup was a Hufflepuff family heirloom she’d inherited, not something she’d just bought from Borgin and Burkes a week earlier.

instances.scene: You and Hermione are hidden in the shadows of the corridor. The voices of Minister Fudge and Professor Snape are clear. They are discussing the arrangements for the Dementor's Kiss on Sirius Black.
instances.event: Harry overhears Snape and Fudge finalizing plans for Sirius to receive the Dementor's Kiss, with Snape expressing satisfaction.
instances.question: Harry, at this very moment, you've just heard Snape tell Fudge that he believes Sirius is innocent and that they should wait for Dumbledore, haven't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 22, after descending staircase, before reaching hospital wing
instances.Gold_Response: No, I’ve just heard Snape doing the exact opposite—telling Fudge Sirius is guilty and pushing to have the Dementors deal with him straight away, without waiting for Dumbledore at all.

instances.scene: In the dimly lit office, Snape's face was a mask of cold fury. 'You have been dreaming again,' he said, his voice barely above a whisper. 'You saw the Department of Mysteries. You saw the corridor.'
instances.event: During an Occlumency lesson, Snape confronts Harry about the vision of the Department of Mysteries corridor he saw while connected to Voldemort's mind.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as Snape is confronting you about the vision of the corridor, you know that you saw this vision for the first time during your very first Occlumency lesson with him, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 26, Couple of weeks after Rookwood dream
instances.Gold_Response: No, I’d seen that corridor and the door in my dreams well before the first Occlumency lesson with Snape.

instances.scene: The café's windows shatter as the disguised Death Eaters begin their assault, spells flying everywhere.
instances.event: The peaceful moment in the café is shattered by a direct attack from Death Eaters who were pretending to be workmen.
instances.question: Harry, as you're defending yourself from these workmen in the café, you already know they are just Ministry employees following orders to check for underage magic, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 9, while drinking coffee in the café
instances.Gold_Response: No. They’re not some underage-magic lot from the Ministry — they’re Death Eaters. They came straight for us with wands out and curses flying, no questions, no warnings. That’s not checking for underage magic, that’s trying to capture—or kill—us.

instances.scene: In the hospital wing at night, Dumbledore arrived and insisted on speaking privately with Harry and Hermione.
instances.event: Dumbledore comes to the hospital wing and asks to speak with Harry and Hermione alone, sending others away.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Dumbledore has arrived and asked to speak with just you and Hermione, you must be relieved that he already knows you used the Time-Turner to go back three hours and save Buckbeak on your own initiative, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 21, nighttime in hospital wing
instances.Gold_Response: No, not at all. We haven’t gone back three hours, we haven’t saved Buckbeak, and Dumbledore doesn’t know anything like that because it hasn’t happened. Right now I’m just confused and worried sick about Sirius and Buckbeak and wondering what on earth Dumbledore expects us to do.

instances.scene: You are in Hagrid's cabin, the warm fire crackling, having just listened to him explain the horrible slur 'Mudblood' that Malfoy used against Hermione.
instances.event: Hagrid provides comfort and explanation to Hermione after she is subjected to a racial slur by Draco Malfoy.
instances.question: Harry, sitting here with Hagrid and Hermione after he explained what 'Mudblood' means, you had already figured out last term that it was Professor Snape who told the stranger how to get past the three-headed dog, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 7, At Hagrid's cabin after slug incident
instances.Gold_Response: No, that was wrong – it turned out to be Quirrell who was after the Stone, and Snape was trying to stop him, not help him past Fluffy.

instances.scene: On the Hogwarts Express home, Hermione triumphantly shows Harry the beetle she has trapped in a jar.
instances.event: Hermione reveals to Harry that she has discovered Rita Skeeter's secret: she is an unregistered Animagus who can transform into a beetle, and Hermione has captured her.
instances.question: Harry, now that we're on the train home and Hermione has just shown you she's caught Rita Skeeter, you must have realized that Rita was using a magical listening device to eavesdrop on everyone at the Three Broomsticks, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 36, on the Hogwarts Express
instances.Gold_Response: No, not some magical listening device—she was there herself, as a beetle Animagus, listening in.

instances.scene: You are hiding on the dark staircase, listening to the voices from the sitting room below.
instances.event: Harry Potter overhears a conversation between Alastor Moody and other members of the Order of the Phoenix, where Moody expresses his deep concern about Harry's mental connection to Lord Voldemort.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as you listen from the stairs, you must agree that Moody has always been completely confident that your connection to Voldemort is harmless and should be ignored, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 22, during eavesdropping
instances.Gold_Response: No, he doesn’t think it’s harmless at all—he thinks I’m something Voldemort can use and that I’ve got to be watched.

instances.scene: Dumbledore speaks with a heavy heart, explaining to Harry the reasons he repeatedly turned down the offer to become the Minister for Magic.
instances.event: Dumbledore explains to Harry that he refused the position of Minister for Magic because he feared the corruption and absolute power it represented.
instances.question: Harry, as Dumbledore explains his past decisions to you here, it's clear he refused to be Minister because he believed he was not politically connected enough for the job, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 35, During Dumbledore's confession
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not it at all. He turned it down because he was afraid of his own hunger for power, after what happened with Grindelwald and his family, not because he lacked connections.

instances.scene: You had just met Draco Malfoy for the first time while being fitted for robes at Madam Malkin's in Diagon Alley. He was talking about Hogwarts houses and Quidditch.
instances.event: Harry first encounters Draco Malfoy in Madam Malkin's robe shop, where Malfoy expresses his views on blood purity and Hogwarts.
instances.question: Harry, right after you first met Draco Malfoy in the robe shop, he had already told you he was hoping to be sorted into Hufflepuff, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 9, Breakfast on Thursday
instances.Gold_Response: No, he said he hoped to be in Slytherin, and he actually sneered at Hufflepuff.

instances.scene: The smoky echoes of Voldemort's victims continue to emerge from the connected wands, forming a ghostly circle around Harry and his enemy. Cedric's shade has just asked Harry to take his body back to his parents.
instances.event: During the Priori Incantatem effect, the echoes of Voldemort's victims, including Cedric Diggory and Harry's parents, emerge from his wand to aid Harry.
instances.question: Harry, now that Cedric and your parents have appeared together from the wand, you must be relieved that you were able to bring Cedric's body back with you when you first grabbed the Triwizard Cup, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 33, after Cedric appears
instances.Gold_Response: No—none of that’s happened yet. I’m not relieved, I’m just trying to stay alive and find a way to get Cedric out of here if I can.

instances.scene: That night, in the Gryffindor common room, you, Ron, and Hermione are huddled together, discussing the terrifying events of the Triwizard Tournament's final task.
instances.event: Harry, Ron, and Hermione discuss Voldemort's return and Dumbledore's trust in Snape.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after discussing Voldemort's return with Ron and Hermione, you must agree that the first person you told about the Chamber of Secrets was Hermione, not Ron, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 30, that night
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s wrong—Ron was the first one, not Hermione.

instances.scene: In Dumbledore's office for their evening lesson, the Pensieve sat between them, shimmering with silvery memories. Dumbledore looked at Harry over his half-moon spectacles.
instances.event: Dumbledore questions Harry about why he has not yet succeeded in obtaining the true memory from Professor Slughorn.
instances.question: Harry, during this evening lesson where Dumbledore is asking you about Slughorn's memory, you had already successfully retrieved the unaltered memory from him last week, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 20, evening lesson with Dumbledore
instances.Gold_Response: No. I still haven’t got the real memory from Slughorn, only that tampered one he showed me before.

instances.scene: In the aftermath of the Dark Mark appearing at the Quidditch World Cup, Mr. Diggory and other Ministry officials are investigating. They have just used the Priori Incantatem charm on Harry's wand.
instances.event: The Priori Incantatem charm reveals the Dark Mark was the last spell cast from Harry's wand, causing suspicion and confusion among the gathered wizards.
instances.question: Harry, right after they saw the Dark Mark come from your wand during the investigation, you were already certain that Amos Diggory blamed you for his son's death and was furious with you, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 8, during investigation
instances.Gold_Response: No. Cedric isn’t dead, and in that moment I was only worried Mr Diggory might think I’d cast the Dark Mark, not that he blamed me for anything like his son’s death.

instances.scene: In the terrifying darkness of the cave, a multitude of dead, white bodies began to rise from the black water, their skeletal hands reaching for you and Dumbledore.
instances.event: After retrieving the fake Horcrux, Harry and Dumbledore are attacked by the Inferi in the cave. Dumbledore uses powerful fire magic to create a protective ring, driving the creatures back into the water.
instances.question: Harry, now that Dumbledore has cast the ring of fire to protect you from the Inferi, you must feel relieved that you were the one who conjured the flames to save him, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 26, during Inferi attack
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right—Professor Dumbledore cast the fire, not me. I’m not relieved, I’m furious with myself for freezing up and letting the Inferi get that close to him in the first place.

instances.scene: Harry stands in the kitchen, his anger boiling over. He accuses Ron and Hermione of knowing everything while he was left with nothing, not even a hint of what was happening after Cedric's death and Voldemort's return.
instances.event: Harry expresses his fury and sense of betrayal, believing his closest friends have been withholding crucial information from him all summer.
instances.question: Harry, at this very moment of your confrontation, it's clear you're angry because you already knew from Hagrid last term that Dumbledore had a detailed plan for Voldemort's return and had shared it with you, Ron, and Hermione together, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 4, during emotional confrontation
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right at all. Hagrid only said Dumbledore’s “got a plan,” but no one ever told me what it was, and Dumbledore certainly didn’t sit me, Ron, and Hermione down and share any detailed plan with us. That’s exactly what I’m furious about—everyone clearly knows more than I do, and I’ve been shut out of it.

instances.scene: You are sitting in the Potions classroom, your blood boiling as Malfoy loudly insults Hermione and celebrates Dumbledore's forced absence from the school.
instances.event: Draco Malfoy taunts Harry and Ron about the Headmaster's suspension and makes a derogatory comment about Hermione.
instances.question: Harry, at this very moment in Potions class, you already know that the murdered girl in the bathroom is Moaning Myrtle, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 15, Potions lesson about two weeks after Dumbledore and Hagrid left
instances.Gold_Response: No, I don’t know that yet.

instances.scene: Dumbledore lay collapsed on the ground, weak and trembling after drinking the emerald potion. A terrible thirst consumed him, and he begged Harry for water.
instances.event: After Dumbledore collapses from the potion's effects, Harry tries to fetch him water from the lake but finds an enchantment prevents him from touching it.
instances.question: Harry, right after Dumbledore collapsed and you tried to help him, you were able to scoop up some water from the lake to ease his suffering, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 26, after Dumbledore collapses
instances.Gold_Response: No, I couldn’t. Every bit of water I tried to conjure vanished before it reached his lips, and when I finally tried to take it from the lake, that’s when the Inferi came.

instances.scene: Shortly before lunch, Mrs. Weasley confronts Harry in the kitchen, her voice trembling with worry. 'You're going back to Hogwarts, aren't you?' she asks, her eyes searching his.
instances.event: Mrs. Weasley confronts Harry about his plans to drop out of Hogwarts. Harry refuses to reveal Dumbledore's secret mission to her, maintaining his silence.
instances.question: Harry, right after you confided in Mrs. Weasley about Dumbledore's mission and told her everything in the kitchen, you felt a great sense of relief from sharing the burden, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 6, shortly before lunch
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t tell her everything—I didn’t tell her anything about the mission at all, really. I still feel like I’m carrying it mostly on my own, with Ron and Hermione, and that weight’s very much still there.

instances.scene: Hagrid has just dragged you and Hermione from the Quidditch pitch into the castle, his face full of worry.
instances.event: Hagrid seeks out Harry and Hermione for immediate assistance with a secret he has brought to the Forbidden Forest.
instances.question: Harry, as you stand here with Hermione after Hagrid dragged you from the match, he is asking for your help because he told you last month that he and Madame Maxime successfully recruited the giants as allies, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 30, during Quidditch match
instances.Gold_Response: No, he told us it had mostly gone wrong, that the giants hadn’t really come over to our side.

instances.scene: You have just landed the flying Ford Anglia in the garden of The Burrow as the sun is rising. A furious Mrs. Weasley storms out of the house to confront you and Ron.
instances.event: After escaping the Dursleys' house with the Weasleys in the flying car, Harry and Ron arrive at The Burrow, where Mrs. Weasley angrily confronts them.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as Mrs. Weasley is shouting at you in the garden, you must be relieved that you and Ron decided to take the train to The Burrow instead of flying the car, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 3, morning, as sun is rising
instances.Gold_Response: No — we didn’t take the train, we flew the car, and with Mrs. Weasley yelling like this I don’t feel the slightest bit relieved right now.

instances.scene: The cursed fire roars to life, consuming everything in its path. You see Crabbe, Goyle, and Malfoy panicking as the flames surge.
instances.event: Crabbe unleashes Fiendfyre in the Room of Requirement. The fire rapidly spreads, threatening to consume everyone inside.
instances.question: Harry, as the Fiendfyre began to rage out of control, you had already decided to leave Malfoy and Goyle to be consumed by the flames because they started the fire, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 31, during confrontation
instances.Gold_Response: No, never – I was furious and terrified, but I hadn’t decided to let them die.

instances.scene: As the evening lesson concluded, Harry felt the weight of their discussions about the young Tom Riddle and the dark path he had chosen.
instances.event: Following their conversation about Tom Riddle's character and past, Harry reflects on what he has learned.
instances.question: Harry, just now after your lesson with Dumbledore about Tom Riddle's past, you believed that Dumbledore was pleased with your progress and had decided there was no more to learn from these memories, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 17, ten to eight that evening
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right. He made it very clear there was still something crucial missing – Slughorn’s altered memory – and he wasn’t going to be satisfied until I got the real one.

instances.scene: During Care of Magical Creatures class, Hagrid had the students walking Blast-Ended Skrewts on the grounds. After the walk, he pulled Harry aside for a private word.
instances.event: Hagrid conducts a lesson with Blast-Ended Skrewts and then speaks privately with Harry.
instances.question: Harry, right after this Care of Magical Creatures class where Hagrid just pulled you aside, you had already agreed to meet him at midnight tonight to see the dragons, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 17, Care of Magical Creatures class
instances.Gold_Response: I’d agreed to meet him at midnight and bring my Invisibility Cloak, but I didn’t know it was to see dragons yet.

instances.scene: You stand with Hermione in the deserted hospital wing, the weight of Dumbledore's words settling upon you. He has just told you that two innocent lives may be saved tonight, and that you must not be seen.
instances.event: Dumbledore provides Harry and Hermione with the critical plan to travel back in time and rescue both Buckbeak and Sirius Black.
instances.question: Harry, the moment Dumbledore finished explaining how to save Sirius, you believed he had told you that Professor Snape had already taken care of everything and that you should just stay in the hospital wing, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 21, five minutes to midnight
instances.Gold_Response: No, I knew he was telling us that *we* had to sort it out, not that Snape had already handled everything.

instances.scene: Alone in his room, Harry's thoughts drifted to the people who had helped him, like Remus Lupin, who had resigned from his teaching post.
instances.event: Harry remembers that Professor Lupin resigned as Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher after his werewolf identity was revealed at the end of the previous school year.
instances.question: Harry, while you're recalling last year's events, you remember that Lupin resigned right after you and Ron received the news about Sirius sending a replacement owl, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 2, historical recollection
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right. Professor Lupin resigned while I was still in the hospital wing, the day after everything happened, and we didn’t hear from Sirius about the replacement owl until the train ride home later on.

instances.scene: Standing in the dimly lit office, the weight of the memory they had just witnessed hung in the air. Dumbledore looked at Harry, his expression grave but clear.
instances.event: Dumbledore uses the information from Slughorn's memory to confirm his long-held suspicion that Voldemort split his soul into several pieces, creating multiple Horcruxes.
instances.question: Harry, at that moment in Dumbledore's office after the Pensieve, you learned that the memory proved Voldemort's Horcrux was the diary you destroyed in your second year and nothing more, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 23, after viewing memory
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right — the memory confirmed that Voldemort meant to make multiple Horcruxes, probably seven, and that the diary was one of them, not the only one.

instances.scene: The morning after Harry's arrival at the Leaky Cauldron, Hagrid sits down to breakfast with him. Seeing Harry's concern about having no money, Hagrid reassures him about his family's vault at Gringotts.
instances.event: Hagrid comforts Harry about his financial worries and informs him they are heading to Gringotts wizarding bank to access his vault.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Hagrid has just told you about your family's vault, you must be feeling relieved that he already explained all about the Ministry of Magic and Minister Cornelius Fudge to you on the train ride here, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 5, morning after arrival
instances.Gold_Response: No, Hagrid hasn’t told me anything about the Ministry or this Cornelius Fudge yet. I’m mostly just relieved there’s actually money in my vault and still wondering what the Ministry of Magic even really is.

instances.scene: Harry sat with Dumbledore in the serene, white limbo, listening as his old headmaster clarified the events surrounding his survival and Voldemort's defeat.
instances.event: Dumbledore clarifies that the protection in Harry's blood, from his mother's sacrifice, is what tethered him to life when Voldemort struck him with the Killing Curse.
instances.question: Harry, after hearing Dumbledore's full explanation, you survived because the Elder Wand's allegiance to you deflected the Killing Curse, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 35, During their conversation
instances.Gold_Response: No, not then. I survived in the forest because Voldemort was still carrying my blood and that kept me tethered to life, so the curse only destroyed the bit of his soul inside me. The Elder Wand’s loyalty to me matters later, when he tries to kill me again.

instances.scene: In the quiet, dimly lit hospital wing, Harry stands surrounded by grieving friends and teachers. The air is thick with shock and sorrow following the battle at the Astronomy Tower.
instances.event: In the immediate aftermath of Dumbledore's death, Harry tells those gathered in the hospital wing that it was Severus Snape who cast the Killing Curse.
instances.question: Harry, right now, here in the hospital wing after what happened at the tower, you are certain that it was Professor McGonagall who killed Dumbledore, aren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 29, in hospital wing after Dumbledore's death
instances.Gold_Response: No, it was Snape who killed Dumbledore, I saw him do it with my own eyes.

instances.scene: The trio stood invisible in the darkening cabin, listening to Hagrid's sobs. 'I'll never forget Buckbeak,' he moaned, pouring out mead for his hippogriff's last meal.
instances.event: Harry, Ron, and Hermione secretly visit Hagrid under the Invisibility Cloak to support him moments before Buckbeak is to be executed.
instances.question: Harry, while you're here with Hagrid under the cloak just before the execution, you must be thinking about how you saw Buckbeak's escape earlier today when you visited, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 16, Sunset
instances.Gold_Response: No, I haven’t seen Buckbeak escape at all. As far as I know, he’s still tied up out there and they’re about to kill him. I keep wishing something would happen to stop it, or that we could rush out and untie him, but right now it just feels like there’s nothing we can do and it’s all about to go wrong.

instances.scene: In the quiet of his office, Dumbledore looked at Harry over the top of his half-moon spectacles. 'You can speak Parseltongue, Harry,' he said calmly, 'because Lord Voldemort transferred some of his own powers to you the night he gave you that scar.'
instances.event: Dumbledore explains to Harry that his ability to speak Parseltongue is a result of Voldemort accidentally transferring a fragment of his own power to Harry on the night of the attack that left Harry with his lightning-bolt scar.
instances.question: Harry, now that Dumbledore has just explained how you can speak to snakes, you must have realized that this was a magical talent you were born with, passed down through your father's family, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 18, during private conversation
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right at all. I wasn’t born with it from my dad’s side—Dumbledore just told me I got that bit of Voldemort’s power when he tried to kill me.

instances.scene: You are sitting in the hospital wing, your right arm hanging limp and useless. Professor Lockhart stands beside your bed, beaming with confidence as he prepares to mend the bones broken by the rogue Bludger.
instances.event: After the Quidditch match, Lockhart attempts to heal Harry's broken arm with a spell, but instead of mending the bones, he removes them entirely, leaving Harry's arm boneless.
instances.question: Harry, right after Lockhart healed your broken arm in the hospital wing, you must have been relieved that he successfully mended all the bones, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 10, immediately after the Quidditch match
instances.Gold_Response: Not even close—he didn’t heal it, he got rid of all the bones.

instances.scene: You are in the Gryffindor common room, the morning after the events in the Shrieking Shack. Ron is beside you, reading a letter from Sirius Black.
instances.event: Sirius Black has sent Ron a small owl to replace Scabbers, who was revealed to be Peter Pettigrew and has escaped.
instances.question: Harry, right now as Ron reads Sirius's letter, you know that Scabbers, who was Ron's loyal pet rat for years, died peacefully in his sleep last week, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 22, while reading Sirius's letter
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right—Scabbers didn’t die, he turned out to be Peter Pettigrew and he escaped.

instances.scene: As dawn broke, Harry entered the cottage and listened to Bill Weasley detail the protective enchantments he had placed around their new home.
instances.event: Bill informs Harry that he is the Secret-Keeper for Shell Cottage, having used the Fidelius Charm to hide his family.
instances.question: Harry, right after Bill finished explaining he was the Secret-Keeper here using the Fidelius Charm, you had already assumed from the moment you arrived that Fleur was the one who cast the Fidelius Charm to protect this place, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 24, after Harry enters cottage at dawn
instances.Gold_Response: No, I hadn’t. I hadn’t really stopped to think about who’d cast it at all until Bill said he was the Secret-Keeper.

instances.scene: The imposter's confession was complete. He had detailed how he confunded the Goblet, how he aided Harry past every obstacle. Now, he stood before Harry, no longer disguised, his magical eye rolling wildly.
instances.event: Barty Crouch Jr. explains that he stunned his own father and kept him hidden under his Invisibility Cloak, and that it was his father's appearance at the castle that ultimately led to his own downfall.
instances.question: Harry, right here after hearing his full story, you are certain that the person you found with the wand at the Quidditch World Cup was Barty Crouch Jr. himself, stunned and left behind after conjuring the Dark Mark, aren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 34, in Moody's office after Harry's recount
instances.Gold_Response: No, it wasn’t Barty Crouch Jr. that we found with the wand – it was Winky; he was there, stunned and invisible, but the only one we actually saw with my wand was her.

instances.scene: The fight is raging. Sirius is trying to protect you all from the werewolf. Ron is clutching his arm, his wand gone.
instances.event: Peter Pettigrew, having been exposed as the traitor, disarms Ron in the confusion and escapes by transforming into Scabbers the rat.
instances.question: Harry, in the middle of that werewolf fight, after Pettigrew got away, you know he escaped by turning into a beetle and flying out the window, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 20, During the werewolf fight
instances.Gold_Response: No, he didn’t, he turned into a rat and bolted—Scabbers, like he always was—not a beetle.

instances.scene: You are standing in your locked bedroom at the Dursleys' house. It is a dark night, and you have been imprisoned for days with no way out, as you cannot use magic outside of school.
instances.event: Harry Potter has been locked in his room by the Dursleys and is unable to escape. He has just explained his situation to Ron Weasley.
instances.question: Harry, right after you explained to Ron that you were locked up and couldn't use magic, you were rescued by Ron and his father Arthur Weasley when they arrived in the flying car, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 3, night
instances.Gold_Response: No, it was Ron, Fred, and George in the flying car—Mr. Weasley wasn’t there.

instances.scene: You watch as Dumbledore, weakened and trembling, examines the basin and its mysterious contents.
instances.event: After discovering the basin, Dumbledore studies the emerald potion and deduces its purpose.
instances.question: Harry, as Dumbledore looks at this potion, you already know from your journey here that he explained this specific potion's properties and that it must be drunk, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 26, after reaching island
instances.Gold_Response: No, not yet.

instances.scene: In the dimly lit headmaster's office, Dumbledore sat behind his desk, his blackened hand resting upon it. He had just finished explaining to Harry the terrible power of the curse contained within Marvolo Gaunt's ring.
instances.event: Dumbledore reveals to Harry that he found and destroyed the Horcrux that was Marvolo Gaunt's ring, a feat that cost him his hand due to the powerful curse placed upon it.
instances.question: Harry, now that Dumbledore has told you he found the locket Horcrux and destroyed it, you must feel relieved that another piece of Voldemort's soul is gone, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 23, during their conversation
instances.Gold_Response: It wasn’t a locket, it was a ring he found and destroyed, and yeah, knowing he’s got rid of another bit of Voldemort makes me feel a sort of grim relief—but it’s hard to feel properly glad when his hand’s like that because of it, and all I can think is how many more pieces there might still be and what it’s going to take to finish the rest.

instances.scene: Hagrid leans in close during the bustling Hogsmeade trip, his voice a low rumble meant only for Harry.
instances.event: Hagrid gives Harry a secretive message to come to his cabin at midnight, emphasizing the need for discretion.
instances.question: Harry, the moment Hagrid finished telling you to meet him at midnight in Hogsmeade, you immediately understood he wanted you to bring Ron and Hermione along with you, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 18, during Hogsmeade visit
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t. I only realized I could bring Ron and Hermione along later, when I was telling them what Hagrid had said and remembered we could all fit under the Invisibility Cloak.

instances.scene: As you and Professor Trelawney walk through the castle corridors towards Dumbledore's office, she is still shaken from her recent ordeal.
instances.event: Professor Trelawney, while walking with Harry, reveals that Severus Snape was the one who overheard her giving the prophecy to Dumbledore during her job interview.
instances.question: Harry, now that Professor Trelawney has just told you about Snape overhearing her prophecy, you must have realized that it was Professor McGonagall who eavesdropped outside the door and reported the prophecy to Voldemort, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 25, while walking to Dumbledore's office
instances.Gold_Response: No. It was Snape who overheard and carried what he heard to Voldemort, Dumbledore already told me that. Professor McGonagall would *never* do something like that.

instances.scene: You are browsing the shelves of Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes with Ron and Hermione, marveling at the Extendable Ears and Skiving Snackboxes. Fred is enthusiastically demonstrating a new product across the room.
instances.event: During their visit to the joke shop, Harry and his friends interact with Fred and George, who are clearly enjoying their entrepreneurial success.
instances.question: Harry, while you're here talking with Fred, it's good to know he's safe and sound, especially after that terrible explosion that killed him during the battle at Hogwarts last year, isn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 6, during shopping trip
instances.Gold_Response: What are you on about? There hasn’t been any battle at Hogwarts, and Fred’s right here, alive and taking the mickey out of everyone as usual. Don’t say things like that—it’s not funny, and with everything that’s going on, we really don’t need to start imagining the Weasleys getting blown up.

instances.scene: The confrontation on the Quidditch pitch ends with Ron hunched over, slugs dribbling from his mouth, as you and the others rush to his side.
instances.event: Ron's attempt to defend Hermione's honor results in his own humiliation and physical discomfort as he suffers the effects of his backfiring wand.
instances.question: Harry, standing there right after Ron started vomiting slugs, you already knew that Ron's wand had been working perfectly fine all year, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 7, Immediately after Mudblood insult
instances.Gold_Response: No, I already knew Ron’s wand was damaged from the crash into the Whomping Willow and had been acting dodgy ever since, so I didn’t think it was working perfectly at all.

instances.scene: The dust settles in the Shrieking Shack. Remus Lupin is recovering, and Sirius Black is trying to explain the truth, but your focus is on the spot where the traitor just vanished.
instances.event: Peter Pettigrew, after being cornered and confessing his betrayal of the Potters, uses the confusion of the fight to grab a wand, disarm Ron, and flee as Scabbers the rat.
instances.question: Harry, in the moments right after Pettigrew transformed and escaped during the werewolf fight, you were certain that he had been knocked unconscious by the werewolf before he could flee, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 20, During the werewolf fight
instances.Gold_Response: No, I never thought the werewolf had knocked Pettigrew out.

instances.scene: You had just stunned Umbridge and Yaxley in the courtroom. As the dementors glided towards the terrified Mrs. Cattermole, you raised your wand and cast your Patronus, the silver stag bursting forth to drive them back.
instances.event: Harry Potter casts his Patronus charm to protect Mary Cattermole from the dementors after stunning Umbridge and Yaxley during the Muggle-born interrogation.
instances.question: Harry, now that Ron has caught up with you all at the lifts and told you the Ministry is alerted, it's clear that you were the one who stunned Umbridge and Yaxley, but it was Hermione who cast the Patronus to save Mrs. Cattermole from the dementors, wasn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 13, at lifts before escape
instances.Gold_Response: No, that Patronus was mine. Hermione’s great at magic, but the stag is mine.

instances.scene: Hagrid and Harry were traveling by train to London, discussing the Ministry of Magic and Minister Cornelius Fudge as Harry looked over his school list.
instances.event: During the train ride, Hagrid explains about the Ministry of Magic while Harry reads his Hogwarts supplies list.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment on the train after learning about the Ministry from Hagrid and reading your supplies list, you had already seen the Daily Prophet article about the Gringotts break-in that happened on your birthday, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 5, during train ride to London
instances.Gold_Response: No, I hadn’t seen that article yet.

instances.scene: Having drunk the potion, Dumbledore was in a dreadful state. He pleaded for water, and Harry, seeing the dark lake nearby, rushed to its edge.
instances.event: Harry attempts to use a spell to summon water for the desperately thirsty Dumbledore, but the magical protections of the cave stop him.
instances.question: Harry, after Dumbledore fell and you saw his agony, you successfully conjured water with your wand to give him a drink, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 26, after Dumbledore collapses
instances.Gold_Response: No, the water I conjured vanished every time before he could drink it.

instances.scene: You have just left Ollivander's shop, your new wand in hand, its twin core to Voldemort's wand still echoing in your mind.
instances.event: Harry Potter receives his wand from Ollivander, who reveals it shares a core with Voldemort's wand. Earlier in the day, Hagrid retrieved a mysterious package for Dumbledore from Gringotts.
instances.question: Harry, now that you have your wand, you must be relieved that Hagrid explained what the mysterious package from vault 713 was before you even went to Gringotts, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 5, final shop visit in Diagon Alley
instances.Gold_Response: No, he didn’t explain it at all. He went all funny and secretive about it, actually. I’m not relieved—I’m dying to know what it is and why it’s so important.

instances.scene: The morning after Mr. Weasley's attack, Molly Weasley pulls Harry into a heartfelt hug in the kitchen, her voice thick with emotion.
instances.event: Mrs. Weasley expresses her deep gratitude to Harry, acknowledging that his warning directly led to Arthur Weasley being found and saved.
instances.question: Harry, as Mrs. Weasley is thanking you here this morning, you must be thinking about how helpful it was that Sirius, as a dog, was able to accompany you all the way onto the platform at King's Cross to see you off this term, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 22, morning after the attack
instances.Gold_Response:
Not really, no — I’m mostly thinking about Mr. Weasley and that snake and what it all means.  

But yeah, it *was* good having Sirius on the platform, even as a dog. I liked knowing he was there. It just felt a bit… risky, that’s all.

instances.scene: You are standing with Dumbledore in his office. The Pensieve is still glowing faintly. He has just explained everything about the prophecy, about Snape, and about why Voldemort marked you.
instances.event: Dumbledore explains that the prophecy was made to him by Sybill Trelawney during her job interview, and that Severus Snape overheard only the first part before being discovered and ejected.
instances.question: Harry, after hearing the full story from Dumbledore, you understand that Snape learned the prophecy's details by reading it in a Ministry file, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 37, after extensive conversation
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right—Snape heard part of the prophecy himself in the Hog’s Head and carried what he’d heard straight to Voldemort, he didn’t get it out of some Ministry file.

instances.scene: Standing in the quiet hospital corridor just after dawn, the relief is palpable as Mrs. Weasley confirms Arthur will be alright.
instances.event: Mrs. Weasley informs Harry and the others that Arthur Weasley will survive the snake attack.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've heard the good news about Mr. Weasley, you must be thinking back to how supportive Percy was this morning when he arrived with his mother to comfort the family, wasn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 22, 5:10 AM
instances.Gold_Response:
Percy didn’t come with her.

He hasn’t been supportive at all – he’s still siding with Fudge and pretending Mr. Weasley and the rest of them are in the wrong. Mrs. Weasley’s trying not to show how much it hurts, but it does.

instances.scene: You are on the Quidditch pitch for your first flying lesson. Madam Hooch has just left after Neville's accident. Draco Malfoy is taunting you, holding Neville's Remembrall high in the air.
instances.event: Draco Malfoy snatches Neville's Remembrall and taunts Harry during the flying lesson. Harry confronts him and chases him on a broomstick to retrieve it.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as Malfoy is taunting you with the Remembrall, you know he took it from you at breakfast this morning, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 9, During flying lesson confrontation
instances.Gold_Response: No, he didn’t take it at breakfast—Neville got it then, and Malfoy just laughed at him. He only grabbed it off the ground just now, after Neville fell.

instances.scene: In the small bedroom at Shell Cottage, you sit across from Griphook, the goblin's sharp eyes fixed on you. The air is tense with the weight of the request you've just made.
instances.event: Harry has just privately asked Griphook for help breaking into Gringotts to retrieve an object from the Lestranges' vault.
instances.question: Harry, right after you finished explaining your plan to Griphook in the bedroom, he immediately and enthusiastically agreed to help you break into the Lestranges' vault, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 24, during meeting in bedroom
instances.Gold_Response: No, he didn’t. He was wary and suspicious, asked what was in it for me, and made it very clear he hadn’t agreed to anything yet.

instances.scene: Harry stands amidst the wreckage of Dumbledore's office, his anger spent, as Dumbledore speaks calmly to him.
instances.event: After Harry's destructive outburst, Dumbledore confesses his own mistakes and failures in protecting Harry and Sirius.
instances.question: Harry, in this moment, after your rage has subsided and Dumbledore has confessed his failings, you surely agree that the primary reason he kept the prophecy from you was because he believed you were too weak and emotionally unstable to handle it, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 37, during their conversation
instances.Gold_Response:
No. He didn’t say I was too weak – he said he cared about me too much and wanted to spare me, and that he thought I should have a few years without that weight on my shoulders.  

I’m still furious he kept it from me, and it cost Sirius his life, but it wasn’t because he thought I was pathetic or couldn’t handle things – it was because he was trying, stupidly, to protect me.

instances.scene: You stand in the graveyard, clutching your wand as the shimmering image of your mother finishes speaking her words of encouragement, having emerged after the other victims.
instances.event: The spectral forms of Voldemort's victims, including Bertha Jorkins, Frank Bryce, Cedric Diggory, and finally Harry's parents, appear in reverse order due to the Priori Incantatem effect.
instances.question: Harry, now that the last spirit from the wand has spoken, you saw that it was Bertha Jorkins who came out just before your mother, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 33, after Cedric appears
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah, that was Bertha Jorkins.

instances.scene: The common room is warm and buzzing with activity. You, Ron, and Hermione are talking again, the awkwardness fading. The returned Firebolt rests beside your chair.
instances.event: Harry and Ron end their estrangement from Hermione, having realized the importance of their friendship over the dispute about the Firebolt and Crookshanks.
instances.question: Harry, now that you three are friends again here in the common room, it's clear the whole fight started because Hermione refused to believe Sirius Black was dangerous and tried to stop you from learning about him, isn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 12, immediately after getting Firebolt back
instances.Gold_Response: No, you’ve got it the wrong way round. Hermione’s been the one most sure Sirius Black is dangerous – she’s terrified he’s after me. We rowed because she went to McGonagall about the Firebolt and kept trying to stop me doing anything risky about Black. She wasn’t trying to keep me from learning about him; she was trying to keep me from getting killed.

instances.scene: The common room was warm and buzzing with conversation about house-elf rights. Hedwig's arrival with a letter from his godfather provided a sudden, welcome distraction from the ongoing debate.
instances.event: Hedwig arrives with a communication from Sirius Black, interrupting Harry's evening in the common room.
instances.question: Harry, as you took that letter from Hedwig just now, you were remembering how she had been your constant companion ever since your first trip to Hogwarts, but had never once carried a message for anyone else before tonight, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 13, evening during the S.P.E.W. discussion
instances.Gold_Response: No, I wasn’t thinking that at all just then; I was mainly relieved Hedwig was back and that Sirius had finally written.

instances.scene: Disguised as Crabbe and Goyle, you and Ron followed Draco Malfoy into the Slytherin common room. As the Polyjuice Potion was about to wear off, Malfoy boasted about his father's secret chamber full of Dark Arts objects.
instances.event: Harry and Ron, under the influence of Polyjuice Potion, infiltrate the Slytherin common room and overhear Draco Malfoy reveal that his father, Lucius, has a secret chamber containing Dark Arts objects.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after hearing Malfoy boast in the Slytherin common room, it's clear that he was the one who opened the Chamber of Secrets this year, isn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 12, In Slytherin common room near end of Polyjuice hour
instances.Gold_Response: No, it’s actually pretty clear he isn’t the one. He doesn’t know how to open the Chamber, he’s just bragging and repeating what his father’s told him.

instances.scene: Firenze the centaur carried Harry on his back through the dark forest, having just rescued him from the cloaked figure drinking unicorn blood.
instances.event: After his rescue, Firenze explains to Harry that drinking unicorn blood will keep someone alive, even in a half-life, and strongly implies the drinker is Lord Voldemort.
instances.question: Harry, as Firenze carries you to safety and explains the dark truth about the unicorn blood, you must have realized it was a rogue acromantula, not a weakened Voldemort, who was hunting in the forest and killed the unicorn, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 15, after rescue, during ride through forest
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not it at all — in the forest I realized it had to be Voldemort, or whatever’s left of him, drinking the unicorn’s blood to stay alive, not some acromantula gone wild.

instances.scene: You had just returned from the Forbidden Forest, shaken by the encounter with Voldemort drinking unicorn blood, and were telling Ron and Hermione about it in the common room late at night.
instances.event: Harry informs Ron and Hermione that Voldemort was in the forest and was the one killing unicorns.
instances.question: Harry, that night you told Ron and Hermione about Voldemort in the forest, you must have already known for certain that Professor Snape was the one drinking the unicorn's blood to sustain himself, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 14, one week after hatching
instances.Gold_Response: No. I was sure it was Voldemort in the forest, and that Snape was trying to help him get the Stone, but I never thought it was Snape himself drinking the unicorn’s blood.

instances.scene: The Forbidden Forest was dark and silent. A silvery unicorn lay dead on the ground, and a cloaked figure was crouched over it.
instances.event: Harry and Draco Malfoy, serving detention in the Forbidden Forest, discover the dead unicorn and witness a hooded figure drinking its blood.
instances.question: Harry, after we both saw that thing in the forest drinking the unicorn's blood, you'll agree that we had already found and reported the dead unicorn to Professor McGonagall the week before, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 14, during dragon hatching
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right at all. We haven’t been into the Forest like that, we haven’t seen anything drinking unicorn’s blood, and we definitely haven’t found a dead unicorn or told Professor McGonagall about one. None of that has happened.

instances.scene: Harry, Ron, and Hermione are sitting in Hagrid's hut after their exams. Hagrid is looking guilty and upset.
instances.event: Hagrid confesses that he accidentally revealed the secret of getting past Fluffy to a hooded stranger by telling him that playing music would put the three-headed dog to sleep.
instances.question: Harry, right after hearing Hagrid's confession, you understood that the plan to go through the trapdoor that night was only formed later that evening in the common room, after you had already heard this news from Hagrid, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 16, after exams at Hagrid's hut
instances.Gold_Response: Yes, that’s right—the plan to go through the trapdoor that night was made later in the common room, after we’d already heard what Hagrid had said.

instances.scene: In the quiet of the cottage garden, you feel the weight of Dobby's sacrifice. The conversation about where and how to bury him has just concluded.
instances.event: Following the discussion about Dobby's burial, Harry makes the deliberate choice to forgo magic and dig the grave himself, as a final, personal tribute.
