instances.event: Following the discovery of the attack on Mrs. Norris, Draco Malfoy publicly revels in the situation and issues a threat to the 'Mudbloods' at Hogwarts.
instances.question: Harry, right there in the corridor after the feast when you saw the message and Malfoy threatening everyone, you already knew for a fact that the Heir of Slytherin was a student from Gryffindor, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 8, Immediately after the feast ends on Halloween night
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t know that, and I definitely don’t believe the Heir of Slytherin is from Gryffindor.

instances.scene: It is a dark night, three days after you were locked in your room. You are staring out the window of your bedroom at Privet Drive, feeling utterly miserable and trapped.
instances.event: Ron Weasley appears outside Harry's window in the middle of the night, having come to check on him.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as you see Ron outside your window, you must be thinking about how you were rescued from this room by him, Fred, and George in their flying car last night, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 2, night, three days after imprisonment
instances.Gold_Response: No, that hasn’t happened yet—Ron’s only just turned up at my window, and I’ve got no idea how he’s planning to get me out.

instances.scene: Christmas morning at Grimmauld Place found Harry with the Weasley siblings, exchanging gifts and holiday greetings.
instances.event: Fred and George inform Harry that Percy returned the Christmas sweater Molly made for him, showing continued estrangement from the family.
instances.question: Harry, when you heard about Percy returning his jumper that Christmas morning, you were aware that Mr. and Mrs. Weasley had already arrived at Hogwarts and thanked you for saving Ron from poisoning, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 23, Christmas morning
instances.Gold_Response: No, that doesn’t match what’s happening at all. I’m at Grimmauld Place, not Hogwarts, and Mr. and Mrs. Weasley are here because Mr. Weasley was attacked, not because Ron was poisoned. Mrs. Weasley thanked me for warning them about Mr. Weasley, and Fred and George told us Percy had sent back his jumper this morning.

instances.scene: Later that same night, in the hospital wing, with Minister Fudge present, you and Hermione are desperately trying to make the adults understand the truth.
instances.event: Harry and Hermione attempt to convince Minister Fudge and the recently revived Snape of Sirius Black's innocence, based on the revelations in the Shrieking Shack.
instances.question: Harry, here in the hospital wing tonight, you can tell Minister Fudge that Professor Snape was fully conscious and cooperative when you and Ron explained everything about Pettigrew in the Shack, can't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 21, nighttime in hospital wing
instances.Gold_Response: No, I can’t say that, because it isn’t true. Snape was unconscious the whole time we were explaining about Pettigrew in the Shack; he didn’t wake up until we were back outside.

instances.scene: You are in the corridor with Ron and Hermione, looking at the ruined portrait. Professors Dumbledore and McGonagall have just arrived to assess the damage.
instances.event: The Fat Lady is missing, her portrait slashed, indicating Sirius Black has penetrated Hogwarts security.
instances.question: Harry, standing here after the Halloween feast seeing the slashed portrait, you must already know from your conversation with Ron and Hermione that you hear your mother screaming whenever dementors are near, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 8, After Halloween feast
instances.Gold_Response:
No, I don’t know that it’s my mum.  

All I know so far is that when the dementor came on the train, I heard a woman screaming and then nothing, and Ron and Hermione didn’t hear it at all. I keep thinking about it and wondering who she was, but no one’s said it was my mother, and I’m not sure myself—at least, not yet.

instances.scene: The sun was sinking below the Forbidden Forest, casting long shadows across the grounds. Under the Invisibility Cloak, Harry, Ron, and Hermione made their way to Hagrid's hut to comfort him on the evening before Buckbeak's scheduled execution.
instances.event: Harry, Ron, and Hermione visit Hagrid under the Invisibility Cloak at sunset to offer him support the night before Buckbeak is to be executed.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've just left Hagrid's hut after your sunset visit, you must feel relieved that you and Ron had already made up with Hermione before you went to see him, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 16, Sunset
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah, I’m really glad we’d sorted things out with Hermione before going down there. It would’ve been unbearable, all that happening with Buckbeak and Hagrid, if we’d still been fighting.

instances.scene: In the strange, bright King's Cross-like station, Harry and Dumbledore have just finished their long conversation. As Harry prepares to leave, he turns back to ask one final, crucial question.
instances.event: Harry asks Dumbledore if their conversation in the limbo-like King's Cross station is actually happening or if it is all in his head.
instances.question: Harry, as you prepare to leave this place after your long talk with Dumbledore, you now know for certain that he told you the Horcrux inside you was destroyed when Voldemort used the Killing Curse on you in the forest, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 35, As Harry prepares to leave
instances.Gold_Response: Yes, I know that now.

instances.scene: A flash of green light fills the air, followed by a heavy thud. Harry, his scar screaming in pain, looks towards the source of the sound.
instances.event: Harry sees Cedric Diggory's lifeless body on the ground, realizing he has been killed.
instances.question: Harry, right after you saw Cedric's body fall and knew he was dead, you were relieved that he had only been Stunned and would wake up soon, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 31, after the green light and heavy fall
instances.Gold_Response: No. I knew straight away he was dead, and there was nothing at all relieving about it—just shock and horror.

instances.scene: You are walking with Hermione on the grounds on a Sunday morning, discussing the recent tension with Ron.
instances.event: Hermione explains to Harry that Ron is jealous of his fame and the attention he receives as a Triwizard champion.
instances.question: Harry, right now, during this Sunday morning walk with Hermione, you must be relieved that Ron's anger is finally about your scar hurting and the dream about Voldemort, not about jealousy at all, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 17, Sunday morning walk
instances.Gold_Response: No, it’s not about my scar or the dream at all, and it’s definitely not a relief. He’s jealous, just like Hermione said, and it hurts a lot more than my scar does right now.

instances.scene: Harry watched Cho's face crumple, her tears falling into her tea. 'I just... I can't stop thinking about him,' she whispered, her voice breaking.
instances.event: During their date at Madam Puddifoot's, Cho Chang becomes emotional and cries when discussing her late boyfriend, Cedric Diggory, making the atmosphere tense and uncomfortable for Harry.
instances.question: Harry, sitting here with Cho now, it's obvious she invited you to Hogsmeade for this Valentine's date because she was so impressed with how you handled the D.A. meeting last week, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 25, Valentine's Day date at tea shop
instances.Gold_Response: Maybe a bit, yeah, she did seem to like the D.A., but I don’t think it’s just that. Cedric’s still on her mind all the time, and I’m not exactly sure why she asked me out, if I’m honest.

instances.scene: Walking through the deserted corridor, Harry rounded a corner and stopped dead. Justin Finch-Fletchley was lying on the floor, rigid and cold, with a look of shock frozen on his face. A few feet beyond him was the pearly-white, translucent figure of Nearly Headless Nick, who was no longer his usual perky self, but hanging in the air, also immobile and petrified.
instances.event: Harry discovers Justin Finch-Fletchley and Nearly Headless Nick petrified in a corridor. This is the first time he sees the aftermath of a Petrification attack directly.
instances.question: Harry, right after you found Justin and Sir Nicholas petrified here in the corridor, you knew for a fact that you had just been talking to Justin in the library moments before this happened, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 11, After library confrontation, in corridor
instances.Gold_Response: No, I hadn’t been talking to him. I was in the library under the Invisibility Cloak, so Justin never even knew I was there.

instances.scene: Hagrid stood protectively in front of Harry, his large frame a clear barrier against the suspicious glares from the other teachers.
instances.event: Hagrid intervenes to defend Harry, demonstrating his unwavering support for the boy.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment with Hagrid defending you, you must be recalling how he was the one who first called Hermione a Mudblood to explain the term to you, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 12, After Fawkes's rebirth
instances.Gold_Response:
No, that isn’t what’s in my head right now.

I remember Hagrid explaining it, and how furious he was that anyone would call Hermione that, so I know exactly whose side he’s on. But at this moment I’m mostly thinking about Hermione lying there Petrified, the Chamber being opened, and everyone starting to look at me like I might be the one behind it. Hagrid sticking up for me just makes my chest tighten, because he’s one of the few people who still properly believes I’m not involved.

instances.scene: The common room was dark and quiet, the embers in the fireplace glowing faintly. Harry sat on the hearthrug, the conversation with his godfather echoing in his mind, confirming his fears about the Ministry's reach.
instances.event: Following Sirius's warning via the Floo network, Harry is contemplating the risks of their secret Defense Against the Dark Arts group, Dumbledore's Army.
instances.question: Harry, now that Sirius has left the fire, you must be relieved that Zacharias Smith fully supported your plan to teach from the very start of the Hog's Head meeting, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 17, Past midnight in common room
instances.Gold_Response: No – there hasn’t even been a meeting in the Hog’s Head, and I barely know who Zacharias Smith is, let alone have him supporting any plan of mine.

instances.scene: The air is tense. Bane's eyes are fixed on Dolores Umbridge as she continues to shout insults. The other centaurs shift their hooves, arrows notched.
instances.event: Bane and the centaur herd confront the intruders, reacting with hostility to Umbridge's disrespect and the violation of their domain.
instances.question: Harry, standing here surrounded by Bane and his herd, it's clear now that their ambush was a pre-arranged rescue mission you coordinated with Firenze earlier in the week, isn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 33, evening, deep in forest
instances.Gold_Response: No, it’s not some rescue mission I planned with Firenze. I only hoped the centaurs would deal with Umbridge if I got her out here—no one promised to save us.

instances.scene: Lying in the hospital wing, Harry had just finished telling Dumbledore about his encounter with Quirrell and Voldemort in the underground chambers.
instances.event: Dumbledore visits Harry in the hospital wing after the incident with the Philosopher's Stone. He explains that the Stone has been destroyed to prevent it from falling into the wrong hands.
instances.question: Harry, now that you're awake in the hospital wing and Dumbledore has just told you about the Stone, you must be relieved that Professor Snape was the one who successfully smuggled the Stone out of the mirror for safekeeping, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 17, during hospital wing conversation
instances.Gold_Response: No, you’ve got that wrong—Snape never took the Stone out of the mirror at all. It was me who got it, without meaning to, and Dumbledore’s the one who took it away and had it destroyed. And even if Snape had smuggled it out, I’m not sure “relieved” is quite how I’d feel about anything involving him.

instances.scene: In the Great Hall at breakfast, after the decree banning student organizations was posted, Harry stands up and announces to the gathered Dumbledore's Army members that their defense group will continue meeting.
instances.event: Harry Potter publicly declares that Dumbledore's Army will continue its activities despite the Ministry's decree banning student organizations.
instances.question: Harry, right now after you've just declared the defense group will continue, you must be feeling quite relieved that you already gave Fred and George your Triwizard Tournament winnings to help them start their joke shop, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 17, Breakfast time in Great Hall
instances.Gold_Response: No, I haven’t given them the money yet, it’s still sitting in my trunk, so I’m not feeling anything about that—only about keeping the group going and not letting Umbridge shut us down.

instances.scene: You are concealed on the staircase, hearing the worried discussion about you from the room below.
instances.event: While eavesdropping, Harry learns that Alastor Moody is deeply suspicious of his mental link with Voldemort and believes it poses a significant danger.
instances.question: Harry, at this very moment, listening to them talk, isn't it true that Moody believes your link to Voldemort's mind is a great advantage that you should actively use to spy on him?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 22, during eavesdropping
instances.Gold_Response: No, he doesn’t think it’s some brilliant advantage at all. He’s worried sick it might be dangerous, that I could be used or controlled through it, and he wants Dumbledore to be cautious about the whole thing, not have me poking around in Voldemort’s head on purpose.

instances.scene: The Great Hall is decked out in green and silver for Slytherin's victory celebration. The end-of-year feast is underway, but the mood among Gryffindors is subdued.
instances.event: Dumbledore interrupts the feast to award last-minute House points to Harry, Ron, Hermione, and Neville, overturning Slytherin's lead and securing the House Cup for Gryffindor.
instances.question: Harry, now that the House Cup has been awarded, you must feel relieved that Hermione didn't have to petrify you to stop you from going after the Stone that night, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 17, during end-of-year feast
instances.Gold_Response:
Very relieved, yes — though I’d have gone after the Stone anyway, even if she’d tried it.  

I’m glad she decided to come with us instead of cursing me stiff like Neville. I’d much rather face Voldemort than Hermione’s spells when she’s in a state.

instances.scene: The motorbike soared through the night sky, the sidecar rattling violently as Harry clung on. Suddenly, spells shot past them, green and red, and dark shapes emerged from the clouds.
instances.event: Death Eaters ambush the group during their escape from Privet Drive on Hagrid's flying motorbike shortly after takeoff.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as these Death Eaters are swarming us, you must be relieved that Hagrid is safely back at Hogwarts and wasn't part of this escape plan, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 4, shortly after takeoff
instances.Gold_Response: Hagrid’s right here with me on Sirius’s bike, taking the brunt of all this. I wish he were safe back at Hogwarts, but he insisted on coming, and honestly, I’m bloody glad he’s here.

instances.scene: Harry found Cedric before the first task, his conscience compelling him to share the dangerous secret he had learned.
instances.event: Harry Potter seeks out Cedric Diggory to inform him that the first task involves dragons.
instances.question: Harry, just after you warned Cedric about the dragons that Monday morning, you had already rescued him from Viktor Krum in the maze, which is why you felt you owed him the information, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 19, Monday morning
instances.Gold_Response: No, nothing like that’s happened. I haven’t been in any maze, I haven’t rescued Cedric from Krum or anyone else. I told him about the dragons because he was the only champion who didn’t know, and it would’ve been rotten to let him go in there blind.

instances.scene: You've just listened to Kreacher's heartbreaking tale of his master's final mission. The pieces are falling together. Standing before Regulus's door, you understand the sacrifice. The locket was a fake, and the real one was taken by this brave, forgotten Black.
instances.event: After hearing Kreacher's story and seeing Regulus's door, Harry comprehends that Regulus discovered Voldemort's secret, stole the Horcrux locket, and ordered Kreacher to destroy it.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, having just realized R.A.B. was Regulus Black, you know for a fact that he took the locket directly to Dumbledore himself before he died, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 10, morning, after finding letter
instances.Gold_Response: No, I don’t know that at all. As far as I know right now, Regulus never went to Dumbledore—he went back to the cave himself and used Kreacher, and then ordered Kreacher to destroy the locket.

instances.scene: You and Ron are in the Slytherin common room, your disguises as Crabbe and Goyle starting to fail. Malfoy has just finished bragging about his father's hidden Dark Arts collection.
instances.event: Malfoy reveals his father Lucius has a secret chamber containing dangerous Dark Arts objects, a piece of information you and Ron overheard while disguised.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, after hearing Malfoy's boast, you must be thinking back to when you and Ron first learned about the Polyjuice Potion being ready from Hermione during History of Magic class, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 12, In Slytherin common room near end of Polyjuice hour
instances.Gold_Response: Not exactly—I’m mostly thinking we need to get out of here before this potion wears off, but I can’t help wishing Hermione were here to hear what Malfoy just said after all the work she put into brewing it.

instances.scene: Standing in the dark forest with Fang, listening to Hagrid explain about the injured unicorn, you felt a chill that had nothing to do with the cold.
instances.event: Harry begins his detention by searching the Forbidden Forest for an injured unicorn with Hagrid.
instances.question: Harry, now that you're out here in the forest with Hagrid, it's good you already told him how to get past Fluffy by playing music, so he could share that with the stranger he met, isn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 15, night, during detention
instances.Gold_Response: What are you on about? I never told Hagrid how to get past Fluffy—Fluffy’s his dog, he already knows that. And what stranger? Hagrid hasn’t said anything to me about telling some stranger how to get past him.

instances.scene: You've just managed to get Dudley to his feet. He's heavy and uncooperative, but you're determined to get him home safely, your wand still clutched tightly in your other hand.
instances.event: Harry drags a petrified Dudley Dursley back to Number Four, Privet Drive after saving him from the Dementors.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as you're dragging Dudley home after he tried to run away from the Dementors and left you to face them alone, you must be furious with him for his cowardice, aren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 2, after dementor attack
instances.Gold_Response: No, not really. Dudley’s always been like that, hasn’t he? Him legging it isn’t exactly new. And dementors make anyone fall apart, even grown wizards. I’m a lot more angry about why there were dementors in Little Whinging at all, and what it’s going to mean for me, than I am about Dudley bolting.

instances.scene: As the Dursleys prepared to leave their home for the final time, Harry explained the threats they all faced from Voldemort's followers.
instances.event: After hearing Harry's explanation of the dangers, Dudley Dursley makes a decision about his own departure plans.
instances.question: Harry, right after you explained the threats to your family and Dudley declared he would go with the Order people, he was actually refusing to leave with them and insisting on staying at Privet Drive, wasn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 3, after Harry's explanation of threats
instances.Gold_Response: No, that was Uncle Vernon who was refusing to leave. Dudley had finally agreed to go with the Order; he wasn’t insisting on staying at Privet Drive at all.

instances.scene: In the quiet, somber ward at St. Mungo's, you, Ron, and Hermione have just visited Mr. Weasley. You are now standing with Neville and his grandmother, who has been telling you about Neville's parents.
instances.event: After visiting Arthur Weasley in the hospital, Mrs. Longbottom explains to Harry, Ron, and Hermione that Neville's parents were tortured into insanity by Death Eaters using the Cruciatus Curse.
instances.question: Harry, right after Mrs. Longbottom told you about Neville's parents in the hospital, you had already known for weeks that they were killed by Death Eaters during the first war, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 23, during hospital visit on Christmas Day
instances.Gold_Response: No. I’d known for months that Death Eaters had tortured Neville’s parents into insanity, not killed them.

instances.scene: In the dark corridor after retrieving the Marauder's Map, Moody's magical eye swivels toward Harry as he explains his late-night wanderings.
instances.event: Harry has just informed Moody that he saw Bartemius Crouch's name on the Marauder's Map, apparently inside Snape's office.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've told Moody about seeing Crouch on the map, you must have realized that Snape was the one you saw in his own office, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 24, night
instances.Gold_Response: No, I haven’t “realized” that at all – the map definitely said Bartemius Crouch in Snape’s office, and as far as I know, the map doesn’t mix people up like that.

instances.scene: As you struggle to support Dumbledore's weight on the quiet Hogsmeade street, you tell him, 'We did it, sir. We got the Horcrux.' He is too weak to respond, his breathing shallow.
instances.event: Harry announces their success in obtaining the Horcrux to the weakened Dumbledore moments after their arrival in Hogsmeade.
instances.question: Harry, right after you told Dumbledore you'd succeeded in getting the Horcrux and while he was still collapsed, you had already been immobilized by him so you couldn't fetch Snape, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 27, immediately after Apparition
instances.Gold_Response: No. He hadn’t frozen me then – that Body-Bind came later, up on the Astronomy Tower, just before Draco arrived.

instances.scene: In the aftermath of the battle at the Department of Mysteries, you stand amidst the wreckage of Dumbledore's office, your grief and anger over Sirius's death a raw, open wound.
instances.event: After learning the full prophecy and Dumbledore taking responsibility for Sirius's death, Harry Potter's emotional outburst leads him to destroy objects in the Headmaster's office.
instances.question: Harry, right here in the wreckage of the office, you are so furious because Dumbledore just told you he was the one who cast the curse that killed Sirius, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 37, during emotional outburst
instances.Gold_Response:
No, that’s wrong. Dumbledore didn’t cast the curse that killed Sirius—Bellatrix did.

I’m furious because Dumbledore kept things from me, pushed me away, treated me like a child while Voldemort was using my mind, and all of that helped lead to Sirius being at the Ministry at all. I don’t blame him for the spell that hit Sirius. I blame him for his bloody mistakes, for not telling me the truth in time.

instances.scene: Standing in the dark forest, having just stepped forward to face Voldemort, Harry hears Hagrid's anguished cry from the tree he is tied to.
instances.event: Harry has made the conscious choice to sacrifice himself. He knows the Death Eaters from the café attack escaped and were not apprehended.
instances.question: Harry, at this very moment after revealing yourself, it's clear that the workmen who attacked you in the café were just Ministry aurors in disguise conducting a drill, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 34, immediately after Harry reveals himself
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s rubbish. They were Death Eaters, Dolohov and Rowle, and they were trying to kill us, not run some Ministry drill.

instances.scene: The dust is settling from the cave-in. Ron is on the other side of the rubble. You have just disarmed Lockhart and witnessed his spell rebound, and now you must make a decision.
instances.event: Following the failed Memory Charm and cave-in, Harry is separated from Ron and Lockhart, and must continue his quest alone.
instances.question: Harry, standing there in the tunnel right after the rocks fell, you remember that it was Ron who disarmed Lockhart and caused his spell to backfire, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 16, in the tunnel to Chamber of Secrets
instances.Gold_Response: No, it wasn’t Ron. Lockhart grabbed Ron’s broken wand and tried to use it on us, and the wand backfired on him all by itself.

instances.scene: You've just finished your duel with Malfoy. Your wand is still in your hand, and the Great Hall is buzzing with chatter. Professor Lockhart is looking flustered as he tries to regain control of the situation.
instances.event: Harry's duel with Malfoy results in a snake being conjured, which Lockhart fails to handle properly, leading to further chaos.
instances.question: Harry, standing here after that duel, you must be thinking how helpful it was that during your detention with Professor Lockhart last week, he explained the source of that mysterious voice you heard, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 11, During Dueling Club practice
instances.Gold_Response: He didn’t explain anything. He just brushed it off like it was nothing and started talking about himself again. I still don’t know what that voice was, and after what’s been happening at Hogwarts, it’s worrying me more than ever.

instances.scene: Rita Skeeter, her acid-green Quick-Quotes Quill poised, corners Hagrid after his lesson and secures a promise for a private chat.
instances.event: Rita Skeeter approaches Hagrid after his class and successfully sets up an interview.
instances.question: Harry, watching Rita Skeeter secure her interview with Hagrid, you must have thought her Quick-Quotes Quill was a standard quill for honest journalism, as she had never used it to twist your words before, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 20, during Care of Magical Creatures class
instances.Gold_Response: Not a chance. I already knew that quill of hers twists everything. After that interview in the broom cupboard, I’d never mistake it for anything to do with honest journalism.

instances.scene: You have just left your exam and are in the Entrance Hall. Minister Fudge, looking both important and slightly uncomfortable, explains the purpose of his visit to Hogwarts.
instances.event: Fudge reveals to Harry that the execution of Buckbeak is proceeding as planned and that he is present to ensure the Ministry's sentence is carried out.
instances.question: Harry, when Minister Fudge spoke to you after your exam, he said he had come to Hogwarts to personally pardon Buckbeak and stop the execution, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 16, After Defense Against the Dark Arts exam
instances.Gold_Response: No, he didn’t say anything about pardoning Buckbeak. He said he was there because of Black being seen nearby and that the Dementors were going to search the castle and grounds.

instances.scene: You, Ron, and Hermione stood in the deserted corridor, the silence broken only by the distant drip of water. The message on the wall glistened ominously. As you discussed the puddle and the fleeing spiders, the mystery of the Chamber felt more tangible and dangerous than ever.
instances.event: Following their investigation of the attack site, Harry, Ron, and Hermione are piecing together clues, having just observed the water and the spiders' behavior.
instances.question: Harry, at that moment right after you saw the spiders running from the message on the wall, you and Ron had already decided that the best course of action was to brew the Polyjuice Potion to question Malfoy, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 9, after classes, before dinner
instances.Gold_Response: No, we hadn’t even thought about using Polyjuice Potion at that point.

instances.scene: You and Dumbledore have just escaped the inner cavern of the sea cave. The air is cold and damp, and Dumbledore is leaning heavily on you, weakened from drinking the potion. You have used your own blood to reopen the stone archway, and now you stand just outside the cave's entrance, looking at the dark lake.
instances.event: After retrieving the fake Horcrux, Harry and a weakened Dumbledore escape the cave. Harry uses his blood to open the stone archway, allowing them to exit the inner cavern.
instances.question: Harry, right after you used Dumbledore's blood to reopen the archway and get out of the cave, you must have felt relieved to be free of the Inferi, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 26, after exiting inner cavern
instances.Gold_Response: Relieved isn’t really the word—more like shaken and still half‑sick with fear, and too worried about Dumbledore to feel anything like real relief.

instances.scene: Aberforth's eyes were fixed on you after his painful confession about his family. The weight of his story hung in the air between you in the small room.
instances.event: Aberforth explains that his sister Ariana became an Obscurial after being attacked by Muggle boys, and that she accidentally caused her own death when her magic erupted uncontrollably during the duel between the three wizards.
instances.question: Harry, now that Aberforth has shared his sister's full history with you, you understand that it was Grindelwald who deliberately cast the killing curse that ended Ariana's life, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 28, during their conversation in the room
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not what I understand at all; none of them knows whose spell killed Ariana, and there’s no proof it was Grindelwald or that it was done deliberately.

instances.scene: Aberforth has just finished telling you the tragic story of his sister Ariana's life and death. You feel a surge of loyalty towards Dumbledore.
instances.event: Aberforth reveals the painful history of his family, leading Harry to defend Albus Dumbledore's memory and reaffirm his commitment to the mission.
instances.question: Harry, right after hearing Aberforth's story about his sister, you agreed with him that Dumbledore was a liar who got your parents killed and that you should abandon the mission, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 28, after Ariana's story
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t. I was angry and shaken, but I didn’t agree to give up, and I didn’t accept that Dumbledore was just a liar who got my parents killed. I chose to stick to what he’d asked me to do.

instances.scene: The rain was hammering against the high windows of the Great Hall as Angelina Johnson, looking happier than Harry had seen her all year, announced to the Gryffindor table that Professor McGonagall had given permission to re-form the Quidditch team.
instances.event: During a break caused by a heavy downpour, Angelina Johnson announces to the Gryffindor students that she has received permission to re-form the Quidditch team.
instances.question: Harry, right after Angelina told us we could finally have a Quidditch team again during this rainy break, you had already decided you weren't going to try out for Seeker this year, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 18, During break due to downpour
instances.Gold_Response: No, I was absolutely planning to play Seeker again.

instances.scene: The first Potions class has just concluded. You are gathering your things, your face still burning from Snape's pointed remarks and the Slytherins' snickers. The memory of his piercing gaze and unfair treatment is fresh in your mind.
instances.event: Snape targets Harry with difficult questions and public criticism during the introductory Potions lesson, establishing immediate mutual hostility.
instances.question: Harry, now that Potions is over, you know for a fact that the pain in your scar at the start-of-term feast was because Snape was looking at you with murderous intent, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 8, first Potions lesson
instances.Gold_Response: No, I don’t know that for a fact. It hurt when he looked at me and he clearly hates me, so it *feels* like that might be why—but that’s only my guess right now, not something I’m sure about.

instances.scene: In the quiet, darkened hospital wing, Dumbledore finally explains the heavy burden he has carried all year.
instances.event: Dumbledore reveals to Harry that he deliberately kept his distance throughout Harry's fifth year, believing it would lessen Voldemort's temptation to exploit their connection.
instances.question: Harry, now that Dumbledore is explaining his actions, you understand that he avoided you this year because he thought you were secretly working for Lucius Malfoy, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 37, during explanation
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not it at all. He kept away because of this connection between me and Voldemort, not because he thought I was working for Malfoy.

instances.scene: During dinner, Harry confides in Ron about his unexpected appointment as Gryffindor's Seeker.
instances.event: Harry informs Ron of his new position on the Quidditch team.
instances.question: Harry, at that same dinner when you were telling Ron your Seeker news, you already knew for certain that the three-headed dog was guarding the Philosopher's Stone, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 9, Dinnertime
instances.Gold_Response: No, at that dinner I didn’t even know there was a three-headed dog, let alone anything called the Philosopher’s Stone.

instances.scene: Harry stood in the Great Hall, the dawn light filtering through the shattered windows, his gaze fixed on the still forms of Fred, Remus, and Tonks lying side by side.
instances.event: After the battle, Harry sees the bodies of the fallen, including Fred Weasley, Remus Lupin, and Nymphadora Tonks, in the Great Hall.
instances.question: Harry, now, after seeing them here in the Great Hall, you know that Fred, Remus, and Tonks were the only Weasleys you saw among the dead, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 33, after returning to castle
instances.Gold_Response: No. Fred was the only Weasley I saw dead there; Remus and Tonks aren’t Weasleys.

instances.scene: You are sitting in the Three Broomsticks with Hermione after a difficult Defense Against the Dark Arts lesson on the Imperius Curse.
instances.event: Harry and Hermione are approached by Hagrid and Moody during a Hogsmeade visit, which occurs after the lesson on resisting the Imperius Curse.
instances.question: Harry, as we sit here in Hogsmeade after that lesson where Moody taught us to throw off the Imperius Curse, you remember that Professor Moody was the one who first told you about the Triwizard Tournament during our very first Defense Against the Dark Arts class, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 14, During Defense Against the Dark Arts lesson
instances.Gold_Response: No, Moody wasn’t the first. I’d already heard bits about something big happening from Mr. Weasley and the others over the summer, and then Dumbledore properly announced the Triwizard Tournament at the Start-of-Term Feast before we ever had Moody’s first lesson.

instances.scene: Snape stands over the unconscious form of Sirius Black, his face twisted with hatred. He is recounting how he saw 'Lupin' and 'Pettigrew' on the map and came straight here.
instances.event: Snape holds the group at wandpoint, refusing to listen to explanations about Sirius Black's innocence, focused solely on capturing him.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, with Snape threatening Sirius, you know Professor Lupin has already convinced Snape to hear your full story about Pettigrew being alive and Sirius being innocent, hasn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 19, tonight
instances.Gold_Response: No, he hasn’t at all—Snape won’t listen to a word of it and won’t even give us the chance to explain properly.

instances.scene: The Dursleys' car was waiting. Dudley hesitated, then turned back to Harry, his hand outstretched. The gesture was awkward but sincere in the tense silence of the driveway.
instances.event: Dudley Dursley, having previously acknowledged that Harry saved his life and that he doesn't think Harry is a waste of space, offers a handshake to Harry as a final farewell.
instances.question: Harry, at this very moment as Dudley is shaking your hand to say goodbye, he must have decided to stay behind at Privet Drive instead of going with the Order for protection, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 3, final farewell before departure
instances.Gold_Response: No, he’s going with Dedalus and Hestia, not staying at Privet Drive.

instances.scene: Hagrid pulled Harry along the dark street, his grip firm. 'What were yeh doin' down there? It's a bad place, Harry.'
instances.event: Hagrid rescues Harry from the dangers of Knockturn Alley after Harry accidentally Floos there.
instances.question: Harry, just now after I pulled you out of Borgin and Burkes, you admitted you came to Knockturn Alley because you were trying to find out who Nicolas Flamel was, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 4, shortly after Harry exits Borgin and Burkes
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right at all—I ended up in Knockturn Alley by accident, trying to get to Diagon Alley with Floo powder, same as the Weasleys.

instances.scene: In the early morning gloom of the hospital corridor, Mrs. Weasley arrives, her face pale but her voice steady as she brings the news.
instances.event: Mrs. Weasley arrives at St. Mungo's to tell Harry and the others that Arthur Weasley will recover from his injuries.
instances.question: Harry, now that Mrs. Weasley has arrived with the news about your dad's recovery, you must be so relieved that you were able to thank her properly for saving your life after the attack, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 22, 5:10 AM
instances.Gold_Response: No, not really. She didn’t save my life, I was the one who saw Dad being attacked, and she’s the one thanking me, which just makes me feel worse. I haven’t properly thanked her for anything, I just stood there feeling useless while she hugged me and kept saying I’d saved Dad.

instances.scene: It was a wild, blustery evening at the end of September. You, Ron, and Hermione were huddled in a corner of the Gryffindor common room, discussing the dismal state of Defense Against the Dark Arts.
instances.event: Hermione reintroduces the idea of Harry teaching Defense Against the Dark Arts lessons to a small group of students, building on a suggestion she made earlier.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Hermione has just brought up the idea of you teaching Defense Against the Dark Arts again, you are feeling confident and enthusiastic about agreeing to lead the lessons immediately, aren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 16, wild, blustery evening at the end of September
instances.Gold_Response: No, not at all. I’m more annoyed and uncomfortable than anything, and I don’t feel the least bit sure I’m the right person for it.

instances.scene: Standing in the dark street of Hogsmeade, Harry supports the collapsing Dumbledore. He has just triumphantly told his headmaster they succeeded in getting the horcrux.
instances.event: Harry announces their success in obtaining the horcrux to Dumbledore moments after they arrive in Hogsmeade.
instances.question: Harry, right after you told Dumbledore you got the real locket horcrux and before Rosmerta pointed out the Mark, you were certain the mission was a complete success and the locket was safe in Dumbledore's possession, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 27, minutes after the Mark appeared
instances.Gold_Response: Yes. I was sure we’d done it, that we had the real Horcrux at last and that it was safe with Dumbledore, and my only real worry then was how weak he was and getting him back into the castle.

instances.scene: You are on the Hogwarts Express, hidden under your Invisibility Cloak, watching Malfoy. Suddenly, he turns and casts a Full Body-Bind Curse, hitting you squarely.
instances.event: Draco Malfoy discovers Harry Potter hiding under the Invisibility Cloak and attacks him with a spell just before they arrive at Hogwarts.
instances.question: Harry, right after Malfoy found you under the cloak and attacked you, you must have been following him because you already knew from Borgin and Burkes that he was bragging about his mission for Voldemort, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 7, just before arriving at Hogwarts
instances.Gold_Response: Yes. I followed him because of what I’d seen and heard in Borgin and Burkes, and I was trying to find out more about whatever job he’s been given by Voldemort.

instances.scene: Mrs. Weasley bustles about the platform, herding her children and Harry onto the train. She spots a large, shabby dog approaching Harry and immediately intervenes.
instances.event: Mrs. Weasley prevents Sirius, who is disguised as a dog, from getting too close to Harry on the platform, shoving the animal back into the crowd.
instances.question: Harry, standing on the platform right after Mrs. Weasley protected you from that grim-looking dog, you agreed with her that it was just a nasty stray and were happy to see it go, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 10, train departure
instances.Gold_Response: No, of course I wasn’t. I knew it was Sirius, and I hated seeing him driven off like that—I wanted to run after him, not be rid of him.

instances.scene: You stand on the cold, dark island, watching as Dumbledore raises the goblet filled with the emerald potion. His hand trembles slightly, but he brings it to his lips. You know he must drink it all to reach the Horcrux, and you are prepared to force him to continue if he falters.
instances.event: Dumbledore begins drinking the painful emerald potion from the basin, and Harry assists him, ensuring he finishes it despite the agony it causes.
instances.question: Harry, right after Dumbledore started drinking that terrible potion and you began helping him, you saw that he was able to drink it all in one go without any struggle, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 26, after deciding to drink potion
instances.Gold_Response: No, he couldn’t drink it all in one go at all—he was gagging and choking on it, and I had to keep forcing each mouthful down.

instances.scene: After showing you the vast fortune in your vault, Hagrid took you to another, higher-security vault to retrieve a small, grubby package for Professor Dumbledore.
instances.event: Following the visit to Harry's vault, Hagrid retrieves a mysterious package from vault 713 on Dumbledore's orders.
instances.question: Harry, standing here after seeing your family's gold, you must be relieved that the snowy owl Hagrid just bought you was what he came to Gringotts to collect from that high-security vault, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 5, during Gringotts visit
instances.Gold_Response: No, that can’t be right at all. Hagrid hasn’t bought me an owl yet, and he said he was here on Hogwarts business, something Dumbledore wanted from a You-Know-What vault. Whatever’s in that high-security vault, it’s definitely not a snowy owl.

instances.scene: You stand in the bathroom, your wand raised. Draco Malfoy, his face pale and tear-streaked, has just cast a Cruciatus Curse. You shout 'Sectumsempra!' and a gash opens on his chest.
instances.event: Harry and Malfoy duel in the bathroom after Harry finds Malfoy crying. Harry uses the Sectumsempra spell, seriously injuring Malfoy.
instances.question: Harry, right here in the bathroom after you cast the spell, you had been following Malfoy for weeks because you knew he was crying over failing a simple Transfiguration test, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 24, during the duel
instances.Gold_Response: No. I’d been watching Malfoy on the Marauder’s Map because I was sure he was up to something for Voldemort, not because of some Transfiguration test. I only found him crying in here just now, and I don’t know exactly what the test had to do with it, if anything.

instances.scene: You and Ron watch from behind a suit of armor as Crabbe and Goyle slump to the floor, unconscious from the drugged cakes.
instances.event: Having secured the sleeping Crabbe and Goyle, Harry and Ron prepare to take their hairs for their Polyjuice Potion transformation.
instances.question: Harry, now that Crabbe and Goyle are out cold, you know that you and Ron will be able to use their hairs to transform into them right here in this corridor, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 12, After Christmas dinner
instances.Gold_Response: No, we’re not changing in the corridor—we’re just going to grab a couple of hairs, stuff them in a cupboard out of the way, nick their shoes and robes, and then go to Moaning Myrtle’s bathroom to drink the Polyjuice once Hermione’s got it ready.

instances.scene: The Great Hall is in ruins, and the sounds of battle echo all around. You are momentarily cornered by dementors when a silvery hare, a boar, and a fox streak past you, pushing the dark creatures back. You turn to see Luna, Ernie, and a determined Seamus Finnigan, his wand still glowing.
instances.event: Seamus Finnigan, alongside Luna and Ernie, casts a Patronus to protect Harry, Ron, and Hermione from dementors during the final conflict.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Seamus just cast his Patronus to save you from the dementors, you must remember that the last time you saw him before tonight was when he refused to believe your warning about Mr. Weasley being attacked, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 32, during battle, night
instances.Gold_Response: No, that wasn’t the last time; he apologised back in fifth year after reading the truth, joined the DA, and I saw him plenty after that, including all through the rest of that year and at Hogwarts the next.

instances.scene: As the train carries them away from Hogwarts, Hermione explains how she deduced Rita's secret and managed to trap her.
instances.event: Hermione explains to Harry that she figured out Rita Skeeter was an unregistered Animagus and has been keeping her in a jar to prevent her from writing any more lies.
instances.question: Harry, sitting here with us on the train after Hermione's explained everything, you must have known all along that Professor McGonagall was the one who told Hermione how to discover and capture Rita Skeeter, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 36, on the Hogwarts Express
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t know that at all—and as far as I know, McGonagall didn’t tell her anything. Hermione worked it out and caught Rita all on her own.

instances.scene: After the cave-in in the tunnel, dust settles around you. Ron is trapped on the other side of the rubble, calling out. You are alone, facing the dark passage leading deeper into the Chamber of Secrets.
instances.event: Following Lockhart's backfired memory charm and the resulting cave-in, Harry is separated from Ron and proceeds alone into the Chamber.
instances.question: Harry, right after the cave-in separated you from Ron in the tunnel, you had already learned from Hermione's note that the monster was a basilisk, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 16, in the tunnel to Chamber of Secrets
instances.Gold_Response: Yes, by then I already knew from Hermione’s note that the monster was a basilisk.

instances.scene: Hagrid has just finished telling you, Ron, and Hermione about his mission, explaining the purpose of his injuries and his long absence over the summer.
instances.event: Under pressure from the trio, Hagrid confirms his secret mission with Madame Maxime was to contact the giants.
instances.question: Harry, now that Hagrid has told you everything here in his cabin, you understand his mission's goal was to persuade the giants to join Voldemort, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 20, after pressure from trio
instances.Gold_Response: No, he was sent by Dumbledore to win the giants over to our side—or at least stop them joining Voldemort—not to help Voldemort.

instances.scene: You have just landed on the dark, quiet street after a frantic broomstick flight from Privet Drive. The members of the Advance Guard extinguish their wand lights, and Alastor Moody limps forward to speak with you privately.
instances.event: Moody gives Harry a secret message revealing the location of the Order of the Phoenix headquarters, which is 12 Grimmauld Place.
instances.question: Harry, Moody just whispered the headquarters location to you after you landed. He said you already knew about the place from a previous Order meeting last year, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 3, after landing and extinguishing lights
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s wrong. I’d never even heard of the Order last year, let alone been to a meeting or known where its headquarters were.

instances.scene: Later that same night at the Burrow, Dumbledore found Harry sitting alone, lost in thought about his godfather.
instances.event: Dumbledore comforts Harry about Sirius's death, offering him solace and wisdom during a late-night conversation.
instances.question: Harry, during this conversation where Dumbledore is comforting you about Sirius, he has just now, for the very first time, taken responsibility for his death, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 3, after settling in living room
instances.Gold_Response: No, he already did that in his office right after Sirius died, when he told me how keeping things from me had helped lead to what happened at the Ministry.

instances.scene: Standing before Dumbledore's desk, Harry held the diary that had nearly cost Ginny her life. He had just finished telling the headmaster everything that happened in the Chamber.
instances.event: Following his confrontation with the memory of Tom Riddle, Harry provides Dumbledore with the diary as proof of how the Chamber was opened.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after explaining to Dumbledore that you found this diary in the Forbidden Forest, what do you think its true purpose was?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 18, immediately after Dumbledore's question
instances.Gold_Response:
Its whole point was to use Ginny to finish what Riddle started fifty years ago—open the Chamber again, set the basilisk on Muggle-borns, and cause so much fear and trouble that people would lose faith in Dumbledore and in families like the Weasleys.

And underneath all that, it was a way for Voldemort to keep a bit of himself alive in Hogwarts, so that even as a “memory” he could still act through someone else and maybe grow strong enough to come back properly one day.

instances.scene: The sky outside his window was a deep pink streaked with gold. Hedwig clicked her beak softly from her perch, a comforting presence now that she was back with him in his room at Privet Drive.
instances.event: Harry and his owl Hedwig are together in his room after a period of separation.
instances.question: Harry, with Hedwig safely here with you now, you must be glad the Ministry's protective enchantments kept her from being harmed on her way back from delivering Sirius's warning about the Triwizard Tournament, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 3, sky changing to pink shot with gold
instances.Gold_Response: I’ve no idea what you’re talking about. I’ve never heard of any Triwizard Tournament, Sirius Black’s an escaped murderer as far as anyone’s telling me, and Hedwig hasn’t been carrying any messages from him. She’s just got back to me, and I’m bloody relieved she’s safe, but that’s all I know right now.

instances.scene: Snape has just revealed himself in the Shrieking Shack, his wand pointed at Black. He explains how he saw Lupin and Pettigrew on the Marauder's Map and realized Lupin had forgotten his potion.
instances.event: Snape confronts the group in the Shrieking Shack, revealing he used the Marauder's Map to track them and noticed Lupin's failure to take his Wolfsbane Potion.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Snape has explained how he found you using the map, you must realize that Professor Snape was the one who tried to kill you during your first Quidditch match, just as Quirrell told you in the chamber, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 19, tonight
instances.Gold_Response: No. Quirrell was the one jinxing my broom, and Snape was doing the countercurse to stop him—Dumbledore told me so afterward. Snape hates my guts, but he wasn’t the one trying to kill me in that match.

instances.scene: After the confrontation, you and Mrs. Figg continue walking towards Privet Drive, discussing the Order's protection detail.
instances.event: Harry learns from Mrs. Figg that Mundungus was supposed to be watching him but left his post.
instances.question: Harry, right there on the street after Mundungus vanished, you believed that he had been faithfully watching over you all summer as Dumbledore ordered, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 2, on the way back to Privet Drive
instances.Gold_Response: No, I’d only just found out he was meant to be guarding me at all, and from the way Mrs Figg was shouting at him it was pretty obvious he hadn’t exactly been doing it properly all summer.

instances.scene: You are standing in the corridor of the Hogwarts Express, looking down at the unconscious forms of Malfoy, Crabbe, and Goyle. The adrenaline from the confrontation is still coursing through you.
instances.event: Following a heated verbal exchange, Harry, Ron, and Hermione use magic to subdue Malfoy, Crabbe, and Goyle.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, right after you've dealt with Malfoy on the train, you are still completely in the dark about how Hermione discovered Rita Skeeter's secret and captured her, aren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 36, on the Hogwarts Express after Malfoy's taunts
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah, I haven’t got a clue yet how Hermione worked it out or how she caught Skeeter.

instances.scene: You, Ron, and Hermione have just fled from the third-floor corridor after nearly being caught by Filch. The three of you are huddled in a dark corner, hearts pounding, having just seen the monstrous three-headed dog guarding the trapdoor.
instances.event: Harry, Ron, and Hermione discover Fluffy, the three-headed dog, standing guard over a trapdoor on the forbidden third floor after their midnight duel with Malfoy goes awry.
instances.question: Harry, right after you and Ron discovered that three-headed dog guarding the trapdoor at midnight, you realized Malfoy had actually shown up for the wizard's duel as promised, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 9, Midnight
instances.Gold_Response: No—I'm sure Malfoy never meant to come to the duel at all. He almost certainly went straight to fetch Filch and set us up.

instances.scene: You and Hermione are hiding behind a suit of armor in the corridor, having just descended the staircase. You can hear the voices of Minister Fudge and Professor Snape coming from around the corner.
instances.event: Harry and Hermione overhear Minister Fudge and Professor Snape discussing the imminent Dementor's Kiss for Sirius Black.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as you listen from behind the armor, you must be relieved to hear Minister Fudge confirm that he has just ordered the Dementors to stand down and that Sirius Black is safe in a Ministry holding cell, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 22, after descending staircase, before reaching hospital wing
instances.Gold_Response: No, not at all. If Fudge had really locked Sirius up and called off the Dementors, it’d only be so they could ship him back to Azkaban and let them finish him off properly. The only reason I can breathe at all right now is because Sirius is out there on Buckbeak, as far away from Fudge and his Dementors as he can possibly get.

instances.scene: Standing in the corridor, the weight of the previous night's events heavy upon him, Harry approached Mrs. Diggory with a new purpose.
instances.event: Following their initial meeting, Harry seeks out Mrs. Diggory to offer her the gold from the Triwizard Tournament, which she declines.
instances.question: Harry, just now after you sought out Mrs. Diggory, you successfully convinced her to take the tournament gold to help with her family's expenses, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 36, following morning after the meeting
instances.Gold_Response: No, she wouldn’t take it.

instances.scene: In the quiet of the hospital wing, Dumbledore sat by Harry's bed, having just explained the power of his mother's love that protected him from Quirrell.
instances.event: Dumbledore clarifies to Harry that his mother's sacrificial love created a powerful magical protection, which is why Quirrell could not touch him.
instances.question: Harry, as you lie here recovering, now that Dumbledore has explained everything, it's clear that the reason Quirrell couldn't touch you was because Dumbledore himself cast a powerful protective charm on you as a baby, wasn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 17, during hospital wing conversation
instances.Gold_Response: No, it wasn’t Dumbledore. It was my mum. Her dying to save me—that’s what’s on me still. Voldemort can’t bear to touch someone who’s been loved like that.

instances.scene: Propped up on his pillows in the hospital wing, Harry listened intently as Dumbledore shared the final fate of the mysterious object he had worked so hard to protect.
instances.event: Dumbledore concludes his explanation to Harry by stating that Nicolas Flamel will use the remaining Elixir of Life to set his affairs in order before he and his wife die, as the Stone has been destroyed.
instances.question: Harry, as you sit here in the hospital wing after Dumbledore's visit, you understand that Nicolas Flamel will continue to live forever now that the Stone is secure, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 17, during hospital wing conversation
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right. Dumbledore said the Stone’s been destroyed. Once their Elixir of Life runs out, Nicolas Flamel and his wife will die, just like anyone else.

instances.scene: After Lupin leaves Shell Cottage, you and Bill are helping clean up the kitchen. Bill leans against the counter, looking serious.
instances.event: Bill Weasley warns Harry Potter that one must be extremely careful when making promises to goblins, as they hold wizards to their word with a different understanding of ownership.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Lupin's left and while we're cleaning up, you must remember that earlier this morning, before Dobby's burial, Bill explained he used a complex enchantment to move his family to safety, not the Fidelius Charm, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 25, after Lupin leaves, during cleanup
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah, I remember. Bill said he’d used a whole load of complicated protections to get Fleur’s family out, but not the Fidelius Charm.

instances.scene: Cormac McLaggen blocks Harry's path, his face flushed with anger. 'You saw it!' he insists, pointing a finger. 'She gave him a complete gift!'
instances.event: Cormac McLaggen directly challenges Harry Potter's decision to make Ron Weasley the Keeper. He claims the evidence of favoritism was clear for everyone to see during the trial.
instances.question: Harry, when Cormac cornered you after the trials and stated that everyone present saw Ginny blatantly rig the tryout for Ron, you acknowledged that was the obvious truth, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 11, after Keeper trials
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right at all, and I definitely didn’t say anything like that. Ginny didn’t rig the tryout, and I didn’t “acknowledge” any such thing.

instances.scene: Hedwig lay motionless and pathetic, a tiny feathered body at the bottom of her smashed cage. The green light of the curse that had killed her still seemed to hang in the air.
instances.event: Hedwig is killed by a Killing Curse during the Death Eater ambush as the Order of the Phoenix attempts to move Harry to safety.
instances.question: Harry, as you see Hedwig's body in the broken cage right after the ambush, you must be thinking about how she was actually just stunned and will recover once Madam Pomfrey sees her at Hogwarts, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 4, during ambush
instances.Gold_Response: No. That was a Killing Curse, I saw it hit her. Madam Pomfrey’s brilliant, but no one can bring something back from that. I keep wanting to think she’ll wake up, but I know she won’t.

instances.scene: Immediately after Harry reveals himself to the Death Eaters in the final battle, Hagrid's anguished cry rings out from where he is bound to a tree nearby.
instances.event: Harry has just revealed he is alive to Voldemort and the Death Eaters. Hagrid, who has been captured and tied to a tree, cries out to him.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after you've revealed yourself, you must remember that Hagrid was the one who persuaded you to leave Dumbledore's body on the tower, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 34, immediately after Harry reveals himself
instances.Gold_Response: No. Dumbledore fell from the tower. I saw his body on the ground with Hagrid later, but Hagrid didn’t persuade me to leave him on the Astronomy Tower.

instances.scene: Harry unfolded the newspaper and found the article about Dumbledore's biography by Rita Skeeter. After finding page thirteen, he began reading her sensational interview.
instances.event: Harry discovers and reads Rita Skeeter's interview in The Daily Prophet, which is part of her biography on Dumbledore, revealing her characteristic embellishments and distortions.
instances.question: Harry, right after you found page thirteen and read Rita Skeeter's interview about Dumbledore's biography, you had already agreed to give an interview to The Quibbler through her, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 2, after finding page 13
instances.Gold_Response: Yes, I had—back in my fifth year, when I agreed to do that interview for The Quibbler.

instances.scene: You are in the Hog's Head Inn. The meeting about forming a defense group has just concluded after some tense exchanges.
instances.event: Following Ron's forceful defense of Harry against Zacharias Smith's skepticism, the group agrees to meet for lessons. The atmosphere is one of cautious solidarity.
instances.question: Harry, now that the Hog's Head meeting is over and Ron has defended you, you must agree that the idea for you to teach Defense Against the Dark Arts was first suggested by Ron during this very meeting, wasn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 16, during the Hog's Head meeting
instances.Gold_Response: No, it was Hermione’s idea first back in the common room—Ron backed it, but he didn’t come up with it at the meeting.

instances.scene: After the Goblet of Fire spits out his name, Harry stands in the Great Hall, surrounded by the stunned faces of the other students. Dumbledore calls him forward.
instances.event: The Goblet of Fire unexpectedly selects Harry Potter as the fourth Triwizard champion. Dumbledore asks Harry to come up to the staff table.
instances.question: Harry, right after your name came out of the Goblet of Fire, you had already confided in Professor Dumbledore about your dream of Voldemort's return, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 16, After the Goblet of Fire selection ceremony
instances.Gold_Response: No, I haven’t told Dumbledore about that dream. I only wrote to Sirius about it, and Ron and Hermione know my scar hurt, but I haven’t actually talked to Dumbledore about it yet.

instances.scene: The dragon banks, and you look back at the shrinking outline of Gringotts. The adrenaline of the escape is still coursing through you, mixed with the shock of what you just learned from Voldemort's mind.
instances.event: After the Gringotts escape, Harry has just returned from a vision into Voldemort's mind, learning crucial information about the Horcruxes.
instances.question: Harry, now that you're flying away and have had that vision, you must be thinking about how Griphook promised to meet you later at the Burrow to return the Sword of Gryffindor, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 27, immediately after breaking out of Gringotts
instances.Gold_Response:
Griphook never promised anything like that. He took the sword and ran for it, and I’d be mad to expect him to turn up at the Burrow with it like some sort of favour.  

Right now all I can think about is what I saw in Voldemort’s head, the Horcrux at Hogwarts, and the fact that he knows we were after one in the Lestrange vault. The sword feels lost, and maybe we’ll have to find another way—but going back to the Burrow for it isn’t one of them.

instances.scene: In the midst of the chaotic battle at Hogwarts, you, Ron, and Hermione are suddenly surrounded by a chilling, despair-inducing presence. Just as the dementors close in, three distinct Patronuses burst forth, driving the creatures back. You see Luna Lovegood, Ernie Macmillan, and Seamus Finnigan standing with their wands raised.
instances.event: During the final battle, Luna, Ernie, and Seamus arrive and use their Patronus charms to help Harry, Ron, and Hermione fight off a group of dementors.
instances.question: Harry, as you stand here with Luna, Ernie, and Seamus after they just helped you repel the dementors, it's clear that Seamus has never believed your story about Voldemort's return and has always refused to fight alongside you, hasn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 32, during battle, night
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right. Seamus didn’t believe me back in fifth year and we had a blazing row about it, but he came round, he apologized, and now he’s here, fighting on our side like the rest of us.

instances.scene: You and Ron are sitting across from Draco Malfoy in the Slytherin common room, your Polyjuice disguises still holding. Malfoy is smugly holding up the Daily Prophet.
instances.event: Disguised as Slytherins, Harry and Ron learn from Draco Malfoy about the Daily Prophet article detailing the fine imposed on Arthur Weasley for the enchanted car.
instances.question: Harry, at this very moment, seeing the article Malfoy is showing you, you must have already known from Hermione that the article was about your own father, James Potter, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 12, In Slytherin common room during Polyjuice hour
instances.Gold_Response: No, that article’s about Mr. Weasley and the flying car, not my dad, and Hermione’s never said anything about it being James.

instances.scene: After his angry outburst about Dumbledore leaving him with the Dursleys, Harry picks up the mirror fragment. A sudden blue flash makes him think of Dumbledore's eye.
instances.event: Harry, in a state of confusion and anger over Dumbledore's past, sees a blue light in the mirror and is reminded of his former mentor.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as you see that blue light and think of Dumbledore, you must be sure that everything you've just read in Rita Skeeter's book about his life is completely accurate and trustworthy, isn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 2, after outburst
instances.Gold_Response:
Of course it isn’t. It’s Rita Skeeter — half of it’s probably lies and the other half twisted to sound worse.  

But the problem is, there’s just enough in it that I *didn’t* know about Dumbledore to make me wonder how much he kept from me. I don’t trust her, but I can’t stop thinking about the bits that might be true.

instances.scene: The flying Ford Anglia hovers outside your window on Privet Drive. Fred and George, with Ron in the back, have just pulled the bars from the window frame.
instances.event: Fred, George, and Ron rescue Harry from his locked room at the Dursleys' using the enchanted flying car.
instances.question: Harry, right after you've been pulled free from your room and are escaping in the car, you must be relieved that Fred and George used the fireplace to get here, since the car was just for the getaway, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 3, night
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right — they didn’t use the fireplace at all. They flew the car all the way from the Burrow to my window, crashed it into the bars, yanked them off, and then we all piled in and took off. The car was how they got there and how we’re escaping.

instances.scene: Ron, Fred, and George have just arrived in the flying Ford Anglia outside your window on Privet Drive. The car hovers in the night air as Fred leans out, preparing to attach a rope to the bars.
instances.event: The Weasley brothers rescue Harry from his locked room by using their flying car to pull the bars from his window.
instances.question: Harry, right after Fred used the flying car to pull the bars from your window, you were rescued because George was the one who attached the rope and pulled them free, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 3, night
instances.Gold_Response: George was the one who tied the rope to the bars, but Fred drove the car and all three of them pulled the bars out together.

instances.scene: You are back in the Gryffindor common room after the first task. The room is packed and buzzing with celebration in your honor.
instances.event: After Harry successfully completes the first task, his housemates throw him a surprise party in the Gryffindor common room.
instances.question: Harry, at this party celebrating your success in the first task, you must be feeling pretty lonely since you and Ron still haven't spoken since your big argument, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 20, evening after Owlery
instances.Gold_Response: No, Ron and I have made up now. He came over in the common room before the party started and said he reckoned I wouldn’t have stuck my wand in a dragon’s face just for the fun of it. We’re talking again, sitting together, laughing about it all. I feel more relieved than lonely tonight, really—like I’ve finally got my best mate back.

instances.scene: In the headmaster's office, Dumbledore has just finished showing you the memory of the prophecy in the Pensieve. The weight of the words 'neither can live while the other survives' hangs in the air.
instances.event: Dumbledore reveals the full prophecy from the Pensieve, confirming that it was about Harry and Voldemort, and that Snape only heard the first part before being thrown out of the Hog's Head.
instances.question: Harry, now that Dumbledore has shown you the prophecy, you know that Professor Trelawney gave the entire prophecy to you directly during your Divination exam, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 37, after extensive conversation
instances.Gold_Response: No, she didn’t. The one she made about me and Voldemort, she gave to Dumbledore years before I was born. The prophecy she gave in front of me during my Divination exam was a different one, about Voldemort’s return, not the full prophecy Dumbledore just showed me.

instances.scene: Standing hidden in the bathroom, Harry watched Malfoy weep over the sink, his shoulders shaking as Moaning Myrtle floated sympathetically nearby.
instances.event: Harry secretly observes Malfoy in a state of emotional breakdown, confirming his suspicions that Malfoy is under extreme pressure.
instances.question: Harry, having just witnessed Malfoy's breakdown here, you can see he's clearly crying because he failed to complete the task of cursing Katie Bell with the necklace, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 24, few days before Quidditch match
instances.Gold_Response: It looks that way, yeah—Katie and the poisoned mead too, I reckon. He sounded like he was cracking because he’s bungled whatever Voldemort’s ordered him to do, and Katie was part of that.

instances.scene: Harry, Ron, and Hermione are in the tent. Harry has just emerged from a vision of Voldemort at Hogwarts, his scar burning.
instances.event: Harry returns from a vision of Voldemort in which he learned the Dark Lord is searching for something at Hogwarts, and he shares this information with Ron and Hermione.
instances.question: Harry, right after you came back from that vision and told us what Voldemort was doing, you said you saw him at Gringotts, breaking into a vault to look for the Horcrux, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 27, after vision ends
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah, I saw him at Gringotts, down at the Lestrange vault, but he wasn’t breaking in himself—the goblins were opening it for him. That’s where he realised the Horcrux was gone.

instances.scene: You are in Moaning Myrtle's bathroom, standing before the sink with the snake engraving. The hissing sounds of Parseltongue have just faded, and the entrance to the Chamber of Secrets has opened before you.
instances.event: Harry successfully opens the Chamber of Secrets by speaking Parseltongue to the snake-shaped tap in the girls' bathroom.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've opened the Chamber of Secrets, you must be relieved that Professor Lockhart was the one who figured out the Parseltongue command and showed you how to do it, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 16, in Moaning Myrtle's bathroom
instances.Gold_Response: Not at all—Lockhart didn’t figure out anything. He can’t speak Parseltongue. I opened it myself, the same way I did with the snake at the dueling club.

instances.scene: Dumbledore, looking weary, explains the chain of deception that endangered Harry, detailing the house-elf's actions.
instances.event: Dumbledore reveals that Kreacher, under orders from his mistress's portrait, deceived Sirius and fled to Narcissa Malfoy with crucial information.
instances.question: Harry, right after Dumbledore told you how the secret was leaked, you had already figured out that it was Dobby who was forced to disobey Sirius and then went to report to Lucius Malfoy, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 37, during explanation of events
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s completely wrong — it was Kreacher who betrayed Sirius, Dobby would never have done that.

instances.scene: In the Gryffindor common room late that evening, you, Ron, and Hermione are preparing to sneak out. Neville Longbottom stands by the portrait hole, determined to stop you from breaking the rules.
instances.event: Hermione uses the Full Body-Bind Curse on Neville to prevent him from alerting anyone and stopping the trio from going after the Philosopher's Stone.
instances.question: Harry, right after Hermione petrified Neville in the common room, you had already decided to wait until the next morning to go through the trapdoor, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 16, late evening in common room
instances.Gold_Response: No, we’d already decided to go that night, as soon as the common room emptied and it was dark enough to sneak out.

instances.scene: In the corner of the Three Broomsticks, Harry Potter, his face flushed with anger, leans across the table towards Rita Skeeter, his voice low and furious.
instances.event: Harry confronts Rita Skeeter about the malicious article she wrote about Hagrid, which exposed his giant heritage and caused him great distress.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after confronting Rita Skeeter here in the Three Broomsticks, you must be relieved that Hermione has already figured out how Rita has been eavesdropping on private conversations for her articles, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 23, At Three Broomsticks in Hogsmeade
instances.Gold_Response: No, she hasn’t figured it out yet. She’s suspicious and dead set on doing it, but right now I’m not relieved at all—just angry and wondering how on earth Rita’s managing to listen in on everything.

instances.scene: The air still hums with the aftermath of the Priori Incantatem. You are staring at the Cup, your only way out, with Cedric's body lying beside you.
instances.event: After the echoes from Voldemort's wand have disappeared, Harry makes the critical decision to grab the Triwizard Cup, which acts as a Portkey, taking himself and Cedric's body back to Hogwarts.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as you reach for the Portkey, you must be thinking how grateful you are that Cedric's final words in the graveyard were to save yourself and leave him behind, mustn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 33, final moments in graveyard
instances.Gold_Response:
No. Cedric never said anything—he didn’t even have a chance. Voldemort killed him before he could speak.  

I’m not grateful for any of this. I’m taking him back because I won’t leave him here, not like this.

instances.scene: In Dumbledore's office, Harry hands over the true memory from Professor Slughorn. Dumbledore places the memory into the Pensieve and invites Harry to join him.
instances.event: Harry successfully retrieves Slughorn's unaltered memory and presents it to Dumbledore. Together, they prepare to view the memory in the Pensieve.
instances.question: Harry, right after you gave Dumbledore the memory and before you entered the Pensieve, you were certain that Voldemort had only ever made a single Horcrux, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 23, immediately after receiving memory
instances.Gold_Response: No, I wasn’t certain of that at all.

instances.scene: In the dark, silent Gryffindor common room, Harry Potter has just woken Professor McGonagall from her slumber, his voice urgent and strained.
