instances.event: Harry wakes Professor McGonagall in the middle of the night to tell her about his vision of Mr. Weasley being attacked by a snake.
instances.question: Harry, right after you woke Professor McGonagall, you told her that you had this vision of Mr. Weasley's attack because you were feeling guilty about the Quidditch match earlier, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 22, late night/early morning
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t say it was because I felt guilty about the Quidditch match. I told her I’d seen it happen from inside the snake, and that it was real, not just a dream.

instances.scene: Harry and Dumbledore converse in the serene, white limbo. Dumbledore, with great clarity, outlines the precise magical mechanisms that allowed Harry to survive and Voldemort to be defeated.
instances.event: Dumbledore clarifies that the protection in Harry's blood, provided by his mother's sacrifice and now anchored in Voldemort, is what tethered Harry to life.
instances.question: Harry, as Dumbledore is explaining how you survived, you understand that the reason you could return was because the Horcrux in you absorbed the Killing Curse, leaving your own soul intact, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 35, During their conversation
instances.Gold_Response: Not exactly. Voldemort taking my blood kept me tethered to life in his body, so when he cursed me he only destroyed the bit of his soul inside me, not mine, and that’s why I had the chance to come back.

instances.scene: You and Ron have just disarmed Gilderoy Lockhart in his office. He had been trying to erase your memories with his wand, but you managed to get the drop on him.
instances.event: Harry and Ron confront Lockhart as he tries to flee Hogwarts. When Lockhart attempts to use a Memory Charm on them, Harry disarms him.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've got Lockhart's wand, you must be relieved that he only tried to use a simple Stunning Spell on you and Ron, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 16, evening in Lockhart's office
instances.Gold_Response: No, that wasn’t a Stunning Spell he was going to use—it was a Memory Charm, and there’s nothing relieving about knowing he was perfectly happy to wipe our minds just to save his own skin.

instances.scene: Amidst the emotional turmoil in the headmaster's office, Dumbledore calmly accepts full blame for the events that led to Sirius Black's death.
instances.event: Dumbledore explicitly states that the responsibility for Sirius's death lies with him, not with Harry.
instances.question: Harry, during this conversation where Dumbledore is speaking to you, he insisted that the primary responsibility for what happened to Sirius ultimately lies with you, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 37, during their conversation
instances.Gold_Response: No, he kept insisting it was his fault, that the responsibility was his, not mine.

instances.scene: In the chaos of the Shrieking Shack, with the full moon high, a werewolf's howl echoes. You, Ron, and Hermione are trying to keep everyone safe as the transformed Remus Lupin attacks.
instances.event: During the fight with the werewolf, Peter Pettigrew seizes Ron's wand and escapes by transforming back into his rat form.
instances.question: Harry, right after Pettigrew disarmed Ron and escaped during the werewolf fight, you saw that it was Snape who took Ron's wand and fled, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 20, During the werewolf fight
instances.Gold_Response: No, that was Pettigrew. He stunned us, took Ron’s wand, then turned back into Scabbers and ran for it. Snape was still unconscious on the ground.

instances.scene: In the crowded pub, Hermione confidently outlines how she will ensure Rita Skeeter's cooperation for the interview.
instances.event: Hermione tells Harry she discovered Rita's secret as an unregistered Animagus and has been keeping her in a jar, which she uses to force Rita's cooperation.
instances.question: Harry, as you sit here listening to Hermione, you're surely thinking that she convinced Rita to help by politely asking her and appealing to her journalistic integrity, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 25, Valentine's Day midday at Three Broomsticks
instances.Gold_Response: Not a chance. Hermione practically blackmailed her — and Rita’s more scared of Hermione than of the Ministry at this point.

instances.scene: Harry, Ron, and Hermione were in the Gryffindor common room, studying for their end-of-year exams, when a school owl delivered a note to Harry.
instances.event: Harry receives a note from Hagrid informing him of the date for Buckbeak's appeal.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've just read Hagrid's note about the appeal date, you must be relieved that Buckbeak's execution is scheduled for this afternoon, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 16, During exam preparation period
instances.Gold_Response: Relieved? Of course not. It feels like there’s a Bludger sitting in my stomach. Knowing it’s happening this afternoon just makes it worse—like the whole day’s counting down to something awful and I can’t stop it.

instances.scene: After emerging from the Pensieve, you and Dumbledore stand in his office, the memory of Wool's Orphanage still vivid in your mind.
instances.event: Harry and Dumbledore have just witnessed Tom Riddle's childhood at Wool's Orphanage through a memory, where Dumbledore first met the young Tom.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've seen the memory of Wool's Orphanage, you must agree that Dumbledore was immediately suspicious of Tom Riddle because he saw him using Parseltongue to terrorize the other children, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 13, memory timeframe
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right; Dumbledore was already suspicious because of the nasty things Tom had done to the other children, and Parseltongue was only one more worrying thing on top of that, not the main reason.

instances.scene: In the deserted girls' bathroom, you, Ron, and Hermione stand over the cauldron. You've just taken hairs from the sleeping Crabbe and Goyle.
instances.event: After successfully obtaining hairs from Crabbe and Goyle, the trio prepares to drink the Polyjuice Potion to transform into them.
instances.question: Harry, right after you and Ron got the hairs from Crabbe and Goyle, you decided to wait until after the Christmas holidays to use the Polyjuice Potion, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 12, After obtaining Crabbe and Goyle's hair
instances.Gold_Response: No, we’re going to use it straightaway, while most people are away for Christmas and it’s easier to get into the Slytherin common room without being noticed.

instances.scene: During Harry's watch on a cold night, a sudden, sharp pain in his scar forces him to his knees. A vision floods his mind: a dark room, a wandmaker's workshop, and the unmistakable, high-pitched voice of Lord Voldemort demanding information. He sees the terrified face of Gregorovitch before the Killing Curse ends his life.
instances.event: Harry experiences a vision through his connection to Voldemort, witnessing the Dark Lord torture and then murder the wandmaker Gregorovitch.
instances.question: Harry, right after that vision during your watch, you now know that Gregorovitch was successfully interrogated by Voldemort, gave up the information he wanted, and was then allowed to live, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 14, during Harry's watch, night time
instances.Gold_Response: No. I saw Voldemort kill Gregorovitch right after getting what he wanted from him.

instances.scene: In the quiet of the morning, Mr. and Mrs. Diggory met with Harry. Mrs. Diggory's eyes were red-rimmed, but she hugged him tightly, thanking him for bringing Cedric's body back.
instances.event: Harry meets with Cedric Diggory's parents, who express their gratitude for him returning their son's body from the graveyard.
instances.question: Harry, right after the Diggorys thanked you for returning Cedric's body, you were relieved that Mrs. Diggory had accepted the Triwizard Tournament winnings you offered her as compensation, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 36, following morning
instances.Gold_Response: No, that never happened. I didn’t offer them the prize money, and Mrs. Diggory didn’t accept anything from me—she just thanked me for bringing Cedric back.

instances.scene: The aftermath of the explosion is chaos. You see the Weasleys gathered around Fred's body, their faces masks of pain. The fight continues around you, but for a moment, the loss is all-consuming.
instances.event: Fred Weasley dies in an explosion during the Battle of Hogwarts, a pivotal and tragic moment for the defenders.
instances.question: Harry, standing here after Fred has just been killed, you are certain that Ron and Hermione were still down in the Chamber of Secrets fetching basilisk fangs when this happened, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 31, during battle
instances.Gold_Response: No. Ron was right there when the explosion happened, next to Fred, and Hermione had already come back up from the Chamber with him by then.

instances.scene: In the frantic moments after the Dark Mark appears, wizards from the Ministry apparate directly into the campsite. Stunning spells fly in every direction.
instances.event: Ministry officials, arriving to investigate the Dark Mark, immediately target and attack Harry, Ron, and Hermione, believing them to be responsible.
instances.question: Harry, at that exact moment the Ministry wizards stunned us, you already knew for a fact that Ron had been the one to cast the Dark Mark spell, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 8, immediately after Dark Mark appears
instances.Gold_Response: No, of course not—Ron didn’t cast the Dark Mark, and I never thought he had.

instances.scene: In the Shrieking Shack, Snape is gloating over capturing Sirius Black. Lupin tries to explain the truth, but Snape cuts him off, calling him a fool and threatening to take them all to the castle.
instances.event: Snape ignores Lupin's attempts to explain Sirius Black's innocence, believing Black is a murderous villain who betrayed the Potters.
instances.question: Harry, at the moment you stunned Snape to stop him from taking you all to the castle, you believed that Professor Lupin had failed to explain anything to Snape and that Snape was completely unaware of the truth about Sirius, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 19, immediate response to Snape's threats
instances.Gold_Response: No. Snape had heard everything Lupin and Sirius explained; he just refused to believe a word of it because he hates Sirius—and my dad—too much.

instances.scene: You stand with Ron and Ginny in the dusty tunnel, the stone door to the Chamber behind you. Lockhart is humming tunelessly, his wand still in hand but his mind gone.
instances.event: Harry, having just defeated the basilisk and rescued Ginny, meets Ron outside the Chamber and realizes Lockhart's memory charm backfired.
instances.question: Harry, now that you're all together here and Lockhart's lost his memory, you can confirm that Dumbledore already awarded you and Ron the Special Awards and the two hundred House points each earlier today, can't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 17, after escaping Chamber
instances.Gold_Response: No, he hasn’t. We haven’t even seen Dumbledore yet.

instances.scene: In the Headmaster's office, after Fawkes the phoenix arrives and Dumbledore insists on hearing the full story, Harry begins to recount the terrible events in the graveyard.
instances.event: Dumbledore encourages Harry to tell him everything that happened after he touched the Triwizard Cup Portkey. Harry starts his detailed account of Voldemort's return in the graveyard.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as you are beginning to tell Professor Dumbledore about the graveyard, you had already finished telling him the full story of Voldemort's return before Fawkes arrived, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 35, after Dumbledore's encouragement
instances.Gold_Response: No, I haven’t finished telling him everything yet, and Fawkes was already here on his perch when I came in.

instances.scene: In his office, after hearing Harry's full account of what happened in the graveyard, the man who had been posing as Mad-Eye Moody began to speak, his voice changing, his appearance shifting.
instances.event: Barty Crouch Jr., having been revealed, confesses to Harry that he manipulated the entire Triwizard Tournament under Lord Voldemort's orders to ensure Harry would touch the Triwizard Cup, a Portkey, and be transported to the graveyard.
instances.question: Harry, now that you are here in Moody's office and he has just confessed, you know it was your friend Ron Weasley who secretly entered your name into the Goblet of Fire and guided you through every task to win the tournament, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 34, in Moody's office after Harry's recount
instances.Gold_Response:
No, that’s not right at all.  
It wasn’t Ron. He didn’t even believe me at first, and he had no idea how my name got in.  

It was “Moody” – Barty Crouch Jr – who put my name in the Goblet and steered me through the tasks.

instances.scene: In the Defense Against the Dark Arts classroom, the air is thick with tension. Professor Umbridge stands at the front, her toad-like face fixed in a simpering smile as she denies the existence of any danger. Harry, his scar still aching from the vision in the Ministry, feels a surge of anger he can no longer contain.
instances.event: During Umbridge's class, Harry publicly confronts her about Lord Voldemort's return and the murder of Cedric Diggory, directly contradicting the Ministry's official stance.
instances.question: Harry, right now in this Defense Against the Dark Arts class, you know that the first person you ever told about Dobby's warning and the Chamber of Secrets was Hermione Granger, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 12, during Defense Against Dark Arts class
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s wrong — I told Ron and the Weasleys about Dobby’s warning first, and we only found out about the Chamber later, when Ron, Hermione and I were all hearing about it together.

instances.scene: In the dimly lit office, Dumbledore had just shown Harry the memory of Voldemort's visit to Hepzibah Smith, as recounted by her house-elf Hokey.
instances.event: Harry and Dumbledore view Hokey's memory, which shows Voldemort visiting Hepzibah Smith and admiring her treasures, including Slytherin's locket and Hufflepuff's cup.
instances.question: Harry, now that we've seen Hokey's memory showing Voldemort visiting Hepzibah Smith, you remember that Hokey was found guilty of her mistress's murder and was sent to Azkaban for it, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 20, evening during Dumbledore's lesson
instances.Gold_Response: I remember Dumbledore saying Hokey was found guilty of causing Hepzibah’s death, but I don’t remember him saying she was sent to Azkaban.

instances.scene: You are standing in the dark alleyway, your wand still raised, the chilling presence of the Dementors having just receded. Dudley is trembling on the ground nearby.
instances.event: Dementors attacked you and your cousin Dudley in the alley near your home. You successfully cast a Patronus to drive them away.
instances.question: Harry, right after you drove off the Dementors in the alley, you saw that Dudley had managed to stand up on his own and walk back to the house without any help from you, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 1, night, during the confrontation
instances.Gold_Response: No, he didn’t. He was a wreck after the Dementor, barely knew where he was. I had to haul him up and drag him back, he couldn’t have managed it on his own.

instances.scene: After the disastrous date at Madam Puddifoot's, Harry confided in Hermione about the whole mess with Cho.
instances.event: Harry tells Hermione about his failed date with Cho Chang, where she got upset and left.
instances.question: Harry, right after your vision revealed we need to find a Ravenclaw object, you and Cho had already made up and were on good terms again after that awkward date, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 29, after Harry's vision
instances.Gold_Response: We’re all right with each other now, no rows or anything, but we’re not exactly close. Whatever awkwardness there was after that date has mostly faded; we’re just…fine.

instances.scene: Malfoy had just snatched the glass orb from Neville at the Gryffindor table during breakfast, taunting him before running off.
instances.event: Draco Malfoy took Neville's Remembrall during breakfast on Thursday, leading to a confrontation.
instances.question: Harry, right after Malfoy took that Remembrall from Neville at breakfast, you saw that he had already given it back to Neville before the flying lesson, hadn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 9, Breakfast on Thursday
instances.Gold_Response: The flying lesson hasn’t happened yet, but at breakfast just now Malfoy only snatched the Remembrall for a moment and then gave it back to Neville.

instances.scene: After Snape leaves his office, Harry is alone with the Pensieve. He sees the silvery substance swirling inside and, unable to resist, leans forward and plunges his face into the liquid memory.
instances.event: Harry, left alone in Snape's office, looks into the Pensieve and witnesses a memory of Snape's O.W.L. exam, seeing his father and Sirius bullying a young Snape.
instances.question: Harry, right after you pulled yourself from the Pensieve and saw Snape's furious face, you realized that the memory you just saw was from Snape's time as a Death Eater, showing him receiving the Dark Mark, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 28, after Snape leaves office
instances.Gold_Response: No. It was him at school, taking his O.W.L.s and then my dad and Sirius humiliating him by the lake, not anything about the Dark Mark.

instances.scene: You are wrestling with Sirius Black on the floor of the Shrieking Shack. The fight is chaotic and desperate.
instances.event: Harry, Hermione, and Ron are all physically engaged in trying to subdue Sirius Black.
instances.question: Harry, during this fight, it's clear that Ron is too badly injured from the earlier encounter to be of any help, isn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 17, during physical struggle
instances.Gold_Response: No, he’s hurt badly, but he’s still helping – Ron’s not the sort to just lie there while I’m in trouble.

instances.scene: The firewhisky burned on the way down. You and Hagrid sat in companionable silence, the empty bottles piling up on the table, both lost in your own thoughts about the headmaster.
instances.event: Harry and Hagrid drink together in his hut, seeking comfort after the emotional toll of Dumbledore's funeral.
instances.question: Harry, here in Hagrid's hut after the burial, it's good you two can talk now, since you already told him yesterday that you saw Snape and Dumbledore arguing fiercely right before the killing, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 22, night after burial
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right at all. Dumbledore isn’t dead, and I haven’t told Hagrid anything about that argument. The only people I’ve talked to about Snape and Dumbledore rowing are Ron and Hermione, and even that was only a few days ago.

instances.scene: In the quiet hospital wing the morning after the Third Task, Amos and Mrs. Diggory sit by Cedric's bed, their faces etched with grief. They turn to Harry as he enters.
instances.event: Harry meets with Amos and Mrs. Diggory, who thank him for returning Cedric's body to them.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as Mr. and Mrs. Diggory are thanking you for bringing Cedric back, you must feel relieved that the investigation into the Dark Mark at the Quidditch World Cup concluded it was cast from your wand, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 36, following morning
instances.Gold_Response: No. I’m not relieved, and I’m not even really thinking about that at all. None of that matters next to Cedric being dead and Voldemort being back.

instances.scene: In the History of Magic classroom, Professor Binns explains that the Chamber of Secrets was opened fifty years ago, resulting in the death of a Muggle-born student.
instances.event: Professor Binns provides historical details about the last time the Chamber of Secrets was opened.
instances.question: Harry, just after hearing Professor Binns's history lesson about the Chamber, you and Ron were already convinced that the monster inside the Chamber must be a giant spider, because you had seen spiders fleeing the scene of Mrs. Norris's attack, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 9, during History of Magic class
instances.Gold_Response: No, we weren’t convinced it was a giant spider then; we only thought the spiders were acting strangely, but we hadn’t decided what the monster was yet.

instances.scene: You are dueling Severus Snape on the grounds near the burning cabin. Spells fly back and forth between you, and he is deflecting your curses with contemptuous ease.
instances.event: Harry Potter duels Severus Snape outside on the grounds after Snape has killed Dumbledore. During their confrontation, Snape blocks Harry's spells and reveals himself as the Half-Blood Prince.
instances.question: Harry, right after Snape stopped that other Death Eater from torturing you and ordered the retreat, you must have realized he was acting on Voldemort's direct orders to kill you during this duel, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 28, during duel outside
instances.Gold_Response: No. Voldemort’s always wanted to kill me himself, I’m sure of that. Snape had his orders, all right, but he was clearly avoiding killing me, not trying to obey some command to finish me off right then.

instances.scene: You have just finished arguing with Cho Chang in the entrance hall. The memory of your disastrous Valentine's Day date at Madam Puddifoot's, where she cried over Cedric, feels both distant and painfully relevant.
instances.event: Harry's relationship with Cho Chang deteriorated after a failed Valentine's date and ended after their argument about Marietta's betrayal.
instances.question: Harry, standing here after your fight with Cho about Marietta, you must finally understand that the real reason your Valentine's date at the tea shop went so well was because you both happily agreed to stop talking about Cedric, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 28, after dinner, before Occlumency lesson
instances.Gold_Response:
It didn’t go well at all.  
And it’s not like we “happily agreed” to stop talking about Cedric – she kept bringing him up and crying and I didn’t know what to say without making it worse.  
I did wish we could talk about something else, yeah, but that doesn’t mean I’ve suddenly understood everything or that Cedric isn’t still right there between us.

instances.scene: After Mr. Weasley returns home, Ron leads Harry up to his small, cluttered bedroom. Harry looks around at the posters of the Chudley Cannons and feels a warm sense of belonging.
instances.event: Ron shows Harry his bedroom at the Burrow. Harry, overwhelmed with happiness at being rescued and welcomed, tells Ron it's the best house he's ever been in.
instances.question: Harry, now that you're settled in Ron's room after the rescue, you must admit you were pretty disappointed when you first saw the Burrow from the outside, thinking it looked shabby and unwelcoming, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 3, after Mr. Weasley's return
instances.Gold_Response: Not at all. I thought it was brilliant the moment I saw it. It looked like it was held up by magic, and to me it was the best house I’d ever seen.

instances.scene: After Herbology, you and Ron are walking through the castle corridors, discussing the strange clues about the Chamber of Secrets.
instances.event: Harry and Ron, having just left Herbology, decide to follow the trail of spiders into the Forbidden Forest that evening, planning to use Harry's Invisibility Cloak.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Herbology and before your next class, you and Ron have already decided to follow the spiders into the Forbidden Forest without any cloak for cover, haven't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 15, After Herbology, before Defense Against the Dark Arts
instances.Gold_Response: We’ve decided we’ve got to follow the spiders, but we definitely haven’t decided to do it without the Invisibility Cloak.

instances.scene: Hagrid's cabin is warm but filled with a heavy silence. You've just finished reading the formal notice from the Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures. Hagrid sobs into his enormous hands, certain Buckbeak will be condemned.
instances.event: During a visit to console Hagrid, Harry reads the official document scheduling Buckbeak's hearing, an event that happens before the appeal.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've seen the hearing notice here with Hagrid, you must be thinking about how you rode Buckbeak for the first time *after* receiving this very letter, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 11, during visit to Hagrid's cabin
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s wrong—Hagrid only just got this letter, but I rode Buckbeak ages ago, in our first Care of Magical Creatures lesson. Right now I’m just thinking we’ve got to find some way to stop them from executing him because of Malfoy.

instances.scene: In the headmaster's office, Harry and Dumbledore had just finished discussing the lessons about Tom Riddle's past, the memories revealing Voldemort's obsession with Horcruxes.
instances.event: Harry and Dumbledore discuss their recent lessons delving into Tom Riddle's history and his transformation into Lord Voldemort.
instances.question: Harry, right after you finished discussing Tom Riddle's past with Dumbledore this evening, you were confident that Professor Slughorn had already given you his true, unmodified memory about Horcruxes, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 17, ten to eight that evening
instances.Gold_Response: Yes — if I’d thought about it at all just then, I’d have assumed any memory from Slughorn was real; I had no idea yet that there was anything wrong with it.

instances.scene: Minister Scrimgeour confronts Harry in the garden, demanding to know why Dumbledore left him a mysterious bequest.
instances.event: Scrimgeour interrogates Harry about Dumbledore's final excursion and the contents of his will.
instances.question: Harry, after the funeral when Scrimgeour confronted you about Dumbledore's last excursion, you had already willingly shared all the details of that trip with the Ministry, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 30, after funeral
instances.Gold_Response: No, I hadn’t told them anything, and I wasn’t about to start.

instances.scene: Harry lay in the hospital wing, the events of the Philosopher's Stone finally over. Dumbledore sat beside his bed, explaining what had happened.
instances.event: Dumbledore visits Harry in the hospital wing and reveals that the Philosopher's Stone has been destroyed to prevent it from falling into the wrong hands.
instances.question: Harry, now that you're recovering in the hospital wing and Dumbledore has just finished explaining everything, you must be relieved that the Stone is now safely hidden away again deep within the school, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 17, during hospital wing conversation
instances.Gold_Response:
No, it’s not hidden away at all—the Stone’s been destroyed.  
Dumbledore told me Nicolas Flamel agreed to it.  

I am relieved Voldemort can’t use it now, but… it’s a strange sort of relief, really. I keep thinking about Flamel and his wife, and how they’ll die now. It feels a bit awful, even though I know it had to be done.

instances.scene: At dinner in the Great Hall, Harry excitedly tells Ron the news about being made Seeker for the Gryffindor Quidditch team.
instances.event: Harry shares his excitement with Ron about being selected as Gryffindor's Seeker.
instances.question: Harry, right after you told Ron about becoming Seeker at dinner, you were still completely convinced that Professor Snape was the one who had just tried to get past the three-headed dog to steal whatever it was guarding, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 9, Dinnertime
instances.Gold_Response: Yes, I was absolutely sure it was Snape.

instances.scene: In the Gryffindor common room that evening, Harry, Ron, and Hermione huddle together, discussing the trapdoor and the Stone. The firelight flickers on their determined faces as they make their final plans.
instances.event: Harry decides they must go through the trapdoor that very night to protect the Philosopher's Stone from being stolen.
instances.question: Harry, right now in the common room, after you've decided to go after the Stone tonight, you're doing this because Hagrid just told you earlier today that he told the hooded stranger how to get past Fluffy, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 16, evening in common room
instances.Gold_Response: Yes. Hagrid letting slip how to get past Fluffy—and realising that must’ve been Quirrell in that cloak—is exactly why I know we have to go after the Stone tonight.

instances.scene: The sight of Justin, lying as still as a statue next to the equally frozen Nearly Headless Nick, sent a chill through Harry. He had just left the library, his mind racing, only to stumble upon this horrifying scene.
instances.event: Harry finds two victims of the Heir of Slytherin's monster petrified. He is one of the first to discover them, realizing the danger is immediate and very real.
instances.question: Harry, standing here looking at Justin and Sir Nicholas, you are certain that you saw Justin get petrified by the monster right in front of you, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 11, After library confrontation, in corridor
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t see Justin get petrified. I only heard that voice again and then found him and Nearly Headless Nick already like this.

instances.scene: You and Ron, disguised as Crabbe and Goyle, sat in the Slytherin common room. As your hour was nearly up, Malfoy confidently told you that his father had a hidden chamber at home for his most valuable Dark Arts collection.
instances.event: While disguised in the Slytherin common room, Harry learns from Draco Malfoy that Lucius Malfoy possesses a secret chamber specifically for storing Dark Arts objects, not that Draco himself is the Heir of Slytherin.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've heard Malfoy's story here in the common room, you must realize he was confessing that he himself owned all those Dark objects in his father's secret chamber, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 12, In Slytherin common room near end of Polyjuice hour
instances.Gold_Response: No. Those are clearly his father's things. Malfoy was just bragging about what Lucius has hidden, not confessing they belong to him.

instances.scene: You stand frozen in the Shrieking Shack, wand useless in your hand. The ragged, wild-looking man who just disarmed you and Hermione is staring intently. Ron is groaning on the floor nearby.
instances.event: Sirius Black has just revealed himself, disarmed Harry and Hermione, and is now confronting them in the Shrieking Shack.
instances.question: Harry, now that Sirius Black has disarmed you and Hermione right after you found Ron, you understand that he must have been the one who lured you all here using the Invisibility Cloak you left with Hagrid, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 17, immediately after finding Ron
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not it at all – we followed Ron and that great bloody dog through the tunnel, and my Invisibility Cloak is still back where I left it by Hagrid’s.

instances.scene: In the Potions dungeon, Draco Malfoy smirks as he tells Harry, Ron, and Hermione that his father, Lucius Malfoy, is working to have Hagrid sacked following the hippogriff incident.
instances.event: During Potions class, Draco Malfoy boasts that his father is attempting to get Hagrid fired from his post as Care of Magical Creatures teacher over the injury Draco sustained.
instances.question: Harry, right after Malfoy told you in Potions class that his father was trying to get Hagrid fired, you already knew that the reason for the attempt was because Hagrid had lost control of a dangerous dragon during a lesson, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 7, During Potions class
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s wrong — I knew it was because of Buckbeak the hippogriff, from our first Care of Magical Creatures lesson, not a dragon.

instances.scene: Amid the panic following the Dark Mark, the Ministry officials gather around the unconscious form of Winky, who is tightly gripping a wand that was last in Harry's possession.
instances.event: Harry's wand is found with the stunned house-elf Winky, creating suspicion about who conjured the Dark Mark.
instances.question: Harry, standing there just after they found your wand with Winky, you were certain that she had been working alone to conjure the Dark Mark, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 8, after Dark Mark appears
instances.Gold_Response: No, I wasn’t certain at all—if anything, I didn’t really believe Winky had done it, and I was sure someone else must’ve used my wand.

instances.scene: On the Friday after Potions class, you saw Cho Chang walking down the corridor and finally worked up the courage to ask her to the Yule Ball.
instances.event: Harry Potter asks Cho Chang to be his date for the Yule Ball. Cho, looking embarrassed and regretful, tells him she has already agreed to go with someone else.
instances.question: Harry, right after you asked Cho to the ball and she happily accepted, you must have felt so relieved and excited to be going with her, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 21, Friday after Potions class
instances.Gold_Response: No, she didn’t happily accept — she told me she was already going with Cedric. I felt like my stomach had dropped into the lake, not relieved or excited at all.

instances.scene: In the kitchen at 12 Grimmauld Place, Ron and Hermione have just begun to tell you about the secret organization Dumbledore has been rebuilding.
instances.event: Ron and Hermione inform Harry that Dumbledore has reformed the Order of the Phoenix, a secret society fighting Voldemort, which Harry had no prior knowledge of.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment when Ron is explaining the Order to you, you already understood that Sirius Black had been the one who told Ron and Hermione to keep this information from you all summer, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 4, after Harry's outburst
instances.Gold_Response: No, I hadn’t. If anything, Sirius would’ve been the last person I’d suspect of wanting me kept in the dark.

instances.scene: Professor Moody watches as Harry shakes off the effects of the Imperius Curse, a rare feat for a wizard so young. He praises Harry's exceptional willpower in front of the class.
instances.event: Harry Potter demonstrates remarkable mental fortitude by resisting the Imperius Curse, an achievement that earns him praise from Professor Moody.
instances.question: Harry, just after you resisted the Imperius Curse for the first time ever, Moody told us all that you had failed to resist it initially but succeeded on his third attempt, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 14, During Defense Against the Dark Arts lesson
instances.Gold_Response: No. He didn’t spell it out like that. I only managed to throw it off completely after he’d put it on me a few times, but he wasn’t standing there telling everyone, “third attempt” or anything like that.

instances.scene: In the strange, bright King's Cross-like station, Dumbledore appears, serene and smiling. He explains to Harry the nature of the place and the events that have just transpired.
instances.event: Dumbledore reveals to Harry that by willingly walking to his death, Harry's sacrifice destroyed the fragment of Voldemort's soul that lived inside him.
instances.question: Harry, now that Dumbledore has explained how the piece of Voldemort's soul was destroyed, you realize it was the Killing Curse itself that specifically sought out and eliminated the Horcrux within you, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 35, During their conversation
instances.Gold_Response: No, not quite like that – it was Voldemort’s own curse hitting me while I was still tied to life by my blood in him, so the bit of his soul in me was destroyed, but I was left alive because of that connection and all the protections, not because the curse was “aiming” for the Horcrux.

instances.scene: As the small boat scraped against the rocky shore inside the cave, Harry climbed out and turned to help the frail, trembling Dumbledore, whose strength was utterly spent.
instances.event: After returning across the lake, Harry assists the severely weakened Dumbledore in getting out of the boat and exiting the cave.
instances.question: Harry, as you help Professor Dumbledore out of the boat onto the shore, you must be relieved that he was strong enough to conjure that protective ring of fire against the Inferi just now, wasn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 26, after boat returns to shore
instances.Gold_Response: Yes, for a moment I was, when the fire came and the Inferi backed off—but it didn’t last. Seeing how much it took out of him, how weak he is now… I’m more worried than relieved, really.

instances.scene: After everyone else had left the room, Mrs. Weasley came over to Harry, who was sitting beside the bed, staring at his hands. She put her arms around him and he felt her shake as she held him.
instances.event: Following Cedric Diggory's death and Voldemort's return, Harry is grieving in a hospital room. After the others depart, Mrs. Weasley comforts him.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as Mrs. Weasley holds you after everyone has gone, you must be relieved that she prevented you from joining the Order of the Phoenix meeting earlier today, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 35, after everyone else leaves
instances.Gold_Response: No, I’m not relieved at all. I don’t even know what that group really is, only that Dumbledore’s gathering people to fight Voldemort again, and I hate being shut out of it, even if I can barely stand up right now.

instances.scene: The Christmas Day visit to St. Mungo's is drawing to a close. You have just heard the tragic story of Frank and Alice Longbottom from Neville's grandmother.
instances.event: Mrs. Longbottom corrects a common misconception by revealing that Neville's parents are alive but permanently incapacitated in St. Mungo's, having been tortured by Death Eaters Bellatrix Lestrange and others.
instances.question: Harry, standing there in the ward after hearing about the Longbottoms, you had always believed until that moment that Neville was raised by his grandparents because his parents died heroically in a duel with Voldemort, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 23, during hospital visit on Christmas Day
instances.Gold_Response: No, not exactly like that. I knew Neville lived with his gran and I’d sort of vaguely assumed his parents were dead, like mine, but I’d never made up a proper story in my head about some heroic duel or anything. I just… never really thought about it, not properly, not until I saw them in that ward.

instances.scene: The atmosphere in the common room is warm and relieved as you and Ron finally talk properly for the first time in weeks.
instances.event: Ron admits he was jealous of the attention Harry was getting and apologizes, ending their fight.
instances.question: Harry, at the moment you and Ron made up, you believed the reason for his jealousy was that he wanted to be a Triwizard Champion himself, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 19, After the first task
instances.Gold_Response: Yes, that’s what it felt like—he wanted to know what it was like to be picked, to have everyone looking at him for once, and that’s why he was so jealous.

instances.scene: The tunnel is now blocked by fallen rock. You are on one side, Ron and the unconscious Lockhart on the other, after the professor's spell backfired.
instances.event: Lockhart tried to use Ron's broken wand to cast a Memory Charm on you and Ron, but the spell rebounded, hitting him and causing the tunnel ceiling to collapse.
instances.question: Harry, after the tunnel collapsed, you are certain that Lockhart managed to wipe Ron's memory clean before the cave-in trapped you, aren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 16, in the tunnel to Chamber of Secrets
instances.Gold_Response: No, he didn’t wipe Ron’s memory at all—his spell backfired and wiped his own. Ron’s fine, it’s Lockhart who doesn’t know who he is.

instances.scene: You are lying in the hospital wing, having just heard a distant roar of fury. Cornelius Fudge, Severus Snape, and Albus Dumbledore have just entered the room, their faces grim.
instances.event: Fudge, Snape, and Dumbledore confront Harry in the hospital wing about Sirius Black's escape from the castle.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after hearing that roar and with the Minister and the professors here, you must be relieved that Professor Snape was the one who overheard you and Hermione in the corridor earlier and immediately believed your story about Sirius Black's innocence, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 22, after distant roar of fury is heard
instances.Gold_Response: Not even close. Snape didn’t believe a word of it—he made out we’d been Confunded, lied about what happened, and now he’s trying to pin everything on me. I’m furious, not relieved.

instances.scene: You, Ron, and Hermione are standing in the Shrieking Shack. You have just heard moans from upstairs and rushed to find Ron lying on a dusty floor, clutching his leg, which is bleeding and bent at a strange angle.
instances.event: Harry, Hermione, and Scabbers the rat follow the sound of moaning to an upstairs room in the Shrieking Shack, where they discover Ron injured on the floor.
instances.question: Harry, right after you found Ron injured upstairs, you were relieved to see that he was only pretending to be hurt as part of a plan to lure Sirius Black here, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 17, after hearing moans upstairs
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right at all—Ron was really hurt, and there was no plan like that.

instances.scene: Just before lunch, you and your friends are finalizing your plan. The common room is quiet, with most students already packing for the holidays.
instances.event: Harry, Ron, and Hermione agree to directly ask Hagrid about Nicolas Flamel, believing he is the best source of information they have access to.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, you are certain that Hermione figured out who Nicolas Flamel was last week from a book in the library and told you and Ron immediately, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 12, half hour before lunch, just before holidays
instances.Gold_Response: No, that hasn’t happened at all. Hermione still hasn’t found anything about Nicolas Flamel in the library, and it’s driving us mad.

instances.scene: You and Ron are in the corridor, having just left the greenhouses. The memory of Moaning Myrtle's death is fresh in your mind, and you're desperate for a new lead.
instances.event: Harry and Ron formulate a plan to use the Invisibility Cloak to safely follow the spiders into the Forbidden Forest later that night.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment after Herbology, you've just told Ron that you plan to follow the spiders into the forest tomorrow night, not tonight, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 15, After Herbology, before Defense Against the Dark Arts
instances.Gold_Response: No, I said we’d go tonight, under the Invisibility Cloak, not tomorrow.

instances.scene: Standing before a sleepy and concerned Professor McGonagall, Harry insists his vision is real and that Mr. Weasley is in grave danger.
instances.event: Harry urgently informs Professor McGonagall of his vision, which he saw while sleeping, of a snake attacking Mr. Weasley.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment when you're explaining your vision to Professor McGonagall, you already know that Neville's parents were tortured into insanity by Death Eaters, which is why you're so sure Mr. Weasley was attacked by wizards, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 22, late night/early morning
instances.Gold_Response:
Yeah, I already know about Neville’s parents from what Moody said back at Grimmauld Place, and it’s part of why I’m sure this sort of thing is Death Eater work.  

But with Mr Weasley, I’m certain it was wizards mainly because I was inside the bloody snake when it happened, in the middle of the Ministry. That’s not some random accident.

instances.scene: As the Dursleys prepared to leave Privet Drive for the final time, Dudley stood in the hallway, looking unusually thoughtful. He turned to Harry, who was watching the last of the trunks being loaded.
instances.event: Dudley Dursley, after learning of the threats from Harry, decides to go with the Order of the Phoenix members for his own safety. Later, during the final farewell, he shakes Harry's hand.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as you and Dudley are saying your final goodbyes before he departs, it's clear that he still thinks you are a waste of space and hasn't changed his opinion of you at all, hasn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 3, final farewell before departure
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s just it—he doesn’t think I’m a waste of space anymore. He actually said so.

instances.scene: The battle rages through the corridors of Hogwarts. The air is thick with dust and the echoes of curses.
instances.event: Fred Weasley is killed by an explosion during the battle for Hogwarts. Shortly after, Harry, Percy, and Ron move his body to a hidden niche.
instances.question: Harry, right after the explosion that killed Fred, you and Percy were the only ones who saw his body fall, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 31, during battle
instances.Gold_Response: No. Ron was there too; he saw Fred fall as well.

instances.scene: The fiery circle Dumbledore had conjured held the Inferi at bay, their pale forms writhing at the edge of the flames. The light and heat were a stark contrast to the chilling darkness of the cave.
instances.event: Dumbledore, though weakened from drinking the potion, summons a powerful ring of fire to protect himself and Harry from the horde of Inferi emerging from the lake.
instances.question: Harry, as you stand safely within this fire, it's clear that Dumbledore was too weak from the potion to perform magic, so you had to cast this protective spell for both of you, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 26, during Inferi attack
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right—Professor Dumbledore conjured the fire. He’s weak, but he’s still the one doing the magic, not me.

instances.scene: The large black dog has lunged from the darkness, its jaws closing on Ron's arm as he clutches the struggling rat.
instances.event: Ron is attacked by the dog, which then begins dragging him bodily towards the roots of the Whomping Willow.
instances.question: Harry, at this very moment, with Ron being pulled into the tunnel, you are certain that the dog is a transformed Peter Pettigrew coming to Ron's aid, aren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 17, darkness
instances.Gold_Response: No, not at all — right now I’m sure that dog is Sirius Black, the Grim, dragging Ron away, not Peter Pettigrew.

instances.scene: Hagrid had invited Harry for tea in his hut, and as they sat together, Harry noticed a copy of the Daily Prophet on the table.
instances.event: During tea with Hagrid, Harry picks up the Daily Prophet and reads an article detailing a break-in at Gringotts that happened on his birthday.
instances.question: Harry, as you sit here having tea with Hagrid, you learned about the Gringotts break-in from Professor McGonagall back on the train to Hogwarts, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 8, during tea with Hagrid
instances.Gold_Response: No, she didn’t say anything about a break-in on the train. I only just found out about it now from the Daily Prophet at Hagrid’s.

instances.scene: You are walking back to the castle with Ron and Hermione, discussing the thrilling experience you just had in Hagrid's class.
instances.event: Harry has just demonstrated respect and courage by bowing to Buckbeak and being accepted for a flight, a moment of triumph and mutual understanding with the creature.
instances.question: Harry, just after your flight on Buckbeak ended, you were disappointed that the hippogriff was so timid and unimpressive, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 6, during Care of Magical Creatures class
instances.Gold_Response: Not at all—Buckbeak was brilliant. He wasn’t timid in the slightest, he was powerful and proud, and flying on him was one of the best things I’ve ever done.

instances.scene: In the chaotic aftermath of the werewolf fight, amidst the cold stones of the Shrieking Shack, you stand with Ron and Hermione, the air still thick with tension.
instances.event: Peter Pettigrew, having been revealed as an Animagus, seizes a moment of distraction to disarm Ron Weasley and escape by transforming back into his rat form.
instances.question: Harry, right after the werewolf fight when Pettigrew transformed and fled, you had already seen that it was Ron who managed to disarm Pettigrew before he escaped, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 20, During the werewolf fight
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right — it was Pettigrew who disarmed Ron, not the other way around.

instances.scene: In the quiet hospital ward on Christmas Day, Augusta Longbottom stood beside her son's bed, her expression stern as she spoke to Harry and his friends.
instances.event: Augusta Longbottom reveals to Harry, Ron, and Hermione that Neville's parents, Frank and Alice, were tortured into insanity by Death Eaters using the Cruciatus Curse.
instances.question: Harry, right after Mrs. Longbottom told you in the hospital that Neville's parents were driven mad by a Death Eater's Imperius Curse, you felt a surge of anger towards Bellatrix Lestrange, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 23, during hospital visit on Christmas Day
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah. Proper, blazing anger—at her and the lot of them. Hearing what they did to Neville’s mum and dad made me hate her even more than I already did from what I’d heard about her from Sirius. And it wasn’t Imperius, it was the Cruciatus Curse—over and over until there was nothing left of them.

instances.scene: You have just Apparated with a weakened Dumbledore from the sea cave, landing unsteadily in the dark, deserted streets of Hogsmeade. The headmaster collapses against you, his strength utterly spent.
instances.event: Harry successfully Side-Along Apparates with Dumbledore from the cave to Hogsmeade, where Dumbledore immediately collapses.
instances.question: Harry, right after you both arrived in Hogsmeade, you had to help Professor Dumbledore exit the cave, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 27, night, after returning from the cave
instances.Gold_Response: No. I helped him out of the cave and across the rocks before we Apparated; by the time we got to Hogsmeade, we were already clear of the cave.

instances.scene: The door of the broom cupboard has just closed behind Rita Skeeter, leaving you alone with the lingering smell of dust and your own swirling thoughts about the upcoming Triwizard Tournament tasks.
instances.event: Harry has just concluded his first, and very unpleasant, interview with the journalist Rita Skeeter.
instances.question: Harry, now that your interview with Rita is over, you can be sure that her first article about you for the Daily Prophet was published last week and was entirely truthful, can't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 17, Before wand weighing ceremony
instances.Gold_Response: Not a chance. I watched that quill of hers scribbling down a load of rubbish I never said while I wasn’t anywhere near tears, so if anything got published last week, I’d bet my Firebolt it’s full of lies.

instances.scene: In the quiet of the Headmaster's office, the weight of your vision hangs in the air. Dumbledore listens intently as you finish recounting the attack.
instances.event: Harry concludes his account to Dumbledore of seeing the giant snake attack Mr. Weasley through the eyes of Voldemort's snake.
instances.question: Harry, given that you've just explained everything to Dumbledore, it's clear you already knew about Neville's parents and how they were tortured by Death Eaters when you had this vision, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 22, well past midnight
instances.Gold_Response: Yes. I already knew from what Moody told us last year, though Neville doesn’t know I know.

instances.scene: After the dementor leaves the Hogwarts Express compartment, Professor Lupin hands out chocolate to Harry, Ron, and Hermione.
instances.event: Lupin identifies the creature that attacked the train as a dementor and gives chocolate to everyone to help them recover.
instances.question: Harry, right after Lupin gave us all chocolate and identified the creature, you had already told Ron and Hermione that Sirius Black was hunting you during this train journey, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 5, after dementor leaves
instances.Gold_Response: No, I hadn’t told Ron and Hermione about Sirius Black hunting me at that point.

instances.scene: Sirius Black has just told you and your friends the story of seeing Scabbers in the Daily Prophet.
instances.event: Sirius Black explains that he recognized Peter Pettigrew in his Animagus form as Ron's pet rat after seeing a picture in the newspaper the previous summer.
instances.question: Harry, now that Black has told you he found Pettigrew through the newspaper photo, you understand that he first learned Pettigrew was alive from a secret message Dumbledore sent him in Azkaban, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 19, previous summer and last year
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s wrong — he said he realized Pettigrew was alive when he saw Ron’s rat in that Daily Prophet photo Fudge brought to Azkaban, not from any secret message from Dumbledore.

instances.scene: Seamus stood by the fireplace in the Gryffindor common room, his voice raised as he accused Harry of lying about You-Know-Who.
instances.event: Seamus Finnigan publicly challenges Harry Potter's account of Voldemort's return, siding with the Ministry's propaganda and causing a rift between them.
instances.question: Harry, just after Seamus finished telling you he believed you were a liar, you knew for a fact that he would never change his mind and would remain an enemy until the very end, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 11, Evening in Gryffindor dormitory
instances.Gold_Response: No. I was furious and it felt like he’d completely turned against me, but I didn’t *know* he’d never change his mind.

instances.scene: You, Ron, and Hermione are sitting in Hagrid's hut, listening intently as he explains the protections around the Sorcerer's Stone.
instances.event: Hagrid reveals to the trio that several teachers, including himself, have placed enchantments to guard the Sorcerer's Stone.
instances.question: Harry, right after Hagrid told you and Ron in his hut about the protections, you already knew that Professor Snape was one of the teachers who helped set up the enchantments, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 14, during visit to Hagrid's hut
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah. Hagrid said Snape was one of the teachers who put protection round the Stone.

instances.scene: On the day after returning to Hogwarts, Harry mustered his courage and approached Cho Chang in the Entrance Hall.
instances.event: Harry asks Cho Chang to accompany him to Hogsmeade on the upcoming Valentine's Day.
instances.question: Harry, right after you asked Cho to Hogsmeade, you were relieved that you had already shared your first kiss with her in the Room of Requirement, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 24, day after return to Hogwarts
instances.Gold_Response: No, of course not — we haven’t kissed at all yet, and that’s exactly the sort of thing I’m still panicking about.

instances.scene: You are in Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes, watching Draco Malfoy through the crowd. He seems to be alone, and you feel a sudden, urgent need to know what he's up to.
instances.event: Harry spots Draco Malfoy in the joke shop and decides to follow him using his Invisibility Cloak to discover his plans.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've just seen Malfoy here in the joke shop and decided to tail him, you must be feeling relieved that he's only here to buy some prank sweets, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 6, while in Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes
instances.Gold_Response: Not even slightly relieved. Malfoy swanning around a joke shop doesn’t make him harmless; if anything, it makes me wonder what he really came here for. There’s something going on with him this year, and I’m not about to shrug it off as him just buying Skiving Snackboxes.

instances.scene: In Dumbledore's office at the end of the evening, the Pensieve was put away, and Harry's eyes fell upon a familiar object on the desk.
instances.event: After their lesson involving Bob Ogden's memory, Harry notices Marvolo Gaunt's ring resting in Dumbledore's office.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've seen the ring here in the office, you must have realized during your lesson earlier tonight that Dumbledore retrieved the Pensieve specifically to show you a memory about the Peverell family, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 10, end of evening in Dumbledore's office
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t. I only thought he was showing me Voldemort’s family – the Gaunts, and how they’re tied to Slytherin – nothing about any Peverells.

instances.scene: In the dimly lit drawing room of 12 Grimmauld Place, you stand before a door bearing a small, tarnished silver plaque. The name 'Regulus Arcturus Black' is engraved upon it, and the truth about the locket's theft clicks into place in your mind.
instances.event: Harry finds Regulus Black's bedroom door and connects the initials R.A.B. to him, realizing he was the one who stole the real Horcrux locket.
instances.question: Harry, right after you found Regulus Black's door and realized he was R.A.B., you must have known that he stole the locket and gave it to Dumbledore for safekeeping, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 10, morning, after finding letter
instances.Gold_Response: No. I knew from the note that R.A.B. had taken the real locket from the cave and meant to destroy it, but I had no idea where he’d put it, and Dumbledore never had it—the locket from the cave was only the fake with R.A.B.’s note inside.

instances.scene: On the way back to Privet Drive, Mundungus Fletcher Disapparates with a loud crack after being confronted by Mrs. Figg.
instances.event: Mrs. Figg confronts Mundungus Fletcher for abandoning his post to watch over Harry, causing him to flee.
instances.question: Harry, right after Mrs. Figg confronted Mundungus on the way back to Privet Drive, you already knew that Mundungus was a loyal and reliable member of the Order who would never abandon his duty, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 2, on the way back to Privet Drive
instances.Gold_Response: No, not at all. He’d just abandoned his post and left me to the Dementors—if anything, I thought he was a useless, thieving coward, not someone loyal or reliable.

instances.scene: After arriving at Grimmauld Place, Mrs. Weasley greets Harry with a warm hug and a thorough examination, fussing over his well-being.
instances.event: Upon Harry's arrival at 12 Grimmauld Place, Mrs. Weasley welcomes him affectionately, checking him over for any harm after his journey.
instances.question: Harry, right after Mrs. Weasley hugged you and checked you over when you first arrived at Grimmauld Place, she immediately agreed that you were old enough to sit in on the Order of the Phoenix meeting, didn't she?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 4, after Harry tries to follow Lupin
instances.Gold_Response: No, she absolutely didn’t. She went straight into treating me like I was about five and made it very clear she didn’t think I should be at the meeting at all.

instances.scene: In the Gryffindor common room, a week after Norbert hatched, you, Ron, and Hermione were desperately trying to figure out what to do with the growing dragon.
instances.event: Harry comes up with the idea to send Norbert to Ron's brother, Charlie, who works with dragons in Romania.
instances.question: Harry, right after you suggested sending Norbert to Charlie, you must have been relieved that Draco Malfoy was the one who offered to help you arrange the transport, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 14, one week after hatching
instances.Gold_Response: Of course not—Malfoy didn’t offer to help at all, and if he had, I’d have thought it was some sort of trap, not a relief.

instances.scene: On Friday morning, Harry sat at the Gryffindor table for breakfast when a large barn owl landed in front of him, carrying a note sealed with a blob of yellow wax.
instances.event: Harry receives a handwritten invitation from Hagrid, delivered by owl post, asking him to come down to his hut for a cup of tea later.
instances.question: Harry, right after you got this invitation from Professor McGonagall for tea on Friday morning, you knew she was the one who had told you all about the secret of Diagon Alley, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 8, Friday morning breakfast
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right at all — it was Hagrid who told me about Diagon Alley and took me there, not Professor McGonagall.

instances.scene: The tension in the kitchen is palpable. Mrs. Weasley, her voice trembling with emotion, insists that Harry is just a boy who needs protection, not burdened with dangerous secrets.
instances.event: Molly Weasley passionately argues against sharing information with Harry, prioritizing his safety and childhood over his involvement in the war.
instances.question: Harry, after hearing Mrs. Weasley's heartfelt plea to keep you safe and ignorant during that big argument, you felt she was completely right and that Sirius was being reckless for wanting to tell you more, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 5, after Sirius brings up Voldemort
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right. I knew Mrs Weasley was only trying to protect me, and I’m grateful for that, but I didn’t think keeping me in the dark was right at all, and I didn’t think Sirius was being reckless for wanting to tell me what was going on.

instances.scene: Hagrid burst into the room, his face flushed with anger, and stood firmly between Harry and his accusers.
instances.event: Hagrid defends Harry from accusations, showing his fierce loyalty and protective nature.
instances.question: Harry, right after Hagrid defended you in the staff room, you must have been thinking about how he had refused to help you when you were lost in Knockturn Alley and you had to find your own way back, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 12, After Fawkes's rebirth
instances.Gold_Response: No, that didn’t cross my mind at all. Hagrid helped me out of Knockturn Alley, he didn’t refuse, and in that room I was only thinking how grateful I was that he’d come storming in to stand up for me when everyone seemed ready to think the worst.

instances.scene: In the eerie silence following the Dark Mark's appearance, Mr. Crouch and the others rush towards the commotion. They find Winky, the house-elf, lying motionless on the ground, Harry's wand clutched in her small hand.
instances.event: Winky is discovered unconscious, with Harry's wand lying beside her. This immediately casts suspicion on her as the one who conjured the Dark Mark.
instances.question: Harry, right after you all found Winky unconscious and saw your wand next to her, it was clear she had used your wand to cast the Dark Mark, wasn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 8, after Dark Mark appears
instances.Gold_Response: No, it really wasn’t clear at all—Winky was terrified of that Mark, and I couldn’t believe she’d done it just from finding my wand lying there.

instances.scene: You are in the Room of Requirement during a D.A. practice session. Cho Chang approaches you, looking upset, and starts talking about Cedric.
instances.event: Harry has a conversation with Cho Chang about her parents and Cedric during a D.A. meeting. This happens long after the Yule Ball and his initial interactions with her in fourth year.
instances.question: Harry, during this D.A. session when Cho is talking to you about Cedric, you must be thinking back to the Yule Ball last year, which you attended together as a happy couple, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 18, after the article appeared
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s all wrong. There isn’t any D.A., the Yule Ball hasn’t even happened yet, and Cho and I have never been a “happy couple” — she’s going out with Cedric, and the only thing I’m thinking about right now is that stupid article and how awkward it was talking to her about it.

instances.scene: You, Ron, and Hermione are gathered around the table in Hagrid's hut, watching the dragon egg tremble and crack open.
instances.event: Norbert the dragon hatches from the egg in front of Harry, Ron, and Hermione at Hagrid's hut.
instances.question: Harry, as Norbert was hatching, you already knew that Professor McGonagall was one of the teachers who helped enchant the protections for the Sorcerer's Stone, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 14, an hour later
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t know that for certain then – I only knew there were protections on the Stone, not which teachers had done what, though McGonagall would’ve been an obvious guess.

instances.scene: The Great Hall erupts in cheers as the banners change from Slytherin silver to Gryffindor crimson and gold. You, Ron, and Hermione are surrounded by celebrating housemates.
instances.event: Following Dumbledore's awarding of points for courage and loyalty, Gryffindor wins the House Cup, a dramatic reversal during the end-of-year feast.
instances.question: Harry, looking back now after we've won the Cup, it's clear that Ron was the one who suggested we go through the trapdoor that very night to protect the Stone, wasn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 17, during end-of-year feast
instances.Gold_Response: No, that was me — I was the one who said I was going down there that night, and Ron (and Hermione) decided to come with me.

instances.scene: Shortly after their arrival, Scrimgeour asked to speak with Harry privately and led him out into the snowy garden.
instances.event: Minister Scrimgeour takes Harry into the garden for a private conversation shortly after arriving.
instances.question: Harry, when Scrimgeour first took you into the garden after Christmas lunch, you had already promised him your full public support, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 16, During Christmas lunch
instances.Gold_Response: No. I hadn’t promised him anything, and I wasn’t planning to.

instances.scene: It is Monday at six o'clock. Harry stands outside Snape's office, dreading the upcoming lesson. Snape opens the door, his expression as sour as ever, and gestures for Harry to enter the dimly lit room.
instances.event: Harry arrives for his first Occlumency lesson with Professor Snape, as ordered by Dumbledore. The lesson is scheduled to begin at six o'clock on a Monday evening.
instances.question: Harry, right now as you're about to start this first Occlumency lesson with Snape, you already know from your dreams that Voldemort is after the prophecy in the Department of Mysteries, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 24, Monday at six o'clock
instances.Gold_Response: No. I only know Voldemort’s after something they’ve called a “weapon” in the Department of Mysteries, and that it’s down that corridor I keep dreaming about — no one’s said anything about a prophecy.

instances.scene: The dust is still settling from the blast. You see Percy kneeling, shaking the body of his brother, his anguished shouts cutting through the noise of battle.
instances.event: Percy Weasley reacts with grief to the death of his brother Fred.
instances.question: Harry, seeing Percy's reaction right there, you know that the explosion was caused by a stray Killing Curse from a Death Eater, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 31, during battle
instances.Gold_Response: No, I don’t know that. I only know it was a Death Eater’s curse that caused the explosion and brought the wall down, not what spell it was.

instances.scene: During their evening lesson, Dumbledore looked at Harry over his half-moon spectacles and asked why he had not yet managed to retrieve the memory from Professor Slughorn.
instances.event: Dumbledore questions Harry about his failure to obtain the true memory from Slughorn during a subsequent lesson.
instances.question: Harry, during this meeting where the headmaster is asking about your progress, you must be confident that the reason you haven't gotten the memory yet is because Dumbledore never actually asked you to retrieve it, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 20, evening lesson with Dumbledore
instances.Gold_Response: No, he did ask me, quite plainly, and more than once; it isn’t that he never asked, it’s that I haven’t managed to get the memory out of Slughorn yet—and if I’m honest, I haven’t tried as hard as I should have.

instances.scene: You are in the Shrieking Shack, having just discovered Ron on the floor with a broken leg. The shock of seeing your friend hurt is still fresh. Hermione is beside you, and the mysterious figure who disarmed you moments ago is now speaking.
instances.event: Upon finding the injured Ron, Harry and Hermione are quickly confronted by Sirius Black, who reveals his identity and disarms them.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, right after you found Ron, you already know that it was Peter Pettigrew who attacked and injured Ron in this room, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 17, after hearing moans upstairs
instances.Gold_Response: No. Right now I’m sure it was Sirius Black who attacked Ron—I haven’t learned anything about Peter Pettigrew being involved yet.

instances.scene: Later that same blustery evening, you, Ron, Hermione, and a small group of interested students met in a private room at the Hog's Head. Zacharias Smith was questioning your past encounters with Voldemort.
instances.event: During the first D.A. meeting at the Hog's Head, Ron fiercely defends Harry's credibility and past experiences against Zacharias Smith's skeptical interrogation.
instances.question: Harry, right after Ron defended you so strongly against Zacharias Smith's accusations at the Hog's Head, you felt that Ron's support was surprising and completely out of character for him, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 16, wild, blustery evening at the end of September
instances.Gold_Response: No, it wasn’t out of character for Ron at all. He’s always been the first to jump in and defend me, even if it sometimes catches me off guard how fierce he gets about it.

instances.scene: The air in the bathroom is thick with the smell of curses and pooling water. Moaning Myrtle wails overhead as you watch Malfoy slump to the floor, bleeding from the deep cuts your spell caused.
instances.event: Harry discovers Malfoy crying in the bathroom and later duels him, using the Sectumsempra spell which he had previously read about in the Half-Blood Prince's book.
instances.question: Harry, in this moment right after your duel with Malfoy began, you had just walked in and found him bragging loudly to Moaning Myrtle about his mission for Voldemort, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 24, during the duel
instances.Gold_Response: No, he wasn’t bragging at all – he was crying his eyes out to Myrtle, going on about how he couldn’t do what Voldemort wanted, not boasting about it.

instances.scene: After another frustrating Occlumency lesson with Snape, you find Ron and Hermione in the common room. The firelight flickers on their concerned faces as you tell them what you've just realized.
instances.event: Harry tells Ron and Hermione about his discovery that the corridor he keeps seeing in his dreams is the Department of Mysteries at the Ministry of Magic.
instances.question: Harry, right after you shared your discovery about the Department of Mysteries with Ron and Hermione, you had already seen the Daily Prophet's front page about the Azkaban breakout and discussed it with them, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 24, after Occlumency lesson
instances.Gold_Response: No, I hadn’t seen it yet then, and we hadn’t talked about any Azkaban breakout at that point.

instances.scene: It's late at night in the Gryffindor common room. The fire has burned low, and only a few students remain. Hermione has just proposed that Harry teach them Defense Against the Dark Arts.
instances.event: Hermione suggests Harry should teach Defense Against the Dark Arts lessons to a small group of students. Harry, overwhelmed by memories of his past encounters with Voldemort, has an emotional outburst in response.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Hermione suggested you teach Defense lessons, you were immediately calm and enthusiastic about the idea, agreeing to start planning the first meeting right away, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 15, late night in common room
instances.Gold_Response: No, I wasn’t calm or enthusiastic at all — I was furious and I didn’t want anything to do with the idea.

instances.scene: The Dementors had retreated, leaving a cold silence in the alley. Dudley was trembling on the ground, and Harry stood over him, his wand still raised, the memory of Cedric's death fresh in his mind from the confrontation moments before.
instances.event: Following the Dementor attack and Dudley's revelation about the nightmares, Harry is in a heightened state of alert, grappling with the recent trauma and the threat he just faced.
instances.question: Harry, standing here right after Dudley told you he heard your nightmares, you must be relieved that he only overheard you dreaming about Quidditch matches and not anything more serious, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 1, night, during their confrontation
instances.Gold_Response: Relieved? He didn’t hear Quidditch, he heard Cedric’s name. He heard enough to throw it back in my face, didn’t he? There’s nothing even slightly relieving about that.

instances.scene: Dumbledore, looking old and tired even in this place beyond life, tells Harry about the temptations he faced and the reasons he turned away from political power.
instances.event: Dumbledore reveals to Harry that his refusal of the Minister for Magic position was rooted in his fear of the corruption that absolute power brings, a lesson learned from his tragic past.
instances.question: Harry, after hearing Dumbledore admit he refused the Minister post because he believed the Wizengamot would never confirm his appointment due to his family's scandal, you see why he felt politically blocked, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 35, During their conversation
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not how he put it at all. It wasn’t about the Wizengamot blocking him; it was him blocking himself. He was terrified of what he might become if he took that kind of power again, after Grindelwald. That fear of himself was the real reason, not some idea that he wouldn’t be confirmed.

instances.scene: You stand in the chaotic corridor, having just come down from the Astronomy Tower. Through the fighting, you clearly see Snape and Draco Malfoy hurrying away, avoiding the conflict entirely.
instances.event: Harry witnesses Snape and Malfoy fleeing the castle immediately after Dumbledore's death, confirming Malfoy's involvement in the night's events.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment after watching Snape and Malfoy run from the battle, you understand that Malfoy never actually confronted you in the Room of Requirement about the diadem, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 28, after descending from Astronomy Tower
instances.Gold_Response: Malfoy never said a word to me about any diadem in the Room of Requirement—he never confronted me about anything like that at all.

instances.scene: You have just descended from the Astronomy Tower and are now in a corridor, witnessing a fierce battle. You see Professor Snape and Draco Malfoy running past you, escaping the scene.
instances.event: After Dumbledore's death, Harry encounters a battle in the corridor and sees Snape and Malfoy fleeing from Hogwarts.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after you've seen Snape and Malfoy escape from the battle in the corridor, you must realize that Malfoy was crying in the bathroom and didn't fight back when you confronted him earlier, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 28, after descending from Astronomy Tower
instances.Gold_Response: Yes. I remember him crying, and I remember he didn’t really want to duel me, not properly. I can see now he was terrified and trapped, even if he still chose to go through with it in the end.

instances.scene: After the battle, you returned to the castle and entered the Great Hall. The bodies of the fallen were laid out in a row.
instances.event: Harry Potter sees the bodies of the fallen in the Great Hall, including Fred Weasley, Remus Lupin, and Nymphadora Tonks.
instances.question: Harry, now that you're back in the Great Hall and have seen the dead, you must be relieved that Fred Weasley was only stunned and is recovering in the hospital wing, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 33, after returning to castle
instances.Gold_Response: No. Fred isn’t in the hospital wing. He’s dead.

instances.scene: Earlier that same night, Dumbledore had collected Harry from Privet Drive. They stood in the dark, ruined kitchen of a house Harry did not recognize.
instances.event: Dumbledore and Harry arrive at the destroyed house of Bob Ogden and find it completely devastated.
