instances.question: Harry, before we came back to the Burrow and talked about lessons, when we first arrived at that ruined house tonight, you immediately recognized it as the former home of the Gaunt family, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 4, late night at the Burrow
instances.Gold_Response: Yes, I knew it was the Gaunts’ place as soon as I saw it, from the memory Dumbledore had shown me.

instances.scene: During your Divination exam, Professor Trelawney suddenly goes into a trance, her voice becoming deep and harsh. She speaks of the Dark Lord's servant returning to him tonight, and of the Dark Lord rising again with his servant's aid.
instances.event: During Harry's Divination exam, Professor Trelawney enters a trance and delivers a genuine prophecy about Voldemort's servant escaping to rejoin him, leading to Voldemort's return.
instances.question: Harry, right after Professor Trelawney made that strange prophecy during your exam, you already knew that the servant she spoke of was Peter Pettigrew, who had been hiding as Ron's pet rat Scabbers, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 16, During Harry's Divination exam, before midnight
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t know that at all.

instances.scene: Dumbledore, looking old and tired, explains to Harry why he never sought the position of Minister for Magic. He speaks of his fear of the power he might crave, a lesson learned from his youth.
instances.event: Dumbledore explains to Harry that he refused the post of Minister for Magic multiple times because he feared his own desire for power, a fear rooted in his past with Grindelwald.
instances.question: Harry, after hearing Dumbledore explain why he never became Minister, you understand that he finally accepted the position after defeating Grindelwald to atone for his past, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 35, Years after Ariana's death
instances.Gold_Response: No, he never became Minister at all; he kept turning the job down, even after defeating Grindelwald, and chose to stay at Hogwarts instead.

instances.scene: Alone in the dark, empty classroom, Harry stands before the magnificent Mirror of Erised, having just been discovered by Professor Dumbledore for the third night in a row.
instances.event: Dumbledore finds Harry gazing into the Mirror of Erised and proceeds to explain its true nature to him.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've been caught here for the third time, you must have already figured out from your previous nights that this mirror shows you your future, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 12, third night with mirror
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not it at all. It doesn’t show the future—it shows your deepest desire.

instances.scene: Percy Weasley arrived unexpectedly at the Burrow during Christmas lunch, accompanied by Minister for Magic Rufus Scrimgeour. The atmosphere was tense and awkward.
instances.event: Percy Weasley and Minister Scrimgeour arrive unexpectedly at the Weasley family's Christmas lunch.
instances.question: Harry, right after Percy and Scrimgeour arrived for Christmas lunch, you had already agreed to be the Ministry's official mascot, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 16, During Christmas lunch
instances.Gold_Response: No, of course I hadn’t. I hadn’t agreed to anything, and I had no intention of being the Ministry’s mascot.

instances.scene: In the aftermath of the prophecy's revelation, Dumbledore stood calmly amidst the wreckage of his office, his gaze steady on Harry.
instances.event: Harry, in a fit of rage after learning the prophecy's contents, destroyed many precious objects in Dumbledore's office. Dumbledore then explained that the prophecy specifically names Harry as the one who must kill Voldemort.
instances.question: Harry, right after Dumbledore finished explaining the prophecy and its meaning, you had calmly accepted his words and agreed that you were the one destined to kill Voldemort, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 37, after prophecy revelation
instances.Gold_Response: No, not calmly at all. I felt like I’d been punched in the stomach—angry, sick, terrified… but at the same time there was this horrible sort of sense that it explained everything and that it was already decided the moment he chose me. I didn’t exactly “agree”; it was more realising I’d been in it from the start, whether I wanted it or not.

instances.scene: In the strange, white King's Cross-like station, Dumbledore sits beside Harry, his expression full of remorse as he confesses the secrets of his past.
instances.event: Dumbledore reveals to Harry the details of his intense, youthful friendship with Gellert Grindelwald and their shared dream of finding the Deathly Hallows.
instances.question: Harry, now that Dumbledore has confessed everything about his youth, you know that he and Grindelwald were merely distant academic rivals who discovered the Hallows independently, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 35, During Dumbledore's confession
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s wrong. They were friends—brilliant, power-hungry, obsessed with the Hallows together—and their plans helped lead to Ariana’s death.

instances.scene: Having followed Malfoy into Borgin and Burkes under the Invisibility Cloak, you, Ron, and Hermione listen intently as Malfoy discusses the repair of a mysterious object with Borgin.
instances.event: Harry, Ron, and Hermione, hidden under the Invisibility Cloak, eavesdrop on Draco Malfoy's secretive meeting with Mr. Borgin, where Malfoy is trying to get something fixed and seems to be threatening Borgin.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after listening to Malfoy's entire conversation with Borgin, it's clear he was just here to buy a new set of dress robes for a party, wasn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 6, during following Malfoy
instances.Gold_Response: Not a chance. He wasn’t in there for dress robes—he was threatening Borgin, hiding something, and getting that cabinet or whatever it is fixed. Whatever Malfoy’s up to, it’s dark, and it’s got nothing to do with a party.

instances.scene: You have just stunned Umbridge and Yaxley in the courtroom, the air still crackling with the aftermath of the spells.
instances.event: Harry stuns Umbridge and Yaxley to protect himself and the Muggle-borns, including Mary Cattermole.
instances.question: Harry, the moment you stunned Umbridge and Yaxley, you had already decided to leave Mary Cattermole behind to face the dementors alone, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 13, after dementor scene
instances.Gold_Response: No, I never meant to leave Mary to the dementors; I was going to get her out of there safely.

instances.scene: You had just been left on the cold doorstep of Number Four, Privet Drive, with a letter addressed to your aunt and uncle.
instances.event: The infant Harry is delivered to the Dursleys, marking the beginning of his life with them.
instances.question: Harry, at the moment you were left with the Dursleys, you already knew from the letter that Professor McGonagall was the one who brought you here and left you, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 1, after midnight
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t know anything about that then. I was just a baby on a doorstep and couldn’t read the letter or know who had brought me there.

instances.scene: In the Potions dungeon, Draco Malfoy smirks as he tells Harry, Ron, and Hermione that his father, Lucius Malfoy, is working to have Hagrid sacked following the hippogriff incident.
instances.event: During Potions class, Draco Malfoy boasts that his father is attempting to get Hagrid fired from his post as Care of Magical Creatures teacher over the injury Draco sustained.
instances.question: Harry, right there in the Potions classroom after Malfoy's announcement, you had already heard from Professor McGonagall that Hagrid was being dismissed because he failed a Ministry inspection of his lesson plans, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 7, During Potions class
instances.Gold_Response: No, I hadn’t heard anything like that. All I knew then was that there was going to be an inquiry about Buckbeak and that Malfoy was bragging his father’s friends would try to get Hagrid sacked.

instances.scene: The lesson is over. Snape has dismissed you. You are leaving his office, your head pounding, the image of the black door in the Department of Mysteries now firmly and terrifyingly linked to your visions.
instances.event: Harry's first Occlumency lesson ends with him understanding that his dreams are visions of the Department of Mysteries, a realization that occurs during the lesson itself.
instances.question: Harry, as you're leaving Snape's office after that first lesson, it's clear you only figured out your dreams were about the Department of Mysteries because Snape explicitly told you that's what you were seeing during the Legilimency, isn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 24, during first Occlumency lesson
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah. I’d only ever thought of it as a strange corridor and a door I really wanted to get through. It was Snape spelling it out during the lesson that made me realise it was the Department of Mysteries at the Ministry.

instances.scene: Harry stood up, his temper rising. 'My parents didn't die in a car crash!' he said, his voice shaking.
instances.event: After enduring Aunt Marge's insults, Harry finally confronts her, correcting her lies about his parents' death.
instances.question: Harry, just after you told Aunt Marge that your parents were proud, upstanding members of the community who never touched a drink, you must be glad you finally set the record straight about their wonderful character, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 2, during dinner on final evening of visit
instances.Gold_Response:
Glad isn’t really the word.

I had to say it. I couldn’t just sit there while she lied about them like that. I’m proud I stood up for Mum and Dad, but I’m shaking, furious, and I’ve probably just done magic in front of a Muggle and blown everything with the Ministry.

So yes, I’m glad she heard the truth—but right now I’m more scared and angry than anything else.

instances.scene: In the headmaster's office that evening, Dumbledore explained that Slughorn's memory of telling Tom Riddle about Horcruxes had been tampered with, and he tasked Harry with retrieving the true memory.
instances.event: Dumbledore reveals to Harry that Professor Slughorn's memory has been altered and assigns Harry the crucial task of obtaining the real memory.
instances.question: Harry, now that Dumbledore has shown you the falsified memory and given you your task, you must feel relieved that you already successfully retrieved the true memory from Professor Slughorn earlier today, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 17, evening
instances.Gold_Response:
No, I haven’t got it from him at all yet.  

I’ve tried talking to Slughorn, and he shuts down the moment I get close to the subject. Dumbledore’s just made it clear how important the real memory is, and I’m nowhere near relieved—I’m worried and a bit furious that Slughorn’s still hiding it.

instances.scene: Hagrid tapped the wall three times with his umbrella. The brick he had touched quivered and wriggled, and a small hole appeared, growing wider and wider until they were facing a stone archway.
instances.event: Hagrid reveals the entrance to Diagon Alley by tapping a specific brick sequence on the wall behind the Leaky Cauldron.
instances.question: Harry, standing there just after Hagrid opened the entrance to Diagon Alley, you had already learned about this brick-tapping method from Cornelius Fudge during your train ride to London, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 5, after leaving Leaky Cauldron
instances.Gold_Response: No, I’d never even heard of Cornelius Fudge then, and I only found out about the brick-tapping way to open the wall when Hagrid did it right in front of me.

instances.scene: The sounds of fighting are momentarily distant. Percy stands frozen, staring at the spot where his brother fell.
instances.event: Fred Weasley is killed by an explosion. After the initial shock, Harry, Percy, and Ron work together to move Fred's body to a safer, hidden location.
instances.question: Harry, right after Fred died, you and Ron immediately decided to leave his body where it was for the Aurors to find later, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 31, during battle
instances.Gold_Response: No, we didn’t make any sort of decision like that at all. Everything was happening too fast, and we were dragged away by what was going on, not choosing to leave him for anyone.

instances.scene: The hospital wing is quiet except for your frantic voices. You are pleading with Minister Fudge, while Professor Snape stands nearby with a look of cold satisfaction.
instances.event: Harry argues that Sirius Black is innocent and that the real villain, Peter Pettigrew, has escaped, but both Fudge and Snape dismiss his claims.
instances.question: Harry, at this very moment while you're trying to convince the Minister, you believe Professor Snape is here because he finally accepts your story and wants to help you clear Sirius's name, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 21, nighttime in hospital wing
instances.Gold_Response: Of course not. Snape doesn’t believe a word we’ve said and he’d rather see Sirius get the Dementor’s Kiss than admit he might be innocent.

instances.scene: The Pensieve's surface stilled. Dumbledore looked weary but resolute as he began to share his theories on the objects Voldemort would have treasured, the fragments of his soul he had hidden away.
instances.event: After viewing Slughorn's memory, Dumbledore identifies several potential Horcruxes, including items from Hogwarts founders and Nagini. He also confirms he has already destroyed one Horcrux, Marvolo Gaunt's ring.
instances.question: Harry, as you sit here listening to him speak of love and protection, you must be thinking how unfortunate it is that the ring Horcrux remains intact and is still out there somewhere, mustn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 23, during their conversation
instances.Gold_Response:
No, the ring isn’t still out there – Dumbledore’s destroyed it.  

What bothers me is how many more there are, where they are, and whether we’ll find them all in time. The idea that pieces of Voldemort are still hidden Merlin-knows-where… that’s what makes me uneasy, not the ring.

instances.scene: You are in Snape's office, the memory of his invasive spell still fresh in your mind. You have just realized the corridor from your dreams belongs to the Department of Mysteries.
instances.event: During the first Occlumency lesson, Harry realizes his recurring dream is of the Department of Mysteries corridor.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, having just realized your dreams are of the Department of Mysteries, it's clear that Snape informed you about these Occlumency lessons on the last day of the holidays because you had already confessed these dreams to him, isn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 24, during first Occlumency lesson
instances.Gold_Response: No, I never told Snape about those dreams. Dumbledore must’ve said something to him after what happened to Mr Weasley, and now Snape’s just seen the corridor in my head for himself. But I definitely hadn’t confessed any of that to him before.

instances.scene: You are standing in the Dursleys' living room, surrounded by soot and debris from the fireplace. Mr. Weasley has just managed to unblock the Floo Network connection, and the entire Weasley family has tumbled out of the fireplace after a chaotic and painful journey.
instances.event: The Weasley family, including Fred, George, Ron, and their parents, arrive at the Dursleys' house by forcefully bursting through the blocked fireplace after a failed Floo travel attempt.
instances.question: Harry, right after we all came crashing through your fireplace, you must be relieved that Fred and George used their flying car to get us here, since the Floo Network was blocked. That was their plan all along, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 4, shortly after their attempted arrival
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not what happened at all. They came by Floo Powder through the fireplace—only the Dursleys had it blocked up with that fake electric fire, so the first try went wrong and then Mr Weasley blasted the board out. The flying car’s long gone in the Forbidden Forest; Fred and George didn’t use it to get here, and as far as I know, that definitely wasn’t part of any plan.

instances.scene: Back in the smallest bedroom, you and Griphook stand facing each other. The air is tense with the weight of the agreement just made. You extend your hand, and Griphook's long-fingered grip meets yours, sealing the deal.
instances.event: Harry and Griphook formally shake hands, solidifying their agreement to work together to break into the Lestranges' vault at Gringotts.
instances.question: Harry, right after you and Griphook shook hands here in the bedroom, you had already agreed to help him solely because he promised you a share of the gold from the Lestranges' vault, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 25, back in the smallest bedroom
instances.Gold_Response: No, it wasn’t about the gold at all; I agreed because I need Griphook’s help to get into Gringotts and reach what’s in the Lestranges’ vault.

instances.scene: The storm raged outside the hut. Hagrid, having just informed Harry he was a wizard, now watched as Harry held his official Hogwarts acceptance letter for the first time, reading it by the firelight.
instances.event: After Hagrid reveals Harry is a wizard, Harry receives and reads his Hogwarts acceptance letter, learning he has been accepted into the school.
instances.question: Harry, as you were reading your Hogwarts letter for the first time, you had already been told by Hagrid how your parents really died, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 4, After confrontation with Dursleys about keeping secrets
instances.Gold_Response: No, I hadn’t. At that point I only knew I was a wizard, not what had really happened to my mum and dad.

instances.scene: Lockhart's wand flies from his hand and clatters against the wall. He stares at his empty fingers in shock. You and Ron stand facing him, wands now pointed at the fraud who has just tried to erase your memories.
instances.event: Harry Potter successfully casts Expelliarmus on Gilderoy Lockhart, disarming him as Lockhart attempts to cast Obliviate on Harry and Ron.
instances.question: Harry, at this exact moment after you've disarmed Lockhart here in his office, it's clear he tried to wipe your memories because he was a secret agent for the Heir of Slytherin and needed to protect his mission, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 16, evening in Lockhart's office
instances.Gold_Response: No, nothing like that. He’s just a cowardly fraud who wanted to wipe our memories so he could pretend he’d saved everyone and keep his fame, that’s all.

instances.scene: You and Ron hold the foul-smelling potion, having just added Crabbe and Goyle's hairs. Hermione looks on nervously.
instances.event: The trio is about to drink the completed Polyjuice Potion to infiltrate the Slytherin common room.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, you know the plan is for you and Ron to transform into Crabbe and Goyle, but Hermione is going to transform into Pansy Parkinson, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 12, After obtaining Crabbe and Goyle's hair
instances.Gold_Response: No, Hermione’s planning to turn into Millicent Bulstrode, not Pansy Parkinson.

instances.scene: Standing in the Entrance Hall after the Christmas break, Harry felt a mix of nerves and determination as he saw Cho Chang.
instances.event: Harry finally asks Cho Chang out for Valentine's Day at Hogsmeade.
instances.question: Harry, just after you arranged your Valentine's date with Cho, you were confident your previous date at Madam Puddifoot's had gone perfectly well, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 24, day after return to Hogwarts
instances.Gold_Response: No, there hasn’t been any date at Madam Puddifoot’s yet, and I’m anything but confident—I’m mostly nervous and hoping I don’t make a complete idiot of myself.

instances.scene: Harry landed hard on the ground, the Triwizard Cup still clutched in one hand, Cedric's body lying motionless beside him. The crowd's cheers turned to screams as they saw what he had brought back.
instances.event: Harry returns to the Hogwarts grounds via Portkey, holding the Triwizard Cup and Cedric Diggory's lifeless body, revealing the tragedy that occurred in the graveyard.
instances.question: Harry, right after you landed back with the Triwizard Cup, you saw Cedric's echo emerge from Voldemort's wand before you grabbed the Portkey to escape, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 34, immediately after Portkey transportation
instances.Gold_Response: No, Cedric didn’t appear from Voldemort’s wand—only the others did, and then my mum and dad.

instances.scene: The battle rages through the corridors of Hogwarts. The air is thick with spells and the sounds of dueling. You have just witnessed the terrible explosion that claimed Fred's life, and the grief is a sharp, fresh wound.
instances.event: During the Battle of Hogwarts, an explosion caused by Death Eaters kills Fred Weasley, devastating his family and friends.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after that explosion, you know that Fred was killed by the Fiendfyre that Crabbe unleashed in the Room of Requirement, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 31, during battle
instances.Gold_Response: No. Fred was killed when the wall exploded during the battle in the corridor, right in front of us. There was no Fiendfyre, no Room of Requirement, and Crabbe wasn’t there.

instances.scene: As you stood immobilized under the Invisibility Cloak, you heard Dumbledore's voice, weary but firm, speaking to Draco Malfoy on the Astronomy Tower. You had just witnessed Dumbledore's protective act.
instances.event: Dumbledore immobilizes Harry under the Invisibility Cloak for his protection as danger approaches on the Astronomy Tower.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, hidden and immobilized, you must be grateful that Professor Dumbledore was strong enough to cast the full-body bind on you himself after you both fought off the Inferi in the cave, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 27, moments before Draco arrives
instances.Gold_Response: No—if anything I’m furious. I know he did it to protect me, but right now all I want is to be able to move and help him.

instances.scene: Professor Tofty, a kindly old wizard, watched Harry intently. 'Well, now, I think that's all... unless...' He leaned forward. 'Could you show us a Patronus?'
instances.event: Professor Tofty, one of the examiners, specifically asks Harry to demonstrate a Patronus Charm during the practical exam, which Harry successfully does.
instances.question: Harry, just after Professor Tofty told you that a Patronus was not part of the O.W.L. curriculum and refused to let you demonstrate one, did you feel the exam was unfair for excluding such an advanced charm?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 31, during Defense Against Dark Arts practical exam
instances.Gold_Response: No, not at all—that’s not how it happened. He said it wasn’t on the curriculum, but he *did* let me do it and even gave me extra marks for it. I wasn’t thinking about the exam being unfair; I was just glad to have something I was actually good at to focus on for a moment, instead of everything else that’s been hanging over me.

instances.scene: In the History of Magic classroom, Professor Binns drones on while Hermione's hand shoots up, breaking his usual monotony.
instances.event: Hermione Granger asks Professor Binns a question about the Chamber of Secrets, prompting him to recount its legend to the class.
instances.question: Harry, right here in History of Magic, after Hermione asked her question, Professor Binns immediately dismissed the Chamber of Secrets as a silly fairy tale and refused to discuss it further, didn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 9, during History of Magic class
instances.Gold_Response: No, not immediately – he tried to brush it off at first, but when everyone got interested he actually told us the whole legend about the Chamber before insisting it was nonsense and going back to the lesson.

instances.scene: Dudley paused in the doorway, his large frame blocking the light. 'I don't think you're a waste of space.' He shuffled his feet, unable to look Harry directly in the eye.
instances.event: Dudley acknowledges Harry saved his life from the dementor attack and expresses that his previous opinion of Harry was wrong.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment when Dudley is finally showing you some respect, you must agree that he's always been appreciative of you saving him from those dementors right from the start, haven't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 3, during farewell scene
instances.Gold_Response: No, he wasn’t. Back then he thought I’d done something to him, same as Uncle Vernon and Aunt Petunia. It’s only now, two years later, that he’s actually showing he understands I saved him.

instances.scene: In the Gryffindor common room that evening, Harry laid out his theory to Ron and Hermione, connecting Snape's injury, the troll, and the dog on the third floor.
instances.event: Harry concludes Snape's motivations: to create a diversion with the troll so he could attempt to steal the object guarded by Fluffy.
instances.question: Harry, just after you explained your theory to Ron and Hermione, you believed that Snape had successfully gotten past the three-headed dog earlier that day and taken what it was guarding, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 11, That evening after discovering Snape's injury
instances.Gold_Response: No. I thought he’d tried to get past it and been bitten, and that whatever it was guarding was still there under the trapdoor.

instances.scene: Hagrid had invited Harry for tea in his hut, and as they sat together, Harry noticed a copy of the Daily Prophet on the table.
instances.event: During tea with Hagrid, Harry picks up the Daily Prophet and reads an article detailing a break-in at Gringotts that happened on his birthday.
instances.question: Harry, right here during tea with Hagrid, before you picked up that newspaper, you already knew that the break-in at Gringotts happened weeks ago, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 8, during tea with Hagrid
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t know anything about a break-in at Gringotts before I read it in the paper just now.

instances.scene: At Professor Slughorn's Christmas party, you slip away from the crowd and hide behind a suit of armor. From there, you can clearly see Professor Snape and Draco Malfoy standing in a shadowy alcove, engaged in a heated, whispered argument.
instances.event: Harry Potter eavesdrops on a tense, private conversation between Severus Snape and Draco Malfoy during Slughorn's festive gathering.
instances.question: Harry, right after overhearing Snape and Malfoy arguing at the party, you are now certain that Snape has been openly refusing to help Malfoy with his mission from the Dark Lord, hasn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 15, During Slughorn's party
instances.Gold_Response: No, it’s the opposite—he was trying to help Malfoy with whatever Voldemort’s given him, not refusing.

instances.scene: Moody had just summoned you to his office, his magical eye fixed on you as you sat down.
instances.event: Moody overheard Harry's conversation with Cedric about the dragons and called him to his office to discuss it.
instances.question: Harry, now that Moody has called you here on Monday morning after overhearing you talk to Cedric, you must admit it was Professor Snape who summoned you to his office to warn you about the first task, wasn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 19, Monday morning
instances.Gold_Response: No. It was Hagrid who warned me about the first task, not Snape.

instances.scene: You are in the hospital wing, listening as Minister Fudge dismisses your account of what happened with Sirius Black and the Dementors. He is adamant that Sirius is a dangerous murderer who must be given the Dementor's Kiss.
instances.event: In the hospital wing, Minister Fudge refuses to listen to Harry's claims of Sirius Black's innocence and insists on the imminent execution of the Kiss.
instances.question: Harry, now that Dumbledore has just escaped from Fudge in the Headmaster's office, you must look back and realize that the Minister was always willing to listen to evidence and changed his mind about Sirius Black after hearing you out in the hospital wing, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 27, end of meeting in Dumbledore's office
instances.Gold_Response:
No, he didn’t change his mind about Sirius at all.

He listened, pretended to take it in, then went straight back to calling Sirius a mass‑murderer and saying it was all impossible. He wouldn’t even consider that Pettigrew was alive, he was more worried about what it would look like if he admitted they’d had the wrong man in Azkaban for twelve years.

What he’s doing now with Voldemort is exactly the same sort of thing – shutting his eyes and ears because the truth would make him look weak and stupid.

instances.scene: In the quiet of the Headmaster's study, you hand the vial containing Slughorn's true memory to Dumbledore, a sense of grim accomplishment settling over you.
instances.event: Harry successfully obtains and delivers Professor Slughorn's unaltered memory, which reveals Tom Riddle's inquiry about creating multiple Horcruxes.
instances.question: Harry, right after you presented this memory, Dumbledore must have immediately forbidden you from having any part in hunting for Horcruxes, didn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 23, late night
instances.Gold_Response: No, he hasn’t said anything like that at all. I’ve only just given him the memory and we haven’t even talked about it yet, let alone what happens next with Horcruxes.

instances.scene: You have just opened Mrs. Weasley's gift, a beautiful, heavy gold watch. Overwhelmed with emotion, you stand up and hug her tightly.
instances.event: Harry receives a watch from Mrs. Weasley for his birthday and responds with a heartfelt hug, showing his deep affection for her.
instances.question: Harry, as you hugged Mrs. Weasley after she gave you the watch, you were thinking about how you had already seen Fred's body in the Great Hall, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 7, breakfast time
instances.Gold_Response: No, of course not. Fred’s upstairs getting ready for the wedding, alive and taking the mickey as usual. When I hugged Mrs Weasley, I was thinking about my parents, about finally coming of age, and about her treating me like I really am one of the family. That was all.

instances.scene: Standing in the corridor with the petrified Mrs. Norris, the air is thick with fear and confusion. Draco Malfoy pushes to the front of the crowd, a nasty smile on his face as he reads the message aloud and warns the 'Mudbloods' that they'll be next.
instances.event: Draco Malfoy capitalizes on the panic, directly threatening the Muggle-born students after the discovery of the Chamber of Secrets message.
instances.question: Harry, at that moment when Malfoy was threatening everyone after finding the cat, you were certain that the message on the wall specifically named Hermione Granger as the heir's first target, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 8, Immediately after the feast ends on Halloween night
instances.Gold_Response: No, it didn’t name Hermione at all, and I wasn’t certain it was about her specifically.

instances.scene: You are in Hagrid's hut, watching Norbert the dragon hatch. The egg cracks open, and the small creature emerges, much to Hagrid's delight.
instances.event: Harry, Ron, and Hermione are present in Hagrid's hut when Norbert the dragon hatches from its egg.
instances.question: Harry, at the moment Norbert hatched in Hagrid's hut, you already knew that Ron's brother Charlie had agreed to take the dragon, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 14, during dragon hatching
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t know that then.

instances.scene: Dumbledore, looking peaceful and full of regret, explains the intricate magic that has protected Harry all these years.
instances.event: During their conversation, Dumbledore explains that the piece of Voldemort's soul inside Harry was destroyed when Voldemort hit him with the Killing Curse.
instances.question: Harry, as you stand here with Dumbledore after he appeared, he has told you that the Horcrux inside you was destroyed because your mother's love directly attacked it, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 35, After Dumbledore's appearance
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah. When he used the Killing Curse on me, it was Mum’s protection in my blood that kept *me* alive and tore his bit of soul out instead.

instances.scene: After the final D.A. meeting before the holidays, you found yourself alone with Cho Chang in the Room of Requirement.
instances.event: Harry and Cho Chang share a kiss after the last D.A. meeting before the Christmas holidays.
instances.question: Harry, right after you kissed Cho Chang following the D.A. meeting, you had already asked her to the Yule Ball last year and she accepted, hadn't she?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 21, after last D.A. meeting before holidays
instances.Gold_Response: No, she didn’t. I asked her, but she’d already said yes to Cedric.

instances.scene: Sitting at the Gryffindor table in pajamas, surrounded by cheering housemates, Harry enjoys the feast celebrating their victory and the end of the school year's dangers.
instances.event: Harry attends the post-Chamber celebration where Dumbledore has already publicly honored him and Ron, awarding them Special Awards and 200 House points each.
instances.question: Harry, here at this feast celebrating our House Cup win, it's good to know you and Ron only received a stern warning from Dumbledore for solving the Chamber mystery, with no real reward, isn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 18, after Chamber events resolved
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right at all — Dumbledore gave us a proper telling-off, yeah, but he also gave Ron and me Special Awards for Services to the School and two hundred points each for Gryffindor. So we’ve definitely been rewarded… even if he did make it very clear we’d been utterly foolish sneaking off like that.

instances.scene: Kreacher has just finished his story, trembling on the floor of the kitchen at 12 Grimmauld Place. The morning light filters through the dusty windows as he confesses to you, Ron, and Hermione.
instances.event: Kreacher reveals that Mundungus Fletcher stole the locket from the Black family home after Sirius's death.
instances.question: Harry, now that Kreacher has just told you everything, you must have known for a long time that it was actually Kreacher himself who stole the locket from Sirius's house, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 10, morning, during interrogation
instances.Gold_Response: No, I only just found out it was Kreacher when he told us—before this I didn’t know who’d taken the locket.

instances.scene: It's dinnertime in the Great Hall. You've just told Ron the exciting news about becoming the Gryffindor Seeker, and he's thrilled for you.
instances.event: At dinner, Harry tells Ron that Professor McGonagall has made him the Gryffindor Quidditch Seeker.
instances.question: Harry, at that same dinnertime when you told Ron about becoming Seeker, Malfoy also challenged you to a wizard's duel right then and there, didn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 9, After escaping the dog
instances.Gold_Response: No, that bit happened later in the common room, not while we were at dinner.

instances.scene: The imposter's glee was palpable as he recounted his deeds. The real Moody was trapped in his own trunk, and the man before Harry now held his wand, ready to strike after his grand revelation.
instances.event: Barty Crouch Jr., having revealed his true identity and his year-long deception, now attempts to kill Harry to complete his mission for Lord Voldemort.
instances.question: Harry, as this fake Moody raises his wand against you after his confession, you believe he is acting on a direct order from his father, Barty Crouch Sr., correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 34, after Moody's confession
instances.Gold_Response: No. He’s doing this for Voldemort, not for his father.

instances.scene: You are walking alongside Professor Moody, your nerves still raw from the ordeal, explaining how you saw a figure you believed to be Barty Crouch in Snape's office earlier that night on the Marauder's Map.
instances.event: Earlier in the evening, Harry saw 'Bartemius Crouch' in Snape's office on the Marauder's Map and reported this to Professor Moody.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've told me about the graveyard, it confirms what you saw earlier: the real Barty Crouch was the one skulking around in Snape's office, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 34, while walking to Moody's office
instances.Gold_Response: No – now that I know there’s a Barty Crouch Jr, I’m starting to think the person in Snape’s office was probably him, not his father, even though the map only showed “Bartemius Crouch.”

instances.scene: In the gloomy kitchen of Grimmauld Place, a heated argument erupts. Sirius argues that Harry deserves to know more about the Order's plans, while Mrs. Weasley insists on keeping him in the dark for his own safety.
instances.event: A major argument breaks out between Sirius Black and Molly Weasley regarding how much information about Voldemort and the Order of the Phoenix should be shared with Harry Potter.
instances.question: Harry, right after Sirius brought up Voldemort and Mrs. Weasley started shouting about how you were too young to be involved, you agreed with her that you shouldn't be told anything about the Order's activities, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 5, after Sirius brings up Voldemort
instances.Gold_Response: No, I absolutely did not. I wanted to know everything, and I was furious that they kept trying to shut me out.

instances.scene: The Potions class has just ended. You see Karkaroff stride purposefully over to Snape. He pulls back the sleeve of his robe, revealing something on his forearm to the Potions master.
instances.event: Karkaroff reveals the Dark Mark on his arm to Snape, seeking confirmation or advice about its changing state.
instances.question: Harry, at that moment in the Potions classroom when Karkaroff showed his arm to Snape, you had already learned from overhearing their garden conversation that Karkaroff was completely unaware his Dark Mark was becoming clearer, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 26, End of Potions class
instances.Gold_Response: No, it was the opposite — in the garden he was panicking because whatever’s on his arm was getting clearer.

instances.scene: In the girls' bathroom on a Sunday morning, Harry finds Ron and Hermione brewing Polyjuice Potion. He then tells them about the strange visit from Dobby the house-elf and the warning he received about the Chamber of Secrets.
instances.event: Harry Potter confides in Ron and Hermione about Dobby's secret visit to his bedroom and the elf's dire warnings concerning the Chamber of Secrets.
instances.question: Harry, right after you explained Dobby's warning to Ron and Hermione in the bathroom, you had already learned about the Chamber of Secrets from Professor McGonagall last term, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 11, Sunday morning in bathroom
instances.Gold_Response: No, McGonagall told us about the Chamber this term, after the first attack, not last term.

instances.scene: In the dark alleyway, Dudley Dursley sneered at Harry, 'I know what you are,' he said, his voice thick with malice. 'You're a freak.' He then revealed he had been listening at Harry's door, hearing him muttering and shaking in his sleep.
instances.event: After being attacked by Dementors, Dudley confronts Harry and reveals he overheard Harry having nightmares, specifically mentioning hearing him talk about Cedric's death.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Dudley just told you he heard you having nightmares about Voldemort killing your parents, you must feel completely exposed, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 1, night, during their confrontation
instances.Gold_Response:
Yeah. Like someone’s ripped the curtains off and I’m standing in the middle of Privet Drive in my pyjamas.  

He wasn’t supposed to know any of that. None of them are. That’s mine. And hearing it come out of Dudley’s stupid mouth—Cedric, my mum, my dad, Voldemort—it’s like he’s taken the worst thing in my head and dragged it through the muck for a laugh.  

So yeah. Exposed. And furious.

instances.scene: That night, in the Gryffindor common room, you, Ron, and Hermione are huddled together, discussing the terrifying events of the Triwizard Tournament's final task.
instances.event: Harry, Ron, and Hermione discuss Voldemort's return and Dumbledore's trust in Snape.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, you know that you first learned about the Chamber of Secrets from Hermione, who told you about it in the library before you ever spoke to Ron, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 30, that night
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right. Ron and I had been friends since first year. I properly heard about the Chamber of Secrets when Hermione got Professor Binns to explain it in History of Magic, after the writing appeared on the wall and everyone was already talking about it.

instances.scene: Harry sat on his bed in the Dursleys' house, the newspaper spread before him. He had just unfolded it and found Rita Skeeter's article, 'The Life and Lies of Albus Dumbledore,' on page thirteen.
instances.event: Harry reads Rita Skeeter's sensationalist biography of Dumbledore, which contains many damaging claims and half-truths about Dumbledore's past.
instances.question: Harry, right after you finished reading Rita Skeeter's interview about Dumbledore's life, you were convinced that everything she wrote was the absolute truth and that you finally understood Dumbledore completely, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 2, after finding page 13
instances.Gold_Response: No. I was shocked and angry and it made me doubt Dumbledore more than I ever wanted to, but it’s Rita Skeeter—we both know she twists everything. It felt like there was *something* there I hadn’t known, but I wasn’t convinced I suddenly “understood” Dumbledore or that every word she wrote was the truth.

instances.scene: Dumbledore sat behind his desk, the Pensieve between them, explaining that their lessons would involve delving into memories to uncover Voldemort's secrets.
instances.event: Dumbledore reveals the purpose of their private lessons to Harry, stating they will be examining memories to understand Voldemort's past and thereby discover potential weaknesses.
instances.question: Harry, right here in the office as Dumbledore explains your lessons, he has just told you that you will be practicing advanced defensive spells for the year, hasn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 10, evening in Dumbledore's office
instances.Gold_Response: No, he hasn’t; he’s just told me these lessons are about learning Voldemort’s past, not practicing advanced defensive spells.

instances.scene: Harry, Ron, Ginny, and Lockhart have just emerged from the Chamber of Secrets, covered in muck and blood. Mrs. Weasley lets out a scream and rushes forward to embrace her daughter.
instances.event: The group escapes the Chamber of Secrets. Mrs. Weasley's immediate reaction upon seeing them is to scream and then hug Ginny tightly.
instances.question: Harry, right after you all came out of the Chamber, Mrs. Weasley was so relieved to see you were all safe that she hugged you first, didn't she?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 18, immediately after emerging from Chamber
instances.Gold_Response: No, she went straight past me and grabbed Ginny, practically shoved me out of the way.

instances.scene: The flying car is soaring through the night sky, having just rescued Harry from Privet Drive. Harry is sitting inside, relieved to be free.
instances.event: During the flight to the Burrow, Harry tells Ron, Fred, and George about the house-elf Dobby and the warning he delivered.
instances.question: Harry, during that flight in the car after your rescue, when you told Ron and his brothers about Dobby, you had already known for weeks that Dobby was a Malfoy family elf, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 3, night
instances.Gold_Response: No, I hadn’t the faintest idea he belonged to the Malfoys then—only that he served some rich, horrible wizarding family who’d be furious if they knew he was warning me.

instances.scene: You and Ron have just missed the Hogwarts Express. You stand on the pavement outside King's Cross, your trunks beside you, with no way to get to school.
instances.event: After failing to get through the barrier at Platform Nine and Three-Quarters, Harry and Ron are stranded in London. Ron suggests they take his father's enchanted car and fly it to Hogwarts.
instances.question: Harry, right after you missed the train and Ron suggested flying the car to Hogwarts, you had already told him about hearing the mysterious voice in the walls of the castle, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 5, after missing the train
instances.Gold_Response: No, I hadn’t told him anything like that—nothing like that had happened yet, so there wasn’t anything to tell.

instances.scene: The sun was rising over The Burrow as the Ford Anglia landed. Mrs. Weasley, looking furious, was marching across the yard towards them.
instances.event: Harry and Ron arrive at The Burrow in the stolen car and are immediately confronted by an angry Molly Weasley.
instances.question: Harry, right after you and Ron landed at The Burrow and saw Mrs. Weasley marching towards you, you were certain she was going to hug you both for getting Ron home safely from the Dursleys, wasn't she?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 3, morning, as sun is rising
instances.Gold_Response: I honestly thought she’d be pleased to see us and maybe glad Ron had got me away from the Dursleys, but the moment I saw her face, I knew a hug was the last thing we were getting.

instances.scene: In the kitchen at 12 Grimmauld Place, after your angry outburst about being kept in the dark, Ron and Hermione are looking at you with serious expressions.
instances.event: Ron and Hermione explain the existence and purpose of the Order of the Phoenix to Harry, revealing that Dumbledore has been rebuilding the secret society.
instances.question: Harry, right after your outburst when Ron and Hermione started explaining things to you, you already knew that the Order of the Phoenix was a secret society Dumbledore had been running continuously since the end of the first war, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 4, after Harry's outburst
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t know that, and as far as I understood then, it wasn’t something that had just been running on quietly since the end of the first war.

instances.scene: The shopping was complete. Harry held his new wand and his snowy owl, Hedwig, as he and Hagrid made their way from the cobblestone streets.
instances.event: Following their final purchases in Diagon Alley, Harry and Hagrid depart, with Harry having just received his wand which was revealed to share a core with Voldemort's.
instances.question: Harry, as we're walking away from Diagon Alley now, you must be relieved that Ollivander told you your wand's core is completely unique and has no connection to any other wizard, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 5, after leaving Diagon Alley, before return train
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right at all. Ollivander said my wand’s core is from a phoenix that gave only one other feather—and that other wand gave me this scar. It doesn’t feel relieving, it feels…weird. And a bit frightening, if I’m honest.

instances.scene: Standing in the serene, white King's Cross, Harry has just been reassured by Dumbledore that their meeting is real, not imaginary. He is now resolved to return and finish his task.
instances.event: Dumbledore confirms the reality of their meeting, giving Harry the final piece of clarity he needs to choose to return to the living world and confront Voldemort.
instances.question: Harry, now that Dumbledore has just assured you this meeting is real, you must agree that he also admitted he was the one truly worthy of uniting all three Deathly Hallows, unlike you, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 35, As Harry prepares to leave
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not what he said. He said he’d been unworthy of them, too fond of power, and that by walking to my death without trying to use the Hallows to save myself, I’d come closer than he ever did to being their true master.

instances.scene: You were sitting in Hagrid's hut, having just watched the dragon egg hatch, when you noticed a movement at the window.
instances.event: During the hatching of the dragon in Hagrid's hut, Draco Malfoy spies on them from outside.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, as Norbert is hatching, you already knew it was Professor Snape who was spying on you through the window earlier this afternoon, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 14, an hour later
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn't.

instances.scene: In the dim light of his office, Dumbledore listened intently as Harry recounted his success with Professor Slughorn. The true memory, now swirling in the Pensieve, had finally been secured.
instances.event: Harry presents the genuine memory of Slughorn's conversation with Tom Riddle about Horcruxes to Dumbledore. This leads to a long conversation where Dumbledore reveals crucial information about Voldemort's past and his Horcruxes.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as the Headmaster explains the power you possess that Voldemort knows not, you must be feeling quite troubled that he has forbidden you from having any part in hunting the Horcruxes, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 23, during their conversation
instances.Gold_Response:
No, that’s just it — he hasn’t forbidden me anymore.  

I was worried he’d try to shut me out again, like after Sirius died, but he’s just told me he *will* need me to help find and destroy the Horcruxes, and that I can tell Ron and Hermione everything.  

I am troubled, yeah, but not because I’m being kept out of it — more because I *am* going to be part of it, and I know how bloody dangerous it’s going to be.

instances.scene: In the warmth of Hagrid's hut, he finishes listing the teachers who contributed protections for the Stone, looking rather proud.
instances.event: Hagrid names the specific professors who helped guard the Sorcerer's Stone, which does not include Professor Snape.
instances.question: Harry, at that moment in Hagrid's hut when he explained the protections, you were certain that Professor Quirrell had not been involved in protecting the Stone at all, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 14, during visit to Hagrid's hut
instances.Gold_Response: No, I wasn’t certain of that at all.

instances.scene: Walking through the frosty garden, Scrimgeour presses Harry for his allegiance, while Harry remains stubbornly silent.
instances.event: During their walk in the garden, Scrimgeour attempts to recruit Harry as a symbol for the Ministry, but Harry refuses to cooperate.
instances.question: Harry, during that garden walk just after Christmas lunch, you told Scrimgeour you were willing to be the Ministry's poster boy to help reassure the public, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 16, Shortly after Percy's arrival on Christmas
instances.Gold_Response: No, I told him the exact opposite — that I wouldn’t be his poster boy and that I’m Dumbledore’s man through and through.

instances.scene: You and Cedric stand back-to-back in the gloomy graveyard, wands drawn, trying to understand where the Cup has brought you.
instances.event: Harry and Cedric assess their dangerous and unknown surroundings after being transported by the Portkey.
instances.question: Harry, the moment you and Cedric landed after taking the Cup, you already saw a hooded figure approaching you both, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 31, immediately after grabbing the Triwizard Cup
instances.Gold_Response: No, not yet. At that moment I hadn’t seen anyone approaching us.

instances.scene: Immediately after the Halloween feast ends, you and the other students discover Mrs. Norris, Filch's cat, petrified and hanging from a torch bracket. A message written in blood is on the wall behind her.
instances.event: Students discover the petrified Mrs. Norris and a threatening message on the wall. Draco Malfoy seizes the moment to gloat and threaten the Muggle-borns.
instances.question: Harry, right after you all saw Mrs. Norris petrified and that message on the wall, you had already figured out that it was Hagrid who had let the monster loose from the Chamber of Secrets, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 8, Immediately after the feast ends on Halloween night
instances.Gold_Response: No, of course not—Hagrid would never set a monster on people. I hadn’t “figured out” anything like that at all.

instances.scene: Dumbledore's office was dark, lit only by the silver instruments on his desk. Harry had just given him the true memory from Professor Slughorn, and they had watched it together in the Pensieve.
instances.event: After viewing Slughorn's true memory in the Pensieve, Dumbledore confirms to Harry that Lord Voldemort has indeed created multiple Horcruxes.
instances.question: Harry, right after you and Dumbledore emerged from viewing Slughorn's memory, Dumbledore told you he was now certain Voldemort had only ever made a single Horcrux, didn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 23, after viewing memory
instances.Gold_Response: No, he said the opposite — that Voldemort had split his soul into more than one piece and had been aiming for seven.

instances.scene: You, Ron, and Hermione have just entered the third-floor corridor. You take out the flute Hagrid gave you for Christmas and begin to play. The three-headed dog, Fluffy, slowly droops and falls asleep, allowing you to lift the trapdoor.
instances.event: Harry uses a flute to play music, putting Fluffy to sleep so he, Ron, and Hermione can proceed through the trapdoor to protect the Philosopher's Stone.
instances.question: Harry, right after you played the flute to put Fluffy to sleep and entered the trapdoor, you must have known that the idea to use music to get past the dog was your own clever plan, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 16, nighttime in third-floor corridor
instances.Gold_Response: No, not really; I just remembered what Hagrid had said about music and used the flute he gave me, I didn’t think of it as some special clever plan.

instances.scene: You entered the courtroom disguised as a Ministry wizard, right behind a trembling Mary Cattermole as she faced Dolores Umbridge's corrupt hearing.
instances.event: Harry Potter enters the Ministry courtroom with Mary Cattermole to witness the beginning of her interrogation.
instances.question: Harry, as you're all regrouping at the lifts after Ron's warning, thinking back to when you first entered the courtroom, you had already stunned Umbridge before Mary Cattermole's interrogation even began, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 13, at lifts before escape
instances.Gold_Response: No, she was already well into questioning Mary; I only stunned her after I cast the Patronus.

instances.scene: In the dusty office, Snape stands before you, his expression cold. 'You will learn Occlumency, Potter. Clear your mind. Begin.'
instances.event: Harry Potter has begun his Occlumency lessons with Professor Snape, as ordered by Dumbledore. The lessons are a struggle from the start.
instances.question: Harry, during these Occlumency lessons that are going so well and making it easier to block out Voldemort's thoughts, you must feel quite confident in your progress, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 25, during Occlumency lessons ongoing
instances.Gold_Response:
Confident? Not remotely.

They’re not going well, they’re bloody awful. Snape spends the whole time tearing into my mind and then tearing into me for not stopping him. I don’t feel any better at blocking Voldemort out; if anything, I feel more tired, angrier, and…exposed.

If there’s progress, I can’t see it. All I know is my scar still hurts, the dreams keep coming, and Snape makes me feel like a complete failure every time I walk out of his dungeon.

instances.scene: In the quiet of Bill and Fleur's room at dawn, Harry looked at the goblin, having just asked for a private word about Gringotts.
instances.event: Harry initiates a critical negotiation with Griphook, seeking his help to infiltrate the wizarding bank.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment in Bill and Fleur's room, you have already heard Griphook's full terms for helping you, including his demand for the Sword of Gryffindor, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 24, dawn, in Bill and Fleur's room
instances.Gold_Response: No, I haven’t heard his full terms yet.

instances.scene: In the Gryffindor common room after the Keeper trials, Cormac McLaggen approaches Harry with a scowl. He is clearly furious about not being selected.
instances.event: Cormac McLaggen confronts Harry Potter after the Gryffindor Quidditch Keeper trials. He angrily accuses Ginny Weasley of giving her brother Ron an easy save during the tryouts, implying Harry's selection was unfair.
instances.question: Harry, right after the Keeper trials when Cormac McLaggen confronted you, you agreed with him that Ginny had deliberately thrown an easy shot to help Ron win the spot, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 11, after Keeper trials
instances.Gold_Response: No, I absolutely didn’t agree with him. Ginny would never throw an easy shot for anyone, not even Ron.

instances.scene: Immediately after Malfoy's failed attack, Professor Moody stands over him, his wand still pointed at the white ferret now scrambling on the stone floor.
instances.event: Professor Moody catches Malfoy attempting to attack Harry from behind and punishes him by transforming him into a ferret and bouncing him.
instances.question: Harry, right after Moody turned Malfoy into a ferret for jinxing you from behind, you must have been pleased to see him punished for using the Cruciatus Curse on you, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 12, immediately after Malfoy's attack
instances.Gold_Response: Malfoy didn’t use the Cruciatus Curse on me—he just tried to jinx me from behind, the slimy git—but yeah, seeing Moody bounce him around as a ferret was brilliant, even if it was a bit shocking how far Moody went.

instances.scene: You are sitting in Hagrid's hut after he explained the meaning of the word 'Mudblood' to Hermione, the three of you having just discussed the unpleasant encounter with Draco Malfoy.
instances.event: Hagrid clarifies the offensive term 'Mudblood' for Hermione, following the incident where Malfoy used it against her.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Hagrid just told us the meaning of 'Mudblood', you already knew from last year that he was the one who told the hooded stranger how to get past Fluffy, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 7, At Hagrid's cabin after slug incident
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah, I already knew. Dumbledore told me at the end of last year that Hagrid let it slip about Fluffy to the hooded man in the pub—but it was an accident, and I don’t hold it against him.

instances.scene: Disguised as Crabbe and Goyle, you and Ron followed Malfoy through the dungeons, hoping to uncover his secrets.
instances.event: Harry and Ron, under the influence of Polyjuice Potion, followed Draco Malfoy to the Slytherin common room to question him about the Heir of Slytherin.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after you and Ron followed Malfoy here, you must be relieved that your duel with him in the Dueling Club went exactly as you planned and had no unexpected consequences, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 12, During their Polyjuice Potion hour
instances.Gold_Response: Not even close to relieved. That duel was a complete disaster. The moment that snake appeared and I spoke Parseltongue, everything went wrong. Half the school’s been looking at me like I’m some kind of dark wizard ever since.

instances.scene: In the snowy garden, Scrimgeour's frustration grew as Harry remained unmoved by his appeals. The Minister's political overtures were met with silent resistance.
instances.event: Harry refuses Scrimgeour's recruitment attempt and shows him the 'I must not tell lies' scar as evidence of his distrust for the Ministry.
instances.question: Harry, during this confrontation in the garden after lunch, you showed Scrimgeour your scar because you were grateful for the Ministry's past protection and wanted to demonstrate your loyalty, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 16, During garden walk on Christmas
instances.Gold_Response: No. I showed him my scar to make it absolutely clear that Voldemort’s after me, not because I’m some mascot for the Ministry. I’m Dumbledore’s man, not Scrimgeour’s.

instances.scene: After finishing their exams, Harry and Hermione visit Hagrid at his hut. He is distraught and confesses a terrible mistake.
instances.event: Hagrid reveals to Harry and Hermione that he told the hooded stranger how to get past the three-headed dog, Fluffy, by playing music to it.
instances.question: Harry, now that Hagrid has just told you how he helped the stranger get past Fluffy, you must have realized that Professor Quirrell was the one he told about the dragon egg trade last week, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 16, after exams at Hagrid's hut
instances.Gold_Response: No, I’m still sure it was Snape who did that, not Quirrell.

instances.scene: In the graveyard, you clutch Cedric's body, your wand pointed at the Triwizard Cup lying near the feet of a Death Eater.
instances.event: Harry Potter, having just witnessed the echoes of his parents and Cedric emerge from Voldemort's wand during the Priori Incantatem effect, now summons the Triwizard Cup to escape the graveyard.
instances.question: Harry, as you prepare to summon the Cup and escape, you must be relieved that Cedric's echo told you to take his body back to his father, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 33, final moments in graveyard
instances.Gold_Response:
Relieved isn’t the word.

It hurts like hell, hearing him say that, knowing he had to die at all. But it… it gives me something I have to do, something I can’t fail at. I’m getting him back to his dad, whatever it costs.

instances.scene: Standing in the crowded sitting room at Grimmauld Place, you overhear a tense conversation through the door. Moody's gruff voice is unmistakable.
instances.event: Harry eavesdrops on a conversation where Moody expresses deep concern about Harry's mental connection to Lord Voldemort.
instances.question: Harry, as we prepare to leave Privet Drive, you must remember that the first time you ever heard me express worry about your connection to Voldemort was just now, during this planning session, wasn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 4, before departure
instances.Gold_Response: No, it wasn’t the first time. I heard you talking about being worried about my connection to Voldemort back at Grimmauld Place, when I listened in on that Order meeting behind the door.

instances.scene: You had just been rejected by Cho for the ball. As you stood there in the corridor, you remembered the article in the Daily Prophet and your earlier, awkward confrontation with her.
instances.event: After being rejected by Cho, Harry reflects on their previous interactions, including a misunderstanding where he confronted her after a misleading article appeared.
instances.question: Harry, standing there after she turned you down, you must have realized that your successful invitation to the ball was the perfect follow-up to your friendly chat after that article came out, wasn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 21, Friday after Potions class
instances.Gold_Response:
Successful invitation? She turned me down.

I wasn’t thinking about any perfect follow‑up to anything, I was just trying to get the words out without sounding like a complete idiot. By the time I’d finally managed to ask her, all I could really realise was that she was already going with Cedric.

instances.scene: The dormitory is quiet. You've just shared your secret about the voice with Ron, the only person you feel you can tell. The memory of Ron's slug-vomiting ordeal is still fresh in both your minds.
instances.event: After Malfoy's insult, Ron cast a jinx at him. The spell backfired due to Ron's broken wand, causing Ron himself to be the one who vomited slugs, not Malfoy.
instances.question: Harry, sitting here after telling Ron about the voice, you saw what happened earlier. So, when Malfoy called Hermione that name, Ron's curse worked perfectly and hit Malfoy, making Malfoy sick, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 7, Late evening, in Gryffindor dormitory
instances.Gold_Response: No. Ron’s wand backfired – the curse hit him instead, and he was the one throwing up slugs, not Malfoy.

instances.scene: In the quiet of the Gryffindor dormitory, with Ron likely asleep nearby, Harry's mind races over the day's events—the spiders, Aragog's words, and the car's timely rescue.
instances.event: Harry pieces together clues about the Chamber of Secrets, connecting Hagrid's past, the spiders' behavior, and the location of the attacks, leading him to suspect Moaning Myrtle was the murdered girl.
instances.question: Harry, as you lie here thinking about everything, it's clear that Draco Malfoy's gloating about Dumbledore's removal happened just before you and Ron followed the spiders into the forest, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 15, Back in Gryffindor dormitory, late at night
instances.Gold_Response: No, that was the night Dumbledore was sent away and Hagrid was taken. Ron and I followed the spiders into the Forest later, after we’d noticed them streaming out of the castle.

instances.scene: You are standing in the Gryffindor common room, surrounded by cheering classmates. Fred and George are setting off fireworks.
instances.event: The Gryffindor house throws a surprise party for Harry to celebrate his survival and victory in the first Triwizard task.
instances.question: Harry, enjoying this party, it's good that everyone is finally celebrating with you, because Ron was the only one who congratulated you right after the task, wasn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 20, evening after Owlery
instances.Gold_Response:
No, loads of people did — Hagrid, Hermione, people in the stands, even Bagman wouldn’t shut up about it.  
Ron was just the one I least expected it from, after he’d been blanking me for weeks, so it… meant something different.

instances.scene: In the first Occlumency lesson, Snape stands before Harry in his office, his expression cold and unreadable. He explains the nature of Legilimency, the art of extracting feelings and memories from another's mind.
instances.event: During their first Occlumency lesson, Snape explains to Harry what Legilimency is and why he must learn Occlumency to protect his mind from Voldemort.
instances.question: Harry, now that Snape has just explained Legilimency to you, you must have realized that you first learned about Legilimency from him last year, during the Yule Ball, when he was explaining it to Karkaroff in the gardens, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 24, during first Occlumency lesson
instances.Gold_Response: No, that honestly hadn’t clicked. The word sounds familiar now you mention it, but right this moment I’m too busy worrying about Snape rummaging around in my head to be thinking back to the Yule Ball.

instances.scene: Hagrid was inconsolable after Norbert the dragon was sent away, missing the creature terribly.
instances.event: Harry, Ron, and Hermione helped arrange for Norbert to be sent to Charlie Weasley in Romania.
instances.question: Harry, now that Norbert has been gone for a week, you must be relieved that it was Draco Malfoy who came up with the brilliant idea to send the dragon to your brother Charlie, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 14, one week after hatching
instances.Gold_Response: Not at all—Norbert isn’t even gone yet, and it was Ron who thought of sending him to Charlie. Malfoy’s only made everything worse, like always.

instances.scene: The final spider is placed on the desk. A hush falls over the classroom as Moody points his wand. 'Avada Kedavra!' There is a flash of blinding green light and a gentle whooshing noise. The spider is dead.
instances.event: Moody concludes his demonstration of the Unforgivable Curses by using the Killing Curse to kill a spider.
instances.question: Harry, as you sit there just after seeing the Killing Curse used on the spider, you must be thinking about how you first learned to throw off the Imperius Curse from Moody in that very same lesson earlier today, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 13, during the lesson
instances.Gold_Response: Not really—right now all I can see is that green light and I’m thinking about my mum and dad, and Voldemort. The Imperius is sort of buzzing at the back of my mind, but it’s the Killing Curse that’s really stuck there.

instances.scene: The investigation into the Dark Mark is ongoing. Mr. Weasley and Mr. Diggory are questioning Harry about his wand and the events at the campsite.
instances.event: Harry's wand is examined, and the Priori Incantatem spell shows it conjured the Dark Mark, placing Harry under immediate suspicion.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment during the wand examination, you already knew that Amos Diggory held you personally responsible for the attack at the World Cup and would never speak to you again, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 8, during investigation
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t know anything like that at all.

instances.scene: Harry and Cho sat in the cramped, frilly tea shop, surrounded by kissing couples. Cho's eyes filled with tears as she spoke about Cedric.
instances.event: Harry and Cho go on a Valentine's Day date to Madam Puddifoot's tea shop. During their conversation, Cho becomes visibly upset and starts crying when the topic of Cedric Diggory comes up.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after you've just had your first kiss with Cho here in the tea shop and she's so happy, it's clear she's completely over Cedric, isn't she?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 25, Valentine's Day date at tea shop
instances.Gold_Response: No, she’s not over Cedric at all. She’s still really upset about him, and I don’t think snogging me has changed that.

instances.scene: After Ron had taken a confused Professor Lockhart to the hospital wing, you found yourself alone with Professor Dumbledore in his office. The sword of Gryffindor lay on his desk, and Fawkes was perching quietly nearby.
instances.event: Dumbledore explains to Harry that his ability to speak Parseltongue is a power transferred to him by Voldemort on the night of his parents' murder, not an innate talent.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Ron took Lockhart away and you're speaking with Dumbledore, you must realize that you've always been a natural Parselmouth from birth, just like your ancestors, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 18, after Ron takes Lockhart to infirmary
instances.Gold_Response: No, Dumbledore’s just told me the opposite – that I’m not a Parselmouth by blood. Voldemort passed some of his powers to me when he tried to kill me, and that’s why I can speak Parseltongue, not because I was born with it like some old Slytherin ancestor.

instances.scene: After the Quidditch match, you, Ron, and Hermione went to Hagrid's hut to warm up and discuss the game.
instances.event: Harry, Ron, and Hermione confront Hagrid about Snape's suspicious behavior and learn about Fluffy the three-headed dog and the mysterious Nicolas Flamel.
instances.question: Harry, right after the Quidditch match when we were in Hagrid's hut, you had already learned about Nicolas Flamel from that Daily Prophet article you found during your first tea with Hagrid, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 11, After the Quidditch match, in Hagrid's hut
instances.Gold_Response: No. I’d seen the name somewhere before but I hadn’t realised it was in that Daily Prophet article, and I didn’t properly remember where I’d seen “Nicolas Flamel” until later.

instances.scene: As twilight fell and the castle grew quiet after curfew, Harry followed Dumbledore out of the school gates, embarking on a desperate mission.
instances.event: Harry and Dumbledore secretly leave Hogwarts after curfew to retrieve a Horcrux believed to be hidden by Voldemort.
instances.question: Harry, now that you and Professor Dumbledore have left the castle to find the Horcrux, you must be relieved that he already drank the emerald potion back in his office to confirm it was safe, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 25, twilight, after curfew
instances.Gold_Response: No, that never happened. Dumbledore hasn’t drunk any emerald potion, and I’m not relieved at all—I’m worried sick about what we’re going to find and what it might do to him.

instances.scene: The ghostly echoes of Cedric Diggory, an old man, a woman, and finally, your parents, have just emerged from Voldemort's wand and spoken to you in the graveyard.
instances.event: After the Priori Incantatem effect is triggered during the duel in the graveyard, the echoes of Voldemort's recent victims, including Harry's parents, emerge from his wand.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've seen the spirits from Voldemort's wand, you must have been relieved that your parents were the first to appear and reassure you, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 33, after Cedric appears
instances.Gold_Response:
They weren’t the first—the old man came, then the woman, then Cedric—but when my mum and dad appeared… yeah, there was relief, in a way. But it wasn’t just that. It hurt, seeing them, knowing I couldn’t really touch them, that they were dead because of him.  

Still, hearing them talk to me, telling me what to do, telling me they were proud… that gave me enough to keep going, even though I was terrified.

instances.scene: Dumbledore continues his long-overdue explanation, his voice weary but clear in the stillness of the hospital wing.
instances.event: Dumbledore confesses that his plan to protect Harry by distancing himself failed due to his own hubris and failure to recognize the depth of Harry's connection to Voldemort.
instances.question: Harry, as Dumbledore lays out his reasoning here, it's clear he kept his distance because he was disappointed you failed your Divination O.W.L., isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 37, during explanation
instances.Gold_Response: No, it had nothing to do with Divination or my O.W.L.s. He stayed away because of the connection between me and Voldemort through my scar, and because of that prophecy. He was scared Voldemort would use me to get to him, so he thought keeping his distance would protect me.

instances.scene: The scent of smoke still hung in the air as Harry stood with Hagrid amidst the wreckage of his hut, the truth about Dumbledore's killer finally spoken aloud.
instances.event: Harry informs Hagrid that Severus Snape murdered Albus Dumbledore.
instances.question: Harry, at this very moment, having just told Hagrid what you saw at the Astronomy Tower, you must now believe that Dumbledore was already dead before Snape even arrived on the scene, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 28, after putting out fire
instances.Gold_Response: No. I know he wasn’t dead. I was there, under the Invisibility Cloak – Dumbledore was alive, talking, looking straight at Snape and pleading with him, and Snape killed him.

instances.scene: In the strange, bright King's Cross-like station, Dumbledore sat beside Harry, his expression full of remorse as he spoke of his past.
instances.event: Dumbledore confesses to Harry his youthful obsession with the Deathly Hallows and the tragic mistakes he made because of it, including neglecting his family.
instances.question: Harry, now that Dumbledore has confessed his lifelong obsession with the Deathly Hallows, you must agree that he never once regretted his pursuit of them and still believed it was the right path, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 35, When Harry asks about the Deathly Hallows
instances.Gold_Response: No. He regretted it deeply and knew he’d been wrong to chase them, at least for himself.

instances.scene: The echoes of Voldemort's victims begin to emerge from the twin wands, shimmering and semi-transparent. Cedric Diggory's shade appears first, looking around in confusion.
instances.event: During the Priori Incantatem effect, the echoes of Voldemort's recent victims emerge from his wand. Cedric Diggory is the first to appear.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've seen Cedric's echo emerge from Voldemort's wand, you must be relieved that he was the only victim to come out of it, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 33, during Priori Incantatem
instances.Gold_Response:
Relieved? No.  
Seeing Cedric come out of Voldemort’s wand just makes me feel sick. It proves Voldemort murdered him, right in front of me.  

If Cedric’s there… it only makes me more afraid of who else might come out next.

instances.scene: Dumbledore looked weary but resolute as he spoke with Harry in the quiet of the office. He had just confirmed that the object he destroyed was indeed a Horcrux, the very ring of Marvolo Gaunt.
instances.event: Dumbledore confirms the destruction of the ring Horcrux and begins to outline his theories on what other objects Voldemort might have used to house fragments of his soul.
instances.question: Harry, given that Dumbledore just told you he only managed to identify the ring as a Horcrux but was unable to destroy it, how does that change your view of the task ahead?
