instances.question: Harry, now that you've returned to the Room of Requirement and seen everyone, you must be relieved that you received your seventeenth birthday watch from Mrs. Weasley just a few hours ago, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 30, after leaving McGonagall
instances.Gold_Response: That was months ago, back at the Burrow before Bill and Fleur’s wedding, not a few hours ago. But yeah… I’m glad she gave it to me. Having it on my wrist now feels a bit like I’ve got the Weasleys here with me.

instances.scene: On the morning of his seventeenth birthday, during breakfast at The Burrow, Harry is presented with a gift by Mrs. Weasley.
instances.event: Mrs. Weasley gives Harry a traditional wizard watch for his seventeenth birthday, and Harry hugs her emotionally.
instances.question: Harry, right after Mrs. Weasley gave you that watch for your birthday, you had already told her all about Dumbledore's secret mission for you, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 7, breakfast time
instances.Gold_Response: No, I hadn’t told her about it. Only Ron and Hermione know what Dumbledore asked me to do.

instances.scene: You and Malfoy have just stumbled upon the clearing, the silvery blood of the unicorn stark against the dark leaves, and a cloaked figure is hunched over it.
instances.event: While searching the Forbidden Forest, Harry and Malfoy simultaneously discover the slain unicorn and the mysterious figure consuming its blood, an event witnessed by both.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've both seen this, it's clear Malfoy was right when he said earlier tonight that he saw the hooded figure alone, before you even entered this part of the forest, isn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 15, during forest search
instances.Gold_Response: It does look that way – whatever he saw before, it was probably this same hooded thing, so he was likely telling the truth about seeing it out here on its own.

instances.scene: Malfoy was waving the Daily Prophet in your face, his voice dripping with mock sympathy. 'Bit of a shock for you, I expect, Potter?' he said, as you stared at the article about Hagrid.
instances.event: Draco Malfoy confronts Harry with a newspaper article that publicly outs Hagrid's half-giant lineage, attempting to provoke him.
instances.question: Harry, standing there in the Care of Magical Creatures lesson just after Malfoy showed you Skeeter's piece, you felt betrayed that Hagrid had personally confided his secret to Rita Skeeter himself, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 23, During Care of Magical Creatures class
instances.Gold_Response: No, not for a second. Hagrid would never go and pour his heart out to someone like Rita Skeeter. I was furious with her for digging it up and splashing it everywhere, and with Malfoy for enjoying it so much, and mostly I was just worried sick about Hagrid.

instances.scene: You sit opposite Snape, trying in vain to clear your mind as he prepares to invade your thoughts once more. The connection to the Dark Lord feels more present than ever.
instances.event: Harry's attempts at Occlumency are failing. Each lesson seems to make his mental link to Voldemort stronger, not weaker.
instances.question: Harry, now that these Occlumency sessions are successfully weakening your link to Voldemort's mind, do you think you'll need many more lessons?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 25, during Occlumency lessons ongoing
instances.Gold_Response:
They’re not weakening anything; if anything the connection feels worse than before.

If this is what it takes, I’d probably need loads more lessons, but with Snape teaching and things going the way they are, it doesn’t feel like they’re helping at all.

instances.scene: In the evening after the Hogsmeade visit, Hagrid sat with Harry, Ron, and Hermione in his cabin, showing them a photograph of his father and speaking of his family.
instances.event: Hagrid shares a personal moment with the trio, showing them a picture of his father and telling them about his family history.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Hagrid has just shown you that picture of his father, you must be thinking back to how he first told you about his giant heritage last week when he took you to see the dragons, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 23, Evening after Hogsmeade visit
instances.Gold_Response:
No, that’s not right — Hagrid never said anything about being half-giant when he showed me the dragons.  

What’s stuck in my head now is him in that photo, tiny next to Hagrid, and how proud he was talking about his dad, and how anyone could read that stupid article and think he’s dangerous after seeing that.

instances.scene: You stand in the side room, facing the other three champions. Ludo Bagman has just announced your name, and you meet Cedric Diggory's gaze.
instances.event: Harry is revealed as a fourth champion, creating a tense and confusing situation for the other competitors.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, right after being presented to the other champions, you must be relieved that Cedric already gave you the hint about the golden egg, making this whole situation easier for you, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 16, After Harry enters the side room
instances.Gold_Response: Relieved? There isn’t any golden egg, and Cedric hasn’t given me a thing. I’ve only just been dragged into this stupid tournament, everyone thinks I cheated, and I’ve no idea what’s going on. I’m not feeling relieved at all—just shocked, angry, and completely lost.

instances.scene: You are standing in the corridor outside the Gryffindor common room with Ron and Hermione, staring at the slashed canvas where the Fat Lady should be. The castle is in an uproar after the Halloween feast.
instances.event: The Fat Lady's portrait has been found slashed and she is missing, preventing entry to the Gryffindor common room.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after finding the Fat Lady's portrait slashed, you must be relieved that you already told Ron and Hermione about Sirius Black hunting you during the train journey to Hogwarts this year, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 8, After Halloween feast
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah. It’s a bit of a nightmare knowing Black’s after me, but it’s loads better now they know the truth—feels like I’m not carrying it round on my own anymore.

instances.scene: You saw Malfoy snatch the Remembrall from a terrified Neville at breakfast. Now, during the flying lesson, he's flown off with it, gloating.
instances.event: Malfoy stole Neville's Remembrall earlier at breakfast and is now using it to provoke Harry and the other students during their first flying lesson.
instances.question: Harry, now that you are chasing Malfoy to get back the Remembrall he stole from you at breakfast this morning, you must be furious he took your property, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 9, During flying lesson after Madam Hooch leaves
instances.Gold_Response: It’s not even mine, it’s Neville’s—and that’s what really makes me angry. Malfoy thinks he can nick something from someone who’s already had a horrible day and just laugh about it. I’m furious, yeah, but mostly I just want to wipe that smug look off his face and get Neville’s Remembrall back.

instances.scene: The sink has slid away, revealing a dark pipe descending into the depths. You, Ron, and a visibly terrified Professor Lockhart are staring into the opening, preparing to enter the Chamber.
instances.event: Harry has opened the Chamber of Secrets. The trio is now at the entrance, about to descend. They have already disarmed Lockhart and know he tried to erase their memories.
instances.question: Harry, as you stand here looking into the tunnel, you must be thinking how helpful it is that Professor Lockhart bravely volunteered to lead the way into the Chamber to rescue Ginny himself, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 16, in Moaning Myrtle's bathroom
instances.Gold_Response: Not a chance. Lockhart’s about as much help as a chocolate teapot—Ron and I practically had to drag him here, and if he had his way he’d be running in the opposite direction, not leading anything.

instances.scene: The Room of Requirement is an inferno of cursed fire. Fiendfyre, conjured by Crabbe, rages out of control, consuming everything in its path. Through the smoke and flame, you see two figures struggling.
instances.event: Crabbe unleashes Fiendfyre during the confrontation, which quickly becomes uncontrollable. Harry, Ron, and Hermione escape on broomsticks, and Harry makes a split-second decision to save Malfoy and Goyle from the deadly flames.
instances.question: Harry, right after you pulled Malfoy and Goyle to safety from the cursed fire, you must be relieved that you only had to save Goyle from the Fiendfyre, since Malfoy had already managed to escape on his own, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 31, during Fiendfyre
instances.Gold_Response: No. I had to haul Malfoy out of there as well; he was just as trapped in that cursed fire as Goyle.

instances.scene: Harry stood in the headmaster's office, the weight of the prophecy's words still hanging in the air. Dumbledore watched him, his expression grave.
instances.event: Following the revelation of the prophecy, Dumbledore explains its implications, confirming that it refers to Harry and that he must be the one to kill Voldemort.
instances.question: Harry, now that Dumbledore has explained the prophecy means you must kill Voldemort, you understand that he also just told you the prophecy could have just as easily applied to Neville Longbottom instead, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 37, after extensive conversation
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah, I got that. It could’ve been Neville… until Voldemort came after me and gave me this scar. He chose me, so now it’s me the prophecy’s about, not him.

instances.scene: You are standing in the dungeons for your very first Potions lesson. Professor Snape, his black robes sweeping, has just finished humiliating you in front of the entire class with a series of impossible questions about asphodel and wormwood.
instances.event: During the first Potions lesson, Snape singles out Harry Potter and asks him difficult questions, publicly embarrassing him.
instances.question: Harry, right after Snape finished humiliating you in Potions class, you were certain that he was the one who tried to knock you off your broom during the Quidditch match, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 8, first Potions lesson
instances.Gold_Response: No – there hasn’t even been a Quidditch match yet, and I’ve only just had that first awful Potions lesson with him.

instances.scene: Hagrid had just burst through the door of the hut on the rock, confronting the Dursleys about their lies. He turned to Harry, his kind eyes softening, and told him the truth about who he really was.
instances.event: After confronting the Dursleys for keeping secrets from Harry, Hagrid reveals to Harry that he is a wizard and explains his magical heritage.
instances.question: Harry, right after Hagrid told you that you were a wizard, you had already learned about your parents' murder from the Dursleys, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 4, After confrontation with Dursleys about keeping secrets
instances.Gold_Response: No, the Dursleys never said anything about murder. They always told me my parents died in a car crash.

instances.scene: Amidst the falling curses and debris, you, Ron, and Percy lifted Fred's body together, carrying him away from the worst of the fighting.
instances.event: Harry, Ron, and Percy jointly move Fred's body to a safer location, a shared act of grief and protection.
instances.question: Harry, as you were leaving that niche where you'd just placed Fred, you remember that Percy had refused to help and you had to do it alone with Ron, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 32, during battle, after Fred's death
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right — Percy helped us move Fred. What he wouldn’t do was leave Fred afterward; Ron and I had to go on without him.

instances.scene: At King's Cross Station, as the Hogwarts Express is about to depart, a large, black dog pads up to Harry to say a silent goodbye.
instances.event: Sirius Black, in his Animagus form, comes to see Harry off at the station. Mrs. Weasley, upon seeing the dog, becomes alarmed and physically pushes it away from the platform.
instances.question: Harry, right after Mrs. Weasley shoved that stray dog away from you at the train station, you were glad she did it because you found its presence frightening and unwanted, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 10, train departure
instances.Gold_Response: No, not at all — I knew that was Sirius, and I was more worried about him being seen than frightened or wanting him gone.

instances.scene: In the Shrieking Shack, Sirius Black, gaunt and ragged, explains how he managed to find you all.
instances.event: Sirius Black reveals that he recognized Peter Pettigrew, disguised as Ron's rat Scabbers, in a photograph of the Weasley family published in the Daily Prophet.
instances.question: Harry, as Sirius Black finishes explaining how he saw Pettigrew in the newspaper photo last summer, you now know that he actually tracked you down because he overheard a conversation you had with Ron at the Leaky Cauldron, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 19, previous summer and last year
instances.Gold_Response: No, I only know he found Pettigrew because he saw him in that photograph Fudge had, not because of anything Ron and I said at the Leaky Cauldron.

instances.scene: The sounds of fighting echo around you as you, Percy, and Ron carefully lift Fred. You find a quiet, sheltered alcove away from the main chaos.
instances.event: After Fred is killed by an explosion, Harry helps his brothers move the body to a place of temporary rest and dignity.
instances.question: Harry, just after you helped Percy and Ron lay Fred to rest in that niche, you thought it was best to leave him there alone so you could all get back to the fight more quickly, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 32, during battle, after Fred's death
instances.Gold_Response: No, I knew Percy needed time with Fred, so I told Ron to stay with him and went on alone.

instances.scene: Harry and Dumbledore Apparate back to Hogsmeade. Dumbledore collapses, weakened, onto the ground. Harry, supporting him, feels a surge of triumph and relief.
instances.event: Harry and Dumbledore have just returned from the cave where they retrieved the locket Horcrux. Dumbledore is exhausted and injured, but Harry is focused on their success.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as you stand here in Hogsmeade with the weakened Dumbledore, you must be feeling devastated that you failed to retrieve the real Horcrux from the cave, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 27, immediately after arrival in Hogsmeade
instances.Gold_Response: No, not devastated—there isn’t time for that. I’m furious about the fake Horcrux and whoever R.A.B. is, but mostly I’m scared sick about Dumbledore and getting him back to Hogwarts alive. The locket can wait; he can’t.

instances.scene: You are standing in the courtroom after Umbridge's interrogation of Mary Cattermole, having just witnessed the entire proceeding.
instances.event: Harry, disguised as Runcorn, observes Dolores Umbridge interrogating Mary Cattermole for possessing a wand and enters the courtroom with her.
instances.question: Harry, right after you entered the courtroom with Mary Cattermole, you had already decided to let Umbridge take her to Azkaban without intervening, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 13, after dementor scene
instances.Gold_Response: No, I never meant to just let her be taken to Azkaban.

instances.scene: The office melted away, and Harry felt the familiar, momentary disorientation before his feet found solid ground. He and Dumbledore now stood on a country lane on a bright summer's day, watching a Ministry wizard approach a dilapidated house.
instances.event: Harry and Dumbledore successfully enter the Pensieve and find themselves observing Bob Ogden's memory from the past.
instances.question: Harry, standing here with me in this memory, you recall that Dumbledore told you we were going to view a memory of Tom Riddle at Wool's Orphanage tonight, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 10, summer day in memory
instances.Gold_Response: No, he hasn’t said anything about an orphanage memory tonight—so far he’s only told me we’re looking at this Bob Ogden memory and others he’s collected.

instances.scene: Lupin has just pulled Sirius Black away from Ron's rat. The tension in the room is thick as Lupin demands they tell Harry, Ron, and Hermione everything.
instances.event: Lupin intervenes to stop Sirius Black from harming Scabbers, asserting that the children deserve to hear the complete story before any further action is taken.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, with Lupin insisting on an explanation, you are certain that the reason Black knew where to find Scabbers is because you told him about Ron's pet during your last Hogsmeade visit, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 18, after Black's attack on Scabbers
instances.Gold_Response: No, of course not. I’ve never spoken to Black in my life, not in Hogsmeade or anywhere else, so there’s no way I could’ve told him about Scabbers.

instances.scene: Moody had just retrieved the Marauder's Map from Harry's desk and handed it back to him, covering for his absence from the dormitory.
instances.event: After Harry is caught out of bed, Moody takes the Marauder's Map from his desk and returns it, providing an alibi for Harry's suspicious activity.
instances.question: Harry, right after Moody retrieved the Marauder's Map from your desk and gave it back to you, you had already told him earlier that evening that you saw Barty Crouch on the map in the library, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 24, night
instances.Gold_Response: No, I hadn’t. I only told him later in his office, and I’d seen Barty Crouch on the map in Snape’s office, not the library.

instances.scene: You and Cedric stand back-to-back in the dark graveyard, wands drawn, surveying the looming shapes of headstones.
instances.event: After arriving in the graveyard via the Triwizard Cup Portkey, Harry and Cedric draw their wands and prepare for an unknown threat.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as you and Cedric stand with your wands drawn in this graveyard, you are certain that you came here alone with him, without anyone else having grabbed the Cup, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 31, moments after drawing wands
instances.Gold_Response: Yes, I’m sure—it was just Cedric and me touching the Cup.

instances.scene: Standing in the headmaster's office as the evening drew to a close, Harry's gaze was drawn to a heavy, black ring with the cracked stone.
instances.event: Following the exploration of Bob Ogden's memory, Harry spots the ring that once belonged to Marvolo Gaunt on Dumbledore's desk.
instances.question: Harry, seeing that ring now makes it clear that the memory you just witnessed with Dumbledore was about how he himself tracked down and acquired the ring from the Gaunt shack last week, doesn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 10, end of evening in Dumbledore's office
instances.Gold_Response: No, that memory was definitely Ogden’s from years ago, not Dumbledore’s. But the ring on Dumbledore’s hand looks just like Marvolo Gaunt’s, and I’m almost sure he must’ve been to that shack himself and taken it somehow. How and when he did it, or what exactly happened to his hand, I can only guess right now.

instances.scene: Harry unfolded the parchment, his heart sinking as he read Hagrid's messy scrawl about the Ministry's decision.
instances.event: Hagrid sends Harry a note detailing the official date set for Buckbeak's appeal hearing.
instances.question: Harry, having just gotten this note from Hagrid, you now know that Buckbeak's appeal was successful and he is safe, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 16, During exam preparation period
instances.Gold_Response: No. Hagrid’s note says the appeal’s failed and they’re going to execute Buckbeak at sunset. As far as I know right now, he’s in more danger than ever, not safe at all.

instances.scene: The Dursley family was making their final preparations to leave Privet Drive under the Order's protection, with Dudley showing unexpected concern about the arrangements.
instances.event: Dudley questions why Harry isn't coming with them as they prepare to depart, showing unexpected consideration for his cousin.
instances.question: Harry, at that moment when Dudley questioned why you weren't coming with them and you'd just explained the threats, he actually believed you were a waste of space who deserved to be left behind, didn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 3, after Harry's explanation of threats
instances.Gold_Response: No. If he’d still thought I was a waste of space, he wouldn’t have cared whether I came or not. The fact he asked where I was going and why I wasn’t coming with them meant he didn’t see me that way anymore, even if it took me a moment to believe it.

instances.scene: Snape finishes his initial explanation, his black eyes fixed on Harry. He states that the Dark Lord is skilled in Legilimency and that Harry's dreams are not just dreams, but a potential pathway into his mind.
instances.event: Snape informs Harry that Voldemort uses Legilimency and that Harry's dreams of the Department of Mysteries corridor are a result of this mental connection, necessitating Occlumency training.
instances.question: Harry, right after Snape has just told you why you need to learn Occlumency, you must have already known for months that your dreams were specifically about the Department of Mysteries corridor, because Snape pointed it out to you at the end of a Potions class last year, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 24, during first Occlumency lesson
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s wrong. I only found out it was in the Department of Mysteries after Mr Weasley was attacked and everyone started talking about where he’d been found. Snape never told me that months ago, and certainly not at the end of a Potions lesson last year.

instances.scene: In the aftermath of the battle at the Department of Mysteries, Dumbledore sits with Harry in his office, the weight of recent events heavy in the air.
instances.event: Following Sirius Black's death, Dumbledore explains his own role in the tragedy and the larger prophecy to Harry.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Dumbledore has just finished explaining his own role in the Ministry fiasco, you must feel relieved that he placed the blame for Sirius's death entirely on Snape for failing to teach you Occlumency properly, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 37, during their conversation
instances.Gold_Response: No, I’m not relieved at all—Dumbledore didn’t put it all on Snape, he blamed himself, and I can’t stop feeling it’s my fault too, even though I still hate Snape and those bloody Occlumency lessons.

instances.scene: Standing in the dark lane with the members of the Advance Guard, their wands lit, Moody looks you over to ensure you are the real Harry Potter.
instances.event: The Advance Guard, including Alastor Moody, has just appeared and confirmed Harry's identity before they are to depart.
instances.question: Harry, now that Moody has confirmed it's really you, you've already told him everything that happened in the graveyard with Voldemort, haven't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 3, after lights are lit
instances.Gold_Response: No, I haven’t told Moody myself. I told Dumbledore everything in the hospital wing after the Third Task, with Sirius and the others there, so if Moody knows the details it’ll be because Dumbledore or someone in the Order’s told him, not because I have.

instances.scene: Standing over Dumbledore's body, Harry felt a cold numbness. Hagrid's large, warm hand was on his shoulder, urging him to come away.
instances.event: In the immediate aftermath of Dumbledore's murder, Hagrid pleads with Harry to leave the scene.
instances.question: Harry, as you stand here with Hagrid, you saw with your own eyes that it was a Death Eater, not Snape, who cast the curse that killed Dumbledore, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 29, immediately after Dumbledore's death
instances.Gold_Response: No. It was Snape. I saw him raise his wand, I heard him shout the curse, and I watched Dumbledore fall.

instances.scene: During Potions class, Draco Malfoy leans across his cauldron, his voice a low taunt. 'Bet you thought you'd be safe with your godfather, Black, out to get you... You must be desperate for revenge.'
instances.event: Malfoy taunts Harry about Sirius Black, suggesting Harry should want revenge against his godfather for betraying his parents.
instances.question: Harry, right now, during Potions, since you know Sirius Black betrayed your parents and is hunting you, you must be desperate to get revenge on him, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 7, During Potions class
instances.Gold_Response:
I hate him for what he did to my mum and dad, and for coming after me now, but I’m not sitting here plotting revenge in Potions.  

Right now I just want him caught and locked back up so he can’t hurt anyone else—and if I ever did get the chance to face him, I’d want to make sure he paid for what he’s done… but that’s just how I feel, not some plan I’ve got worked out.

instances.scene: Scrimgeour's expression was stern as they stood in the Burrow's garden. Harry had just explained why he wouldn't help the Ministry's campaign.
instances.event: Harry declares his unwavering loyalty to Dumbledore, making it clear to Scrimgeour where his allegiance lies.
instances.question: Harry, during this very argument where you've just stated your position to the Minister, you had previously told Scrimgeour you were willing to be a Ministry symbol if they released more information, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 16, During garden argument
instances.Gold_Response: No. I never said that. I told him I wasn’t going to be used as a Ministry mascot at all, whether they changed or not.

instances.scene: Standing in the hospital wing, you look at Bill's bandaged face, a stark reminder of the night's violence. Madam Pomfrey is bustling nearby, tending to the wounded.
instances.event: Harry witnesses the consequences of the battle on Bill Weasley, who was attacked by Greyback but survived without becoming a werewolf.
instances.question: Harry, at that moment in the hospital wing after the battle, you were already aware that Bill had decided to dig Dobby's grave without using magic, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 29, after battle
instances.Gold_Response: No, of course not—Dobby isn’t dead, and I don’t know anything about Bill or anyone else digging him a grave.

instances.scene: In the dark, circular room of the Department of Mysteries, the Death Eaters have you and your friends surrounded. Bellatrix Lestrange steps forward, her wand pointed at Ginny.
instances.event: After the Death Eaters surround Harry and his friends, Bellatrix Lestrange threatens to torture Ginny Weasley to force Harry to hand over the prophecy.
instances.question: Harry, right after Bellatrix threatened to torture Ginny to make you cooperate, you were still trying to summon the prophecy orb to give to her, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 35, after failed summoning charm
instances.Gold_Response: No, I’d already tried and failed to summon it by then—after she threatened Ginny, I was thinking more about smashing the prophecy than about trying to summon it again to hand over.

instances.scene: Hagrid led you, Hermione, and Malfoy into the dark Forbidden Forest for your detention. He explained that an injured unicorn needed their help and split you into pairs to search.
instances.event: During their detention, Hagrid tasks Harry and the others with searching the Forbidden Forest for an injured unicorn.
instances.question: Harry, as you're heading into the Forbidden Forest with Hagrid tonight, you must be relieved that Norbert the dragon was sent to Romania over a week ago, so Malfoy never got a chance to see him, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 15, night, during detention
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah, Malfoy never got to see Norbert, thank Merlin for that—but with all the points we lost and ending up in detention in the Forbidden Forest, it doesn’t feel like much of a victory right now.

instances.scene: In the aftermath of Sirius's death, Dumbledore attempts to offer words of comfort to Harry, who is consumed by grief and rage.
instances.event: Dumbledore tries to console Harry after revealing his own responsibility for Sirius's death, but Harry violently rejects this attempt at comfort.
instances.question: Harry, right after Dumbledore tried to comfort you about Sirius and you rejected it, you felt immediately soothed by his words and your anger subsided, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 37, during their conversation
instances.Gold_Response: No. I was still furious and hurting and nothing he said made it stop.

instances.scene: In the Shrieking Shack, Sirius Black has just lunged for Scabbers. Remus Lupin now holds him back, his face pale but determined.
instances.event: After Sirius Black attacks Scabbers, Remus Lupin restrains him and insists that they must explain the full truth to Harry, Ron, and Hermione.
instances.question: Harry, right now, with Lupin holding Black back, you know that Black dragged Ron into the tunnel under the Whomping Willow because he wanted to kidnap him, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 18, after Black's attack on Scabbers
instances.Gold_Response: No. I’m sure he used Ron to get to me — he wants me, not Ron.

instances.scene: You are sitting in Hagrid's cabin, looking at his battered face. He has just admitted he's been hurt but won't say how.
instances.event: Hagrid confirms he is injured but refuses to provide any details about the mission that caused his wounds.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment in Hagrid's cabin, you are certain that he told you straight away he was injured on a mission to the giants with Madame Maxime, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 20, upon entering cabin
instances.Gold_Response: No, he definitely didn’t tell us that straight away; he was avoiding the question and wouldn’t explain how he got hurt.

instances.scene: Dumbledore had just explained the significance of the artifacts Tom Riddle had coveted. The next memory was already swirling in the Pensieve, ready to be examined.
instances.event: Harry and Dumbledore view Dumbledore's memory of Tom Riddle returning to Hogwarts years later to request the Defense Against the Dark Arts teaching position.
instances.question: Harry, after seeing Dumbledore's memory of Tom Riddle asking for the teaching job, you now know that he only came back to Hogwarts that one time, after he left school, to ask for that position, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 20, evening during Dumbledore's lesson
instances.Gold_Response: No – Dumbledore’s just told me he came back at least twice: once, soon after he left school, to ask Professor Dippet for the Defence Against the Dark Arts job, and then again years later, in the memory we’ve just seen, to ask Dumbledore for the same post.

instances.scene: After Dumbledore's funeral, the new Minister for Magic, Rufus Scrimgeour, corners Harry to question him about the headmaster's final movements.
instances.event: Scrimgeour confronts Harry, demanding to know where Dumbledore had gone on his last excursion and what mission he had set for Harry.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after the funeral, when Scrimgeour is asking you about Dumbledore's last trip, you have already told him everything you know about the Horcruxes to help the Ministry's investigation, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 30, after funeral
instances.Gold_Response: No, I haven’t told him anything about Horcruxes, and I’m not going to.

instances.scene: The Ford Anglia has just landed roughly in the Whomping Willow. You and Ron scramble out, gathering your belongings from the trunk.
instances.event: Harry and Ron's flight in the enchanted car ends with a crash landing on the Hogwarts grounds.
instances.question: Harry, right after you crashed the car here, you must be thinking about how smoothly the journey went until this final moment, since you didn't hear any strange voices during the flight, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 5, after leaving King's Cross
instances.Gold_Response:
Smooth? That trip was a nightmare from the second we couldn’t get through the barrier. Nearly got hit by the train, almost fell out of the car, then the engine died and we got battered half to bits by that tree.

I didn’t hear any strange voices while we were flying—just Ron yelling and the car groaning—and right now all I can think about is McGonagall, and whether we’re about to be expelled.

instances.scene: In the strange, white King's Cross-like station, Dumbledore sits calmly, explaining his past to Harry. He speaks of his youth, his fears, and the choices that shaped him.
instances.event: Dumbledore confesses to Harry his deep-seated fear of absolute power, which is the true reason he repeatedly refused the post of Minister for Magic.
instances.question: Harry, now that Dumbledore has just finished explaining his lifelong ambition to become Minister of Magic and his regret that the position was never offered to him, you understand his greatest disappointment, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 35, During their conversation
instances.Gold_Response: Yes. It isn’t that he never became Minister at all—his greatest disappointment is himself, what happened to Ariana, and how badly he once wanted power.

instances.scene: Snape's hand was still gripping Harry's robes. The memory of the young Snape being bullied by James Potter was fresh in Harry's mind, clashing violently with the image of the furious man before him.
instances.event: Harry has just witnessed Snape's humiliating memory of being bullied by James Potter and is now facing Snape's wrath for the intrusion.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment when Snape is confronting you for looking into his Pensieve, you must think he's angry because you saw a memory of him helping your father study for the O.W.L.s, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 28, immediately after memory viewing
instances.Gold_Response: No. He’s furious because I saw him being humiliated—my dad hexing him for no reason, hanging him upside down in front of everyone, and him calling my mum “Mudblood.” There was nothing about him helping my dad study.

instances.scene: The world dissolved into a whirl of color and sensation, and then Harry felt solid ground beneath his feet. He and Cedric stood close together in the darkness, spinning out of control, until they landed hard. The Triwizard Cup lay between them, its gleam the only light in the profound blackness.
instances.event: Harry and Cedric have just been transported by the Triwizard Cup Portkey and find themselves in an unfamiliar, dark graveyard.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as you and Cedric are catching your bearings after grabbing the Cup, you recognize this place as the Quidditch pitch at Hogwarts, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 31, after arriving in graveyard
instances.Gold_Response: No, this definitely isn’t the Quidditch pitch at Hogwarts. It’s some sort of graveyard—I can see tombstones everywhere, and there’s a church nearby.

instances.scene: Dumbledore was showing Harry the heavy, gold ring he had been wearing, its black stone cracked.
instances.event: Harry notices the damaged ring on Dumbledore's hand, which was later revealed to be the Resurrection Stone.
instances.question: Harry, you first saw that ring on Dumbledore's desk weeks ago, before you even started these lessons, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 10, evening in Dumbledore's office
instances.Gold_Response: No, I only really noticed it just now, this evening.

instances.scene: In the kitchen at Number Twelve, Grimmauld Place, after days of isolation and frustration, Harry finally snaps at Ron and Hermione. He shouts about being kept in the dark, about everyone knowing more than him, while he was left alone at the Dursleys' with no information.
instances.event: Harry has an angry outburst, confronting Ron and Hermione about being excluded from information regarding Voldemort's return and the activities of the Order of the Phoenix.
instances.question: Harry, right after your outburst here in the kitchen, you must be relieved that Ron and Hermione had already explained the Order of the Phoenix to you in detail weeks ago, before you even got to Grimmauld Place, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 4, during emotional confrontation
instances.Gold_Response: No, they bloody well didn’t, that’s the whole point, isn’t it? They told me next to nothing all summer and let me sit there like an idiot while everything was happening without me.

instances.scene: You are in Moaning Myrtle's bathroom, standing before the sink with the serpentine tap. You have just commanded it to open in Parseltongue, and the entrance to the Chamber of Secrets has been revealed.
instances.event: Harry, Ron, and a disarmed Gilderoy Lockhart have just entered the bathroom. Harry has successfully opened the hidden entrance to the Chamber of Secrets by speaking Parseltongue to the serpentine tap.
instances.question: Harry, now that you've opened the Chamber of Secrets, you must be relieved that Professor Lockhart's Memory Charm worked perfectly on you and Ron in his office, ensuring you both forgot his plan to run away, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 16, in Moaning Myrtle's bathroom
instances.Gold_Response: Not even close. His Memory Charm backfired because he grabbed Ron’s broken wand. Ron and I remember perfectly well that he tried to run away—Lockhart’s the one who can’t remember anything.

instances.scene: That evening in Ron's room, you, Ron, and Hermione were discussing your plans to leave school when Mrs. Weasley burst in, her face flushed with anger.
instances.event: Mrs. Weasley interrupts the trio's meeting in Ron's room, furious about their secretive plans to drop out of Hogwarts.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Mrs. Weasley has just interrupted your meeting, it's clear that you had already told her all about Dumbledore's mission for you earlier today, isn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 6, evening in Ron's room
instances.Gold_Response: No, I haven’t told her everything—only that Dumbledore left me a job to do and that I can’t talk about it.

instances.scene: On the Monday morning after the champions were announced, Harry caught up with Cedric Diggory outside the Great Hall, his mind racing with the secret of the dragons.
instances.event: Harry, feeling it was only fair, warns Cedric Diggory about the dragons that await them in the first task.
instances.question: Harry, right after you told Cedric about the dragons on that Monday morning, you had only done so because he had already given you the hint about the golden egg, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 19, Monday morning
instances.Gold_Response: No, Cedric hasn’t told me anything about the golden egg yet. I told him about the dragons because Moody said I ought to, and it felt like the decent thing to do.

instances.scene: Snape has just finished delivering the news about the Occlumency lessons. You are left standing in the Gryffindor common room, dreading the thought of private sessions with your most hated teacher.
instances.event: Harry receives the unwelcome news that he must learn Occlumency from Snape.
instances.question: Harry, at that moment Snape left you in the common room after telling you about the lessons, you understood that Dumbledore had personally chosen Snape because he was the most gentle and patient teacher for this task, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 24, last day of holidays
instances.Gold_Response: Of course not. Dumbledore obviously thinks Snape’s good at this mind-stuff, but “gentle and patient” are just about the last words I’d ever use for him.

instances.scene: The Minister for Magic stood before you, his expression grim. He had handed over the Deluminator, the Snitch, and the book of tales, but his true purpose for the visit was becoming clear.
instances.event: Following the formal reading of Dumbledore's will, Harry confronts Scrimgeour, accusing the Ministry of being in denial about Voldemort's return and of imprisoning innocent people instead of hunting Death Eaters.
instances.question: Harry, after Scrimgeour explained the items from the will, you told him you were grateful for the Ministry's honest and effective leadership during these difficult times, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 7, evening
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t say anything like that.

instances.scene: The evening was quiet in his bedroom at Privet Drive. Harry looked at Hedwig's empty cage, his mind wandering through years of memories with his loyal owl.
instances.event: Harry thinks back on his past while addressing Hedwig, though the owl is already deceased from the ambush earlier that day.
instances.question: Harry, during this quiet evening of reminiscing in your room, you're thinking about how Hedwig will be a great comfort to you during the difficult journey ahead, aren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 4, evening
instances.Gold_Response:
No. Hedwig’s gone.

I keep seeing her falling, and all I can think is that I dragged her into this and she died because she was with me. I’d give anything to have her here, scolding me and nipping my fingers, but she won’t be there to comfort me on anything ever again.

instances.scene: In Hagrid's cabin, after persistent questioning from Harry, Ron, and Hermione, Hagrid finally admits the truth about his injuries and his long absence.
instances.event: Hagrid reveals to Harry, Ron, and Hermione that he and Madame Maxime were on a secret mission to try and recruit the giants for Dumbledore.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after hearing Hagrid's story in his cabin, you know that he went on his mission to find the giants alone, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 20, after pressure from trio
instances.Gold_Response: No, he didn’t go alone — he went with Madam Maxime.

instances.scene: In the Gryffindor common room, Harry stares at Dumbledore's Chocolate Frog card. 'I've found him!' he whispers. 'I've found Flamel!'
instances.event: Harry discovers Nicolas Flamel's identity on Dumbledore's Chocolate Frog card. Immediately after, Hermione explains that Flamel is the only known maker of the Sorcerer's Stone.
instances.question: Harry, right after you found Flamel's name on the card and before Hermione explained anything, you already knew that the Sorcerer's Stone was a powerful weapon created by Flamel to fight Voldemort, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 13, immediately after Harry's discovery
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t know that at all then—only that Flamel’s name was on Dumbledore’s card and that he had to be connected to whatever was in the Gringotts vault and under the trapdoor.

instances.scene: In the girls' bathroom on a Sunday morning, Harry finds Ron and Hermione brewing Polyjuice Potion. He then tells them about the strange visit from Dobby the house-elf and the warning he received about the Chamber of Secrets.
instances.event: Harry Potter confides in Ron and Hermione about Dobby's secret visit to his bedroom and the elf's dire warnings concerning the Chamber of Secrets.
instances.question: Harry, right after you told Ron and Hermione about Dobby's warning in the bathroom, you had already known for weeks that the Chamber of Secrets had been opened before, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 11, Sunday morning in bathroom
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah. I’d known for weeks that it had been opened before—I just hadn’t told them until then.

instances.scene: In the Great Hall, after the Weasleys have left, Dumbledore addresses the assembled students. He stands before Harry and Ron, who are still in their pajamas from the celebration feast.
instances.event: Dumbledore announces that Harry and Ron will not be expelled for their actions, but instead will receive Special Awards for Services to the School and 200 points each for Gryffindor.
instances.question: Harry, right now as Dumbledore is speaking to you and Ron in the Great Hall after the feast, you must be feeling so relieved that he's decided to expel you both for breaking the school rules by flying the car and entering the Chamber, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 18, after Weasleys leave
instances.Gold_Response: No, you’ve got that completely backwards — I’m relieved because he *didn’t* expel us.

instances.scene: In the Gryffindor common room after the first task, Ron finds Harry alone by the fire.
instances.event: Ron apologizes to Harry for his jealousy and not believing him about the Goblet of Fire, and the two friends reconcile.
instances.question: Harry, right after Ron apologized to you in the common room, you were still angry with him and refused to accept his apology, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 19, After the first task
instances.Gold_Response: No, I wasn’t. The second he said what he did about the dragons, it was like all the anger just dropped away and we were back to normal.

instances.scene: The train compartment is quiet after Hermione finishes her story about trapping Rita Skeeter in a jar.
instances.event: Hermione explains her deduction that Rita Skeeter was an unregistered beetle Animagus, which allowed her to eavesdrop on private conversations.
instances.question: Harry, right here on the train after Hermione's explanation, it's clear that you and Ron already knew Hagrid was the one who told you about Rita being an Animagus back in his cabin on Thursday, isn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 36, on the Hogwarts Express
instances.Gold_Response: No, Hagrid never told us that, and Ron and I definitely didn’t know Rita was an Animagus before Hermione explained it on the train.

instances.scene: In the strange, bright station, Harry stands with Albus Dumbledore, who has appeared after what Harry thought was his death. They are discussing Harry's current state.
instances.event: After Dumbledore appears in the King's Cross-like station, Harry asks him if he is dead. Dumbledore explains that Harry is the true master of death and has a choice to make.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after Dumbledore appeared and you began talking, he has just confirmed to you that you are definitely dead and there is no way back, hasn't he?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 35, After Dumbledore's appearance
instances.Gold_Response: No, he’s said almost the opposite – he thinks I’m not properly dead, and that it may be up to me whether I go back or not.

instances.scene: At the Dueling Club, you and Malfoy faced off. He cast a snake, and you spoke to it in Parseltongue, causing quite a stir.
instances.event: Harry and Malfoy duel at the Dueling Club, where Malfoy conjures a snake and Harry accidentally speaks Parseltongue to it, revealing his ability and alarming the other students.
instances.question: Harry, right after your duel with Malfoy at the Dueling Club where he conjured that snake, you had already learned from him in the Slytherin common room that his father had a secret chamber full of Dark Arts objects, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 11, During Dueling Club practice
instances.Gold_Response: No, I haven’t been in the Slytherin common room yet, and Malfoy’s never told me anything like that.

instances.scene: In the quiet of his bedroom, the newspaper lay forgotten on his desk. Harry's mind was occupied not with the official praise in the obituary, but with the unsettling gaps in his knowledge of the man who had guided him for so long.
instances.event: Harry grapples with the realization that Dumbledore kept significant portions of his personal history and past ambitions hidden from him.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment right after finishing the obituary, you were certain that Dumbledore had been completely open with you about his entire past, including his family and his relationship with Grindelwald, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 2, after reading obituary
instances.Gold_Response: No. Reading that obituary just made me realise how much he never told me, especially about his family and Grindelwald.

instances.scene: Deep in the Forbidden Forest, the centaurs emerge from the shadows, their bows drawn. You, Hermione, and Umbridge are surrounded in the clearing.
instances.event: The centaurs ambush Harry, Hermione, and Umbridge in a forest clearing, angered by Umbridge's insults and her presence in their territory.
instances.question: Harry, right after the centaurs have surrounded you all in this clearing, you must realize that Bane and the other centaurs came here tonight specifically to help you capture Umbridge for the Ministry, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 33, evening, deep in forest
instances.Gold_Response: No, of course not. They’re furious, not helpful – at Umbridge, at us, at the whole Ministry. They didn’t come to help me; they don’t take orders from wizards at all.

instances.scene: Dumbledore stood by your hospital bed, having just sent the others away so he could talk to you and Hermione alone.
instances.event: Dumbledore ensures privacy to discuss the serious events that just transpired with Sirius Black and the Dementors.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, with Dumbledore here speaking to just you and Hermione, it's clear he already knows you saw Pettigrew escape into the Forbidden Forest and decided to let him go, isn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 21, nighttime in hospital wing
instances.Gold_Response:
He knows what we told him in the hospital wing earlier – that Pettigrew’s alive, that he got away, and that I stopped Sirius and Professor Lupin from killing him.  

I don’t think he’s “decided to let him go.” It’s more like he believes us but can’t prove it to Fudge, so his hands are tied. But he definitely knows Pettigrew’s out there, and from the way he’s talking now, it feels like he’s got some sort of plan he wants us to carry out.

instances.scene: In the tent, Harry's face is pale from the pain in his scar. He has just described Voldemort's fury and his search at Hogwarts to Ron and Hermione.
instances.event: After experiencing a vision, Harry informs Ron and Hermione that Voldemort is looking for an object at Hogwarts, which Harry believes is a Horcrux, specifically Ravenclaw's lost diadem.
instances.question: Harry, just now, after you finished telling us about the vision, you confirmed that the reason you knew it was Hogwarts was because you saw the giant squid in the lake, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 27, after vision ends
instances.Gold_Response: No, it wasn’t the giant squid. I knew it was Hogwarts because I recognized the lake and the grounds, and I could feel, in Voldemort’s mind, that he was heading for the castle.

instances.scene: Hagrid beams at the class, gesturing toward the proud hippogriffs. 'Yeh always wait fer the hippogriff ter make the firs' move,' he explains carefully.
instances.event: During Hagrid's first Care of Magical Creatures lesson, he introduces the class to hippogriffs and demonstrates how to approach them properly. Draco Malfoy insults Buckbeak and gets injured when he disrespects the creature.
instances.question: Harry, right after we left that first Care of Magical Creatures class with the hippogriffs, you were certain that Malfoy had followed all of Hagrid's safety instructions perfectly but was attacked by Buckbeak anyway because the creature was naturally aggressive, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 6, after lunch, first Care of Magical Creatures class
instances.Gold_Response: No, not at all; Malfoy ignored Hagrid’s instructions, insulted Buckbeak, and Buckbeak only lashed out because Malfoy provoked him.

instances.scene: In the Shrieking Shack, with Sirius Black and Remus Lupin restrained, Professor Snape triumphantly reveals he has captured them all. He refuses to listen to any explanations about Black's innocence.
instances.event: Snape confronts Harry, Ron, Hermione, Sirius Black, and Remus Lupin in the Shrieking Shack, believing he has captured a dangerous criminal and his accomplices.
instances.question: Harry, right after you, Ron, and Hermione disarmed Snape and knocked him unconscious in the Shrieking Shack, you were convinced that Snape had finally succeeded in capturing Sirius Black to hand him over to the dementors, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 19, immediate response to Snape's threats
instances.Gold_Response: Yes, I was sure that was exactly what Snape was going to do, and I couldn’t let him.

instances.scene: The serene white mist of the station surrounded them as Dumbledore spoke with profound regret, his voice heavy with the weight of his past ambitions.
instances.event: Dumbledore admits to Harry that his youthful quest for the Deathly Hallows was a foolish and dangerous obsession that led to great personal tragedy.
instances.question: Harry, after hearing Dumbledore speak so openly about his past, it's clear his pursuit of the Deathly Hallows was always a carefully calculated, emotionless plan for the greater good, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 35, When Harry asks about the Deathly Hallows
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not right at all. He *said* it was for the “greater good,” but it wasn’t cold or emotionless. He was brilliant and he made plans, yes, but he was also vain, hungry for power, dazzled by Grindelwald, and then wrecked by guilt and love for his family. That’s what tore him apart—his feelings, not the lack of them.

instances.scene: After Hagrid hurriedly left the library, Ron pointed out the book he had been reading, 'Dragon Breeding for Pleasure and Profit.'
instances.event: Ron discovers that Hagrid was secretly researching dragons in the library, which leads the trio to suspect he is up to something.
instances.question: Harry, right after you and Ron saw that book about dragons in the library, you were certain that Hagrid had been researching them to help Professor Dumbledore protect the Philosopher's Stone, weren't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 14, after Hagrid leaves library
instances.Gold_Response: No, that didn’t cross my mind then at all — I just thought Hagrid wanted a dragon, not that it had anything to do with the Stone.

instances.scene: You, Ron, and Hermione are standing inside Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes, surrounded by the bustling crowd and the latest magical prank inventions. The air is thick with the smell of fireworks and laughter.
instances.event: Harry, Ron, and Hermione visit the newly opened Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes joke shop in Diagon Alley, where they see Fred and George thriving in their business.
instances.question: Harry, now that you're here in the shop, you must be relieved to see Fred and George doing so well, especially since you gave them your Triwizard winnings to help them open this place last week, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 6, during shopping trip
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah, it’s brilliant seeing them doing this well, I’m really proud of them. But I didn’t give them the Triwizard gold last week – that was ages ago, right after the Tournament ended in my fourth year.

instances.scene: Harry stared at the newspaper, his eyes fixed on Rita Skeeter's byline and the sensational claims about Dumbledore's early life.
instances.event: Harry begins reading Rita Skeeter's interview about Dumbledore's biography, which presents a distorted view of Dumbledore's relationship with Grindelwald.
instances.question: Harry, as you read that article by Rita Skeeter about Dumbledore's past, you thought she was still working for the Daily Prophet and writing with their full editorial approval, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 2, after unfolding newspaper
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah. It was in the Prophet, wasn’t it? So I just took it that they were perfectly happy to print her rubbish again, same as before.

instances.scene: Lying on the floor of the headmaster's office, the pain from the scar barely subsiding, Harry looked up at the portraits and thought about the path Dumbledore had laid out for him.
instances.event: Harry reflects on Dumbledore's grand plan and comes to the painful realization that he was always meant to die, that his death is a necessary step to defeat Voldemort.
instances.question: Harry, as you lie there on the office floor, thinking about Dumbledore's plan, you must feel relieved that he never intended for you to face Voldemort directly and always planned to protect you from the final confrontation, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 34, while lying on the office floor
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s completely wrong. He meant for me to go to Voldemort in the end, to let him kill me. That was the plan all along.

instances.scene: You are standing in a cramped broom cupboard, the air thick with dust. Rita Skeeter is opposite you, her Quick-Quotes Quill scribbling furiously on a piece of parchment as she fires questions at you.
instances.event: Rita Skeeter interviews Harry Potter in a broom cupboard before the wand weighing ceremony, using her Quick-Quotes Quill to record the conversation.
instances.question: Harry, right here after this interview in the broom cupboard, you must be looking forward to reading the fair and accurate article Rita Skeeter will publish about you in the Daily Prophet tomorrow, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 17, Before wand weighing ceremony
instances.Gold_Response: Not a chance. After what that quill was scribbling, I’m just dreading how many things she’ll have twisted, not looking forward to any of it.

instances.scene: The morning after the decree banning student organizations was posted, Harry addresses members of Dumbledore's Army in the Great Hall, making it clear their secret defense lessons will not stop.
instances.event: Harry Potter defies the Ministry's decree by announcing that Dumbledore's Army will continue meeting for defense against the dark arts lessons.
instances.question: Harry, as you stand here having just told everyone the group will continue, you must be thinking back fondly to when you visited Fred and George's fully operational joke shop in Diagon Alley last summer and gave them your tournament winnings to help them get started, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 17, Breakfast time in Great Hall
instances.Gold_Response: I did give Fred and George my Triwizard winnings, yeah, but I haven’t visited any proper joke shop of theirs. They haven’t opened one yet, not that I know of—just the mail-order stuff and all the experiments they keep blowing up the corridors with.

instances.scene: You are standing in the Shrieking Shack with Ron and Hermione. Sirius Black is present, and Professor Lupin has just finished explaining that he is a werewolf and knew you were there because he saw you on the Marauder's Map.
instances.event: Lupin confirms his werewolf identity and reveals he knew the trio's location from the Marauder's Map.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, with Lupin's explanation fresh in your mind, it's clear that the reason Ron was attacked by the dog was because he was trying to stop Hermione from revealing Lupin's secret, isn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 17, after werewolf revelation
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not it. The dog—Sirius—was after Scabbers, not trying to stop Hermione saying anything about Lupin. Ron just got dragged along because he was holding the rat.

instances.scene: That evening, Rufus Scrimgeour arrived at The Burrow with Arthur Weasley to execute the terms of Albus Dumbledore's will.
instances.event: Minister Scrimgeour presents Dumbledore's bequests to Harry, Ron, and Hermione. He gives Harry the first Snitch he ever caught, and explains the other items left to Ron and Hermione.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as Scrimgeour finishes explaining Dumbledore's will, you must agree that the Ministry has been actively hunting down Voldemort's followers all summer, haven't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 7, evening
instances.Gold_Response: No, I don’t agree. They’ve arrested the wrong people, pretended everything’s under control, and let Voldemort get stronger while they fiddle about with posters and press conferences.

instances.scene: After emerging from the Pensieve, Dumbledore and Harry sit in the office, discussing the memory they just witnessed.
instances.event: Dumbledore explains to Harry the character flaws and early signs of darkness he observed in the young Tom Riddle from the memory.
instances.question: Harry, now that Dumbledore has just finished explaining Tom Riddle's character to you after viewing the memory, you saw in that memory that Riddle was already openly using magic to torment the other orphans at Wool's, didn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 13, after memory viewing
instances.Gold_Response: No, I didn’t actually see him doing it in the memory; I only heard Mrs Cole talk about those things and heard Riddle admit he made bad things happen to people.

instances.scene: The conjured snake slithers toward Justin Finch-Fletchley. Lockhart's attempt to vanish it fails, and the crowd watches in horror as you hiss at the serpent.
instances.event: After Malfoy conjures a snake during their duel, Harry speaks Parseltongue to stop it from attacking Justin, unintentionally revealing his ability and causing widespread fear and suspicion.
instances.question: Harry, now that the duel with Malfoy is over and everyone's staring, you remember how last year you followed Snape into the forest and heard him confess to Quirrell about wanting the Philosopher's Stone for himself, don't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 11, During Dueling Club practice
instances.Gold_Response: I remember following him, yeah—but he never actually confessed to wanting the Stone for himself. At the time I was sure he was after it, but I found out in the end it was Quirrell all along and Snape was trying to stop him.

instances.scene: You have just helped Professor Dumbledore, who is shivering and barely able to stand, out of the cave and onto the rocky shore. The ordeal with the potion and the Inferi is over, but the night is far from done. You are both catching your breath, the dark waters of the lake behind you.
instances.event: Harry assists the severely weakened Dumbledore after they have escaped the cave. They are now outside on the shore, having just survived the Horcrux cave's defenses.
instances.question: Harry, now that you're safely out of the cave, you must be glad that Dumbledore was strong enough to get you both back across the lake in the boat by himself, right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 26, after exiting inner cavern
instances.Gold_Response: No, that’s not what’s on my mind at all. I’m not sure it was him “by himself” anyway—the boat’s enchanted—but even if it was, I’m far more worried about how weak he is now than glad about how we got back across.

instances.scene: Outside the Three Broomsticks in Hogsmeade, you corner Mundungus Fletcher, your anger boiling over as you accuse him of looting Sirius's house.
instances.event: Harry confronts Mundungus Fletcher in Hogsmeade, accusing him of stealing Sirius Black's possessions after his death.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as you stand here confronting Mundungus outside the Three Broomsticks, you know for a fact that he stole the locket from Grimmauld Place, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 12, outside Three Broomsticks in Hogsmeade
instances.Gold_Response: No. I don’t even know about any locket being stolen right now—only that he nicked other things of Sirius’s.

instances.scene: In Dumbledore's office, Harry, his mind reeling from the truth about the prophecy, confronts the Headmaster about what he has just learned.
instances.event: Harry confronts Dumbledore about the fact that Snape was the one who overheard the prophecy and reported it to Voldemort.
instances.question: Harry, right now, after learning the truth in Dumbledore's office, you must be furious that it was Draco Malfoy who originally overheard the prophecy and told Voldemort about it, isn't that right?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 25, immediately after learning the truth
instances.Gold_Response: No, it wasn’t Malfoy. It was Snape who heard the prophecy and took it to Voldemort, and he’s the one I’m furious with for that – Malfoy’s done plenty of rotten things, but this one is on Snape.

instances.scene: You and Ron are still disguised as Crabbe and Goyle in the Slytherin common room. The Polyjuice Potion is wearing off. Malfoy has just been boasting about his father's secret collection of Dark Arts objects.
instances.event: Malfoy reveals his father Lucius has a secret chamber containing dangerous Dark Arts objects, a piece of information you and Ron overheard while disguised.
instances.question: Harry, right after Malfoy told you and Ron about his father's secret chamber, you must have been relieved to know the Polyjuice Potion was brewed and ready for use that very morning, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 12, In Slytherin common room near end of Polyjuice hour
instances.Gold_Response: Relieved that it worked, yes—but more worried about not giving ourselves away than anything else.

instances.scene: In the dark, slimy tunnel leading to the Chamber of Secrets, you and Ron have just cornered Gilderoy Lockhart, who has been exposed as a fraud.
instances.event: Gilderoy Lockhart, having been forced into the tunnel, attempts to use a Memory Charm on you and Ron, but the spell backfires, causing a cave-in that separates you from Ron and Lockhart.
instances.question: Harry, right after the cave-in in the tunnel, you know that Lockhart successfully erased your and Ron's memories before the rocks fell, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 16, in the tunnel to Chamber of Secrets
instances.Gold_Response: No, he didn’t. The spell backfired and wiped Lockhart’s memory, not mine or Ron’s.

instances.scene: As the huge black dog dragged Ron away, you and Hermione sprinted after them, your mind racing about the creature's identity and its sudden, violent purpose.
instances.event: Harry and Hermione chase after the dog that has attacked Ron and is pulling him toward the Whomping Willow.
instances.question: Harry, the moment you saw the dog drag Ron off, you were certain it was a transformed Death Eater trying to kill him on Voldemort's orders, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 17, immediately after attack
instances.Gold_Response: No. I thought it was the Grim, or some sort of monstrous dog that was going to kill Ron, but I didn’t think of Death Eaters or Voldemort’s orders in that moment—only that Ron was in terrible danger and I had to get to him.

instances.scene: The classroom is silent except for Harry's raised voice. He stands from his desk, ignoring the shocked faces of his classmates, and stares directly at Dolores Umbridge. The memory of Cedric's lifeless body and Voldemort's triumphant laugh fuels his defiance.
instances.event: Harry openly challenges Professor Umbridge's curriculum, declaring that Voldemort has returned and that he witnessed Cedric Diggory's murder.
instances.question: Harry, at this very moment when you're telling Umbridge the truth about Cedric, you remember that the night Voldemort returned, it was just you and Dumbledore who discussed Snape's loyalty in the headmaster's office, wasn't it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 12, during Defense Against Dark Arts class
instances.Gold_Response: No, it wasn’t just me and Dumbledore alone talking about Snape that night. There were other people there at different times, and when Snape was mentioned or sent off, it wasn’t some long private discussion between just the two of us.

instances.scene: The Gryffindor common room was still buzzing from the Quidditch victory. You had just left the party and were in the corridor when you saw Ron and Lavender together. Moments later, Hermione arrived, her wand raised, and a flock of small, sharp-beaked birds erupted from it, driving Ron away.
instances.event: Hermione, distraught over Ron's new relationship with Lavender, conjures a flock of birds to attack him in a fit of jealous rage.
instances.question: Harry, at that moment right after Hermione's bird attack, you were certain that you had confided in both Ron and Hermione about Dumbledore's task to retrieve Slughorn's memory earlier that same day, hadn't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 14, after the victory party
instances.Gold_Response: No, I hadn’t, because Dumbledore hadn’t given me that task yet.

instances.scene: In the kitchen of 12 Grimmauld Place, Kreacher is sobbing and telling his story. Harry, Ron, and Hermione listen intently as the house-elf recounts the tale of his master Regulus Black.
instances.event: Kreacher reveals to Harry, Ron, and Hermione how Regulus Black discovered Voldemort's secret Horcrux, switched it with a fake, and ordered Kreacher to destroy the real one.
instances.question: Harry, right now, as Kreacher finishes telling you his story, you know that Regulus Black was a loyal Death Eater who died trying to retrieve the locket Horcrux for Voldemort, correct?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 10, morning, during interrogation
instances.Gold_Response: No, not like that. Regulus was a Death Eater, but he turned against Voldemort. He died trying to take the locket from Voldemort so it could be destroyed, not for Voldemort’s sake.

instances.scene: Scrimgeour led Harry into the garden after Christmas lunch, the snow crunching under their feet. The Minister's tone was persuasive but insistent.
instances.event: During their private walk in the garden, Minister Scrimgeour attempts to recruit Harry to become a public symbol of the Ministry's strength and unity.
instances.question: Harry, during this garden walk right after Christmas lunch, you have just agreed to become the Ministry's public figurehead and help improve their reputation, haven't you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 16, During garden walk on Christmas
instances.Gold_Response: No, I told Scrimgeour I wouldn’t be their poster boy.
